text: Aristotle (Stagira, Macedonia, 384 BC – Chalicis, Euboea, Greece, 7 March 322 BC) was a Greek philosopher. He was one of the most important philosophers in the history of Western civilization.
title: Aristotle

text: Chanakya (IAST: Cāṇakya; c. 350-283 BCE) was an adviser and Prime minister to Chandragupta Maurya (c. 340-293 BCE). He played a key role in helping Chandragupta in the establishment of Maurya Empire.
title: Chanakya

text: Confucius (born 551 BC, died 479 BC) was an important Chinese educator and philosopher. His original name was Kong Qiu or Zhong Ni.
title: Confucius

text: René Descartes (31 March 1596 – 11 February 1650) was a famous French philosopher and physicist. He wrote books that are very important in the fields of maths, physics and especially philosophy.
title: René Descartes

text: Sigmund Freud (Moravia, 6 May 1856 – London, 23 September 1939) was an Austrian neurologist (a person who treats the nervous system). He invented the treatment of mental illness and neurosis by means of psychoanalysis.
title: Sigmund Freud

text: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel (August 27, 1770 – November 14, 1831) was a German philosopher born in Stuttgart, Württemberg, which is now southwest Germany. He started Hegelianism and is a part of German Idealism.
title: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel

text: Martin Heidegger (26 September 1889 – 26 May 1976) was a German philosopher.
title: Martin Heidegger

text: Immanuel Kant (22 April 1724 – 12 February 1804) was a German philosopher born in Königsberg, East Prussia. Kant studied philosophy at the University of Königsberg, and later became a professor of philosophy.
title: Immanuel Kant

text: John Maynard Keynes, 1st Baron Keynes, CB (5 June 1883 – 21 April 1946) was a British economist. His ideas, called Keynesian economics, had a big impact on modern economic and political theory.
title: John Maynard Keynes

text: Laozi (Lao Tsu, Lao-Tze) was a Chinese philosopher best known for Taoism, the Tao Te Ching, and becoming a deity of Taoism and Chinese folk religions. A legendary figure of Chinese culture, Laozi may have lived during the Warring States period.
title: Laozi

text: John Locke (pronounced /ˈlɒk/; 29 August 1632 – 28 October 1704), known as the Father of Liberalism, was an English philosopher and physician. His writings on the theory of social contract influenced Voltaire and Rousseau, many Scottish Enlightenment thinkers, and the American revolutionaries.
title: John Locke

text: Niccolò Machiavelli (3 May 1469 – 21 June 1527) was a Florentine Renaissance man, statesman, and writer. He was a diplomat and government official in the Medici period of the Florentine Republic.
title: Niccolò Machiavelli

text: Karl Marx (5 May 1818 in Trier, Prussia – 14 March 1883 in London, England) was a German political thinker who wrote about economics and politics. Marx thought that human societies develop through class struggle.
title: Karl Marx

text: Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche was a German philosopher, writer, and scholar of ancient languages. He was born on 15 October 1844 and died on 25 August 1900.
title: Friedrich Nietzsche

text: Plato (c. 427 – 347 BC) was one of the most important philosophers of all time. Born to wealthy parents in Athens, Greece, Plato was a student of Socrates (who did not write) and, later, became the teacher of Aristotle.
title: Plato

text: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, (28 June 1712 – 2 July 1778) was a famous French-speaking philosopher. He was born in Geneva, Switzerland and always described himself as being Genevan.
title: Jean-Jacques Rousseau

text: Jean-Paul Charles Aymard Sartre (21 June 1905 – 15 April 1980) was a French existentialist philosopher, novelist, playwright, screenwriter, and critic. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature for 1964, but refused it, saying "a writer should not allow himself to be turned into an institution".
title: Jean-Paul Sartre

text: Sima Qian (Chinese: 司马迁) was the historian of the Han Dynasty under Emperor Wu. He was born at Xia Yang (present-day Shan Xi Province, Han City) in either 145 or 135 BC.
title: Sima Qian

text: Adam Smith (baptise date 16 June 1723 – 17 July 1790) was a Scottish economist, who is called the Father of Modern Economics. He wrote two classic books, The Theory of Moral Sentiments (1759) and An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations (1776).
title: Adam Smith

text: Socrates (399 BC-470 BC) was one of the most famous Greek philosophers. He showed how argument, debate, and discussion could help people to understand difficult issues.
title: Socrates

text: François-Marie Arouet (also known as Voltaire) was a French philosopher. He was born in 1694 and grew up in Poitou.
title: Voltaire

text: Maximilian Carl Emil Weber (pronounced: maks ˈveːbɐ) (21 April 1864 – 14 June 1920) was a German political economist and sociologist who was considered one of the founders of the modern study of sociology and public administration.
title: Max Weber

text: This is a Chinese name; the family name is Xi.
title: Zhu Xi

text: Abraham (originally Abram) is a man in the Bible's Book of Genesis and the Qur'an. Abraham is said to be the Patriarch (father) of the Jewish People.
title: Abraham

text: St. Thomas Aquinas, (1225 – 7 March 1274) was a Catholic Dominican priest from Italy, saint and philosopher. He was born in Roccasecca, as the son of Count Andulf of Aquino and Countess Theodora of Teano.
title: Thomas Aquinas

text: Siddhartha Gautama (c. 563 BC - c. 483 BC) was an ancient Indian Philosopher and the founder of Buddhism. He is better known by the title the Buddha which means "Fully Awakened One".
title: Gautama Buddha

text: Abū Ḥāmid Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Ghazālī (1058-1111) (Persian: ابو حامد محمد ابن محمد الغزالی), often Algazel in English, was born and died in Tus, in the Khorasan province of Persia.
title: Al-Ghazali

text: Jesus (or Jesus Christ, or Jesus of Nazareth) was a Jewish preacher and reformer of religion and the central figure of Christianity. In Christian tradition, Jesus is believed to be the Jewish Messiah mentioned in the Hebrew Bible.
title: Jesus

text: Martin Luther (November 10, 1483 ‒ February 18, 1546) was a German monk and theologian of Christianity credited with leading the Protestant Reformation, a movement that marked the start of Protestantism. Luther founded the Lutheran Church, the first large Protestant church.
title: Martin Luther

text: Moses (Mōše; Ancient Greek: Mωϋσῆς in both the Septuagint and the New Testament; Arabic: موسىٰ, Mūsa) is a person in Abrahamic religions. He was a religious leader, lawgiver, and prophet according to the Hebrew Bible.
title: Moses

text: Muhammad (Arabic: مُحَمَّدٌ; 570 – 8 June 632) was an Arab religious, social, and political leader, best known as the founder of Islam. Islamic teachings say Muhammad was a prophet who God inspired to preach and confirm the monotheistic teachings of Adam, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets.
title: Muhammad

text: Nagarjuna was an Indian Buddhist monk and philosopher in the Mahayana tradition and the founder of the Madhyamaka school of Buddhist Philosophy. He is highly regarded as one of the most important Buddhist Philosophers.
title: Nagarjuna

text: Akbar (Abu'l-Fath Jalal ud-din Muhammad Akbar, 15 October 1542 – 27 October 1605), also known as Akbar the Great was the 3rd Mughal Emperor. He was the son of 2nd Mughal Emperor Humayun.
title: Akbar

text: Alexander the Great was Alexander III of Macedonia 20/21 July 356 BC – 10/11 June 323 BC). He was king of the ancient kingdom of Macedonia from 336 BC until his death in 323 BC.
title: Alexander the Great

text: Ashoka was the greatest emperor of the Mauryan Empire. He ruled from 268–232 BC.
title: Ashoka

text: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk (1881 – 10 November 1938) was a Turkish marshal and statesman who was the first President of Turkey from 1923 to his death in 1938.
title: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk

text: Augustus (Latin: Imperator Caesar Dīvī Fīlius Augustus; 23 September 63 BC – 19 August 14 AD) was the first Roman Emperor, ruling from 27 BC until his death in AD 14. He led Rome in its transition from the Roman Republic to the Roman Empire.
title: Augustus

text: Prince Otto Eduard Leopold von Bismarck-Schönhausen Duke of Lauenburg, (1 April 1815 – 30 July 1898), was an aristocrat and statesman of the 19th century in Europe.
title: Otto von Bismarck

text: Simón Bolívar (1783 - 1830) was a Venezuelan military and political leader. He was born in Caracas, Venezuela.
title: Simón Bolívar

text: Gaius Julius Caesar (12 July 100 BC – 15 March 44 BC) was a military commander, politician and author at the end of the Roman Republic.
title: Julius Caesar

text: Charlemagne ( SHAR-lə-mayn; Latin: Carolus Magnus, French: Charlemagnes, English: Charles the Great, German: Karl der Große, Dutch: Karel de Grote) (c. 2 April 748 – 28 January 814) was the King of the Franks and the first Holy Roman Emperor. He was crowned as emperor on Christmas Day in 800.
title: Charlemagne

text: Sir Winston Leonard Spencer-Churchill KG OM CH TD FRS PC (30 November 1874 – 24 January 1965) was an English politician. He was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom twice, once during World War II, and again in the early 1950s.
title: Winston Churchill

text: Constantine I (27 February 272 – 22 May 337 AD) was a Roman emperor from 306 until he died. He was emperor for longer than any other emperor since Augustus, the first emperor.
title: Constantine the Great

text: Cyrus the Great (Persian: کوروش بزرگ, Kurush-e Bozorg, c. 590 BC or 576 – August 530 BC), was the founder of the Achaemenid dynasty in today's Iran. He was chosen as the leader of Persian people in Anshan, he defeated the Medes and was chosen as the Shah of the Persian Empire in 559 BC.
title: Cyrus the Great

text: General Charles André Joseph Marie de Gaulle (22 November 1890 - 9 November 1970) was a French military and political leader. He was president of France from 1959 to 1969.
title: Charles de Gaulle

text: Elizabeth I (7 September, 1533 – 24 March, 1603) was the Queen of England and Ireland from 17 November 1558 to her death. She was also called Good Queen Bess or the Virgin Queen or the Gloriana.
title: Elizabeth I

text: Mohandas Karmchand Gandhi (2 October 1869– 30 January 1948) was a leader of nationalism in British-ruled India. He is more commonly called Mahatma Gandhi. mahatma is an honorific meaning "great-soul" or "venerable" in Sanskrit.
title: Mahatma Gandhi

text: Genghis Khan (born Temüjin; c. 1162 – August 1227), also known as Chinggis Khan, was the first ruler of the Mongol Empire, which he created in 1206 in his fatherland in what is now Mongolia.
title: Genghis Khan

text: Ernesto "Che" Guevara, commonly known as el Che or Che (June 14, 1928 - October 9, 1967) was an Argentine Marxist, revolutionary, physician, author, guerrilla, diplomat, and military theorist. He is popular with socialists.
title: Che Guevara

text: Saint Joan of Arc or The Maid of Orléans (Jeanne d'Arc, c. 6 January 1412 – 30 May 1431) was a national heroine of France. She is also a Catholic saint.
title: Joan of Arc

text: Martin Luther King, Jr. (born Michael King, Jr.; January 15, 1929 – April 4, 1968) was an American pastor, activist, humanitarian, and leader in the Civil Rights Movement. He was best known for improving civil rights by using nonviolent civil disobedience, based on his Christian beliefs.
title: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: Vladimir Ilyich Ulyanov (22 April 1870 – 21 January 1924), better known as Vladimir Lenin, was a Russian revolutionary, politician, and political theorist. He was the first leader of the Soviet Union, starting when the country was created in 1922.
title: Vladimir Lenin

text: Abraham Lincoln ( LINK-ən; February 12, 1809 – April 15, 1865) was an American politician who served as the 16th president of the United States from 1861 until his assassination in 1865.
title: Abraham Lincoln

text: Louis XIV (5 September 1638 — 1 September 1715), also popularly known as the Sun King and Louis the Great, was the King of France, King of Navarre and Prince of Andorra from 14 May 1643 until his death in 1715. He is the longest-reigning monarch in history, reigning for 72 years and 110 days.
title: Louis XIV

text: Rosa Luxemburg (5 March 1871 in Zamość, Russian Poland – 15 January 1919 in Berlin) was a Polish-Jewish Marxist politician working in both Poland and Germany. Her birth name was Rosalia Luxemburg.
title: Rosa Luxemburg

text: Napoleon Bonaparte (French: Napoléon Bonaparte) was a French politician and army leader who ruled France from 1799 to 1814 and for a short period (the "Hundred Days") in 1815.
title: Napoleon

text: Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela (18 July 1918 – 5 December 2013) was a South African politician and civil rights activist. On 27 April 1994, he became the first President of South Africa, elected in a fully represented democratic election.
title: Nelson Mandela

text: Mao Zedong (26 December 1893 – 9 September 1976) was a Chinese Communist politician and revolutionary. He was also called Chairman Mao, because he was the first Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) from 1943 until his death in 1976.
title: Mao Zedong

text: Jawaharlal Nehru (also referred to as Pandit Nehru) (November 14, 1889 - May 27, 1964) was the first prime minister of India for 17 years. He became prime minister after India became independent in 1947.
title: Jawaharlal Nehru

text: Dr. Kwame Nkrumah (born Francis Nwia-Kofi Ngonloma, September 21, 1909 – April 27, 1972) was an African political leader. He was the first Prime Minister, then President, of Ghana.
title: Kwame Nkrumah

text: Qin Shi Huang (Chinese: 秦始皇; literally: "First Emperor of Qin"; 18 February 259 B.C. – 10 September 210 B.C.) was the founder of the Qin dynasty and was the first emperor of a unified China.
title: Qin Shi Huang

text: Franklin Delano Roosevelt (January 30, 1882 – April 12, 1945) was the 32nd president of the United States from 1933 to his death. He died shortly after he he had begun his fourth term.
title: Franklin D. Roosevelt

text: Salah ad-Din Yusuf ibn Ayyub (Arabic: صلاح الدين يوسف ابن أيوب, romanized: Salah ad-Dīn Yūsuf ibn Ayyūb; 25 December 1138–1193), better known as Saladin, was a famous Kurdish Muslim Sultan of Egypt and Syria during the Crusades.
title: Saladin

text: Joseph Vissarionovich Stalin (born Ioseb Besarionis dze Jughashvili); (18 December 1878 – 5 March 1953) was a communist revolutionary and politician who led the Soviet Union from 1924 to his death.
title: Joseph Stalin

text: Suleiman I, commonly known as Suleiman the Magnificent in Western Europe and Suleiman the Lawgiver (Ottoman Turkish: قانونى سلطان سليمان, romanized: Ḳānūnī Sulṭān Süleymān) in his Ottoman realm, was the tenth Sultan of the Ottoman Empire. He became sultan when he was 26 years old.
title: Suleiman the Magnificent

text: Sun Wen, Sun Zhongshan or Sun Yat-sen (12 November 1866 – 12 March 1925) was born in China and was a Chinese political leader. On his 8th attempt while living in Maui Sun helped overthrow the Qing Dynasty in October 1911 during the Xinhai Revolution.
title: Sun Yat-sen

text: Timur (Emir Timur), Tamerlane or Tamerbeg (9 April 1336 – 17 February 1405) was a Central Asian conqueror of Mongolian origin in the 14th century who is regarded as one of history's greatest military leaders and strategists. He founded the Timurid Empire in 1370.
title: Tamerlane

text: Umar ibn al-Khattab (Arabic: عُمَر بْن ٱلْخَطَّاب, romanized: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb; c. 582/583 – 644), also spelled Omar, was the second Rashidun caliph, ruling from August 634, when he succeeded Abu Bakr (r. 632–634) as the second caliph, until his assassination in 644.
title: Umar

text: George Washington (February 22, 1732 – December 14, 1799) was the first president of the United States from 1789 to 1796. Before he became president, he had been the commander-in-chief of the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War and one of the Founding Fathers of the United States.
title: George Washington

text: Archimedes of Syracuse (c. 287 – c. 212 BC) was a Greek scientist. He was an inventor, an astronomer, and a mathematician.
title: Archimedes

text: Ibn Sina (Persian/Tajik: ابن سینا; 980 – June 1037 CE), commonly known in the West as Avicenna, was a Persian polymath and the most important doctor and Islamic philosopher of his time.
title: Avicenna

text: Sir Timothy John Berners-Lee (born 8 June 1955) is a British computer scientist who was the inventor of the World Wide Web and he created a new computer language called HTML (Hypertext Markup Language) which most web pages are written in. The first web page was available on 6 August 1991.
title: Tim Berners-Lee

text: Nicolaus Copernicus (19 February 1473 – 24 May 1543) was a Polish astronomer. People know Copernicus for his ideas about the sun and the earth.
title: Nicolaus Copernicus

text: Marie Salomée Skłodowska, Madame Pierre Curie (born Maria Salomea Skłodowska; 7 November 1867 – 4 July 1934) was a Polish-born French physicist and chemist. She did research on radioactivity.
title: Marie Curie

text: Charles Robert Darwin (12 February 1809 – 19 April 1882) was an English naturalist. He is famous for his work on the theory of evolution.
title: Charles Darwin

text: Thomas Alva Edison (ED-e-son)(February 11, 1847 – October 18, 1931) was an American inventor, entrepreneur and businessman. He developed many devices in the fields such as electricity generation, mass communication, sound recording and reproduction, and motion pictures .
title: Thomas Edison

text: Albert Einstein (14 March 1879 – 18 April 1955) was a German-born Jewish scientist. He worked on theoretical physics.
title: Albert Einstein

text: Euclid of Alexandria (Greek: Εὐκλείδης) (about 325 BC–265 BC) was a Greek mathematician who lived in Alexandria, Egypt and worked at the Library of Alexandria. Little is known about this person, but people think he lived there when Ptolemy I was Pharaoh.
title: Euclid

text: Leonhard Euler (pronounced Leonard Oiler) (April 15, 1707 – September 7, 1783) was a Swiss mathematician and physicist. He spent most of his adult life in Russia and Germany.
title: Leonhard Euler

text: Michael Faraday (Newington Butts, Surrey. 22 September 1791 – Hampton Court, Surrey, 25 August 1867) was the son of a blacksmith who became one of the most famous scientists of the 19th century.
title: Michael Faraday

text: Enrico Fernando Fermi (September 29, 1901 — November 28, 1954) was an Italian-American physicist who worked on the first nuclear reactor and helped make quantum theory. He also was important to particle physics, and statistical mechanics.
title: Enrico Fermi

text: Henry Ford (30 July 1863 – 7 April 1947) was an American engineer and businessman. He started making cars in 1896 and founded the Ford Motor Company.
title: Henry Ford

text: Galen of Pergamum (129–199/217 AD) was a prominent Greek physician and philosopher from Pergamon, a Greek city in western Asia Minor. He was an important medical researcher in the Roman Empire and his theories influenced Western medical science for over a thousand years.
title: Galen

text: Galileo Galilei (15 February 1564 – 8 January 1642) was an Italian polymath. Galileo was originally going to be a doctor but became a tutor instead.
title: Galileo Galilei

text: Johannes Gensfleisch zur Laden zum Gutenberg (more commonly known as Johannes Gutenberg) (1390s – 3 February 1468), was a German metal-worker and inventor. He is famous for his work in printing in the 1450s, and is specifically known for inventing typography.
title: Johannes Gutenberg

text: David Hilbert (Königsberg, Prussia, 23 January 1862 –Göttingen, Germany, 14 February 1943) was a German mathematician, logician, and philosopher of mathematics. He is widely considered to be one of the most influential and greatest mathematicians of the 19th and 20th centuries.
title: David Hilbert

text: James Prescott Joule (24 December 1818 – 11 October 1889) was an English physicist, born in Salford, near Manchester. In his time he had great contribution to the world of electricity and thermodynamics.
title: James Prescott Joule

text: Johannes Kepler (27 December 1571 – 15 November 1630) was a German mathematics teacher, astronomer, optician, natural philosopher, astrologer and Lutheran theologian.
title: Johannes Kepler

text: Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī (Persian: محمد بن موسى خوارزمی, Arabic: محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي) was a Persian mathematician and astronomer. He was believed to have been born around 800 AD and died in 850 AD during the Abbasid Empire.
title: Al-Khwarizmi

text: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (also Leibnitz or von Leibniz) 1 July 1 (21 June OS) 1646 – 14 November 1716) was a German intellectual who wrote mostly in French and Latin.
title: Gottfried Leibniz

text: Carl Linnaeus (23 May 1707 – 10 January 1778), also known as Carolus Linnaeus, was a Swedish botanist, physician and zoologist who created the binomial nomenclature. In this system, every kind of animal and plant is given a name consisting of two Latin words, for its genus and species.
title: Carl Linnaeus

text: James Clerk Maxwell FRSE (born 13 June 1831 in Edinburgh – died 5 November 1879) was a British mathematician, physicist and discoverer of Maxwell's equations.
title: James Clerk Maxwell

text: Dmitri Ivanovich Mendeleev (born 8 February (O.S. 27 January) 1834 near Tobolsk – 2 February (O.S. 20 January 20) 1907 in Saint Petersburg) was a Russian chemist who created the periodic table of elements.
title: Dmitri Mendeleev

text: Sir Isaac Newton (25 December 1643 – 31 March 1727) was an English physicist, mathematician and astronomer. He is well known for his work on the laws of motion, optics, gravity, and calculus also, he presents his theory of universal gravitation and three laws of motion.
title: Isaac Newton

text: Louis Pasteur (December 27, 1822 – September 28, 1895) was a French microbiologist and chemist.
title: Louis Pasteur

text: Max Karl Ernst Ludwig Planck (April 23, 1858 in Kiel – October 4, 1947 in Göttingen) was a physicist from Germany. He discovered quantum mechanics.
title: Max Planck

text: Ernest Rutherford, 1st Baron Rutherford of Nelson OM PC FRS (30 August 1871 – 19 October 1937) was a New Zealand-born British scientist. He won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1908 for his work on nuclear physics, and for his theory of the structure of the atom.
title: Ernest Rutherford

text: Erwin Schrödinger (Erwin Rudolf Josef Alexander Schrödinger, 12 August 1887, Vienna-Erdberg – 4 January 1961, Vienna) was an Austrian physicist and theoretical physicist and biologist. He was one of the founding fathers of quantum theory and won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1933.
title: Erwin Schrödinger

text: Nikola Tesla (Smiljan, July 10, 1856 - New York, January 7, 1943) was an American inventor and engineer of Serbian origin. He is best known for his contributions to the design of the modern alternating current (AC) electricity supply system.
title: Nikola Tesla

text: Alan Mathison Turing (London, 23 June 1912 – Wilmslow, Cheshire, 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician and computer scientist. He is known as the father of computer science.
title: Alan Turing

text: James Watt (19 January 1736 – 25 August 1819) was a Scottish mathematician and engineer. He did not invent the first steam engine, but he did modify it to work better.
title: James Watt

text: Charles-Edouard Jeanneret-Gris (birth name), (6 October 1887 – 27 August 1965), known by the popular name of Le Corbusier, was an architect and writer born in Switzerland. In the 1930s, he became a French citizen.
title: Le Corbusier

text: Albrecht Dürer (21 May 1471 – 6 April 1528) was a Hungarian-German painter, engraver and mathematician.
title: Albrecht Dürer

text: Vincent Willem van Gogh (30 March 1853 – 29 July 1890) was a Dutch post-impressionist painter. His work had a great influence on modern art because of its striking colours and emotional power.
title: Vincent van Gogh

text: Francisco José de Goya y Lucientes (30 March 1746 – 30 April 1828) was a Spanish painter. He painted many portraits of the Spanish Royal Family.
title: Francisco de Goya

text: Katsushika Hokusai (葛飾北斎, Katsushika Hokusai; October 31, 1760 – May 10, 1849), also called Hokusai, was a Japanese artist. He was a master of the ukiyo-e style of woodblock prints and painting.
title: Katsushika Hokusai

text: Magdalena Carmen Frida Kahlo y Calderón (6 July 1907 – 13 July 1954), Mexican Painter usually known as Frida Kahlo. She was known for her surreal and very personal works.
title: Frida Kahlo

text: Leonardo Da Vinci (15 April 1452 – 2 May 1519) was an Italian polymath who lived during the Renaissance. He is famous for his paintings.
title: Leonardo da Vinci

text: Henri Matisse (Le Cateau-Cambrésis, Nord, 31 December 1869 – 3 November 1954) was a French artist known for his use of color and his original ideas.
title: Henri Matisse

text: Michelangelo di Lodovico Buonarroti Simoni (6 March 1475 – 18 February 1564), known as Michelangelo, was an Italian Renaissance painter, sculptor, architect, poet, and engineer. Along with Leonardo da Vinci, he is often called a "Renaissance Man" which means that he had great talent in many areas.
title: Michelangelo

text: Pablo Picasso (full name: Pablo Diego José Francisco de Paula Juan Nepomuceno María de los Remedios Cipriano de la Santísima Trinidad Ruiz y Picasso, October 25, 1881 – April 8, 1973) was a Spanish painter and sculptor. He created over 20,000 works of art.
title: Pablo Picasso

text: Raffaello Sanzio, usually known as Raphael (April 6, 1483 - April 6, 1520) was a Renaissance painter and architect. With Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo, he is one of the three greatest painters of the High Renaissance.
title: Raphael

text: Rembrandt Harmenszoon van Rijn (Leiden, 15 July 1606 – Amsterdam, 4 October 1669) was a famous Dutch painter and artist.
title: Rembrandt

text: Pieter Pauwel (Peter Paul) Rubens (28 June 1577 – 30 May 1640) was a painter.
title: Peter Paul Rubens

text: Mimar Sinan or Koca Mi'mâr Sinân Âğâ (Ottoman Turkish: خواجه معمار سنان آغا‎; Modern Turkish: Mimar Sinan) (15 April 1489 – 9 April 1588) was an Ottoman architect and civil engineer. He worked for sultans Suleiman the Magnificent, Selim II, and Murad III.
title: Mimar Sinan

text: Diego Velázquez (baptized 6 June 1599 – 6 August 1660) was a Spanish painter, the leading artist in the court of King Philip IV.
title: Diego Velázquez

text: Andy Warhol (Andrew Warhol, Jr.; August 6, 1928 – February 22, 1987) was one of the most famous American artists of the latter half of the 20th century. Many people think that Warhol is the "bellwether of the art market".
title: Andy Warhol

text: Frank Lloyd Wright (born Frank Lincoln Wright; June 8, 1867 – April 9, 1959) was a famous American architect from the early 20th century. He designed all kinds of buildings including banks, holiday resorts, office buildings, churches, a synagogue, a gas station, a beer garden and an art museum.
title: Frank Lloyd Wright

text: Louis Armstrong (August 4, 1901 – July 6, 1971), nicknamed Satchmo or Pops, was an American jazz trumpeter and singer from New Orleans, Louisiana. He sang the blues and played the trumpet and the cornet.
title: Louis Armstrong

text: Johann Sebastian Bach (31 March 1685 in Eisenach – 28 July 1750 in Leipzig; pronounced BAHK) was a German composer, who was more known as an organist in his time. He lived in the last part of the Baroque period.
title: Johann Sebastian Bach

text: The Beatles were an English pop/rock band, started in Liverpool, England in 1960. The members were John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr.
title: The Beatles

text: Ludwig van Beethoven (baptized 17 December 1770 in Bonn – 26 March 1827 in Vienna; pronounced LUD-vig vahn BAY-TOH-ven) was a German composer. He wrote classical music for the piano, orchestras and different groups of instruments.
title: Ludwig van Beethoven

text: Johannes Brahms (7 May 1833 – 3 April 1897) was a famous German composer. He started his career as a pianist.
title: Johannes Brahms

text: Fryderyk Franciszek Chopin (1 March 1810 – 17 October 1849; pronounced SHOH-pen) was a Polish composer and virtuoso pianist. He is considered one of the greatest Romantic piano composers.
title: Frédéric Chopin

text: Antonín Leopold Dvořák (8 September 1841 – 1 May 1904) was a Czech composer. Along with Smetana and Janáček, Dvorak is one of three famous composers who wrote nationalist Czech music.
title: Antonín Dvořák

text: George Frideric Handel (German: Georg Friedrich Händel) (23 February 1685 – 14 April 1759) was an German composer who went to live in England when he was a young man and later became a naturalised Briton. Johann Sebastian Bach and Handel were born in the same year.
title: George Frideric Handel

text: Franz Joseph Haydn (31 March 1732 – 31 May 1809) was an Austrian composer. He was one of the most famous composers in the Classical music period.
title: Joseph Haydn

text: Michael Joseph Jackson (August 29, 1958 – June 25, 2009), also known by his initials MJ, was an American singer, songwriter, dancer, and philanthropist. Known as the "King of Pop", he is often regarded as one of the most culturally significant figures of the 20th century.
title: Michael Jackson

text: Umm-kulthoum Ibrahim es-Sayyid el-Beltagi (31 December 1898 – 3 February 1975) was an Egyptian singer, songwriter and actress in the Arab world of the 20th century. She is seen as a national icon of Egypt.
title: Umm Kulthum

text: Gustav Mahler (born Kalischt (now Kalište), Bohemia, July 7 1860; died Vienna, May 18 1911) was a Czech-Austrian composer and conductor. He was one of the last great composers of the Romantic period.
title: Gustav Mahler

text: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (January 27, 1756 – December 5, 1791; pronounced MOHT-sart) was a composer, instrumentalist, and music teacher. His full baptised name was Johannes Chrysostomus Wolfgangus Theophilus Mozart.
title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart

text: Giovanni da Palestrina (born Palestrina, (c.1525 – February 2, 1594 in Rome) was a very important Italian composer of church music of his time. He lived in the period called the Renaissance.
title: Giovanni da Palestrina

text: Giacomo Puccini (23 December 1858 - 29 November 1924) was the most famous Italian opera composer after Verdi. He wrote 16 operas.
title: Giacomo Puccini

text: Franz Peter Schubert (31 January 1797, Vienna – 19 November 1828, Vienna) was an Austrian composer. Although he died at the age of 31, he composed over one thousand pieces of music.
title: Franz Schubert

text: Igor Stravinsky was born in Lomonosov (then Oranienbaum), 17 June 1882 and died in New York, 6 April 1971. He was one of the most important composers of the 20th century, and a leader in modernism in music.
title: Igor Stravinsky

text: Giuseppe Verdi (born Roncole near Busseto, 9 or 10 October 1813; died Milan 27 January 1901) was an Italian composer of operas.
title: Giuseppe Verdi

text: Antonio Vivaldi (born Venice, 4 March 1678; died Vienna, 28 July 1741) was an Italian composer. He was the most important composer in Italy at the end of the Baroque period.
title: Antonio Vivaldi

text: Richard Wagner (22 May 1813 in Leipzig – 13 February 1883 in Venice) was a German opera composer. He was one of the most important opera composers in Germany during the Romantic period.
title: Richard Wagner

text: Sir Charles Spencer "Charlie" Chaplin (16 April 1889 – 25 December 1977) was an English comic actor, filmmaker, and composer. He was famous in silent movies (where there was no talking or sound).
title: Charlie Chaplin

text: Sergei Mikhailovich Eisenstein (Russian: Сергей Михайлович Эйзенштейн; Sergej Mihajlovič Ejzenštejn; January 23, 1898 – February 11, 1948) was a Soviet Russian movie director and movie theorist. He was known mostly for his silent movies Strike, The Battleship Potemkin and October.
title: Sergei Eisenstein

text: Federico Fellini (born 20 January 1920 in Rimini, died 31 October 1993 in Rome) was an Italian movie-maker and director. Fellini's movies combine memory, dream, and fantasy.
title: Federico Fellini

text: Sir Alfred Joseph Hitchcock (13 August 1899 – 29 April 1980) was a British movie director who later became an American citizen, but still kept his British citizenship. He mostly made mystery and suspense movies.
title: Alfred Hitchcock

text: Stanley Kubrick (26 July 1928 - 7 March 1999) was an American movie director. Kubrick is thought to have been one of the great directors of the 20th century.
title: Stanley Kubrick

text: Akira Kurosawa (March 23, 1910 – September 6, 1998) was a Japanese movie director. Kurosawa's movies are liked in Japan.
title: Akira Kurosawa

text: Abū Nuwās al-Ḥasan ibn Hānī al-Ḥakamī (variant: Al-Ḥasan ibn Hānī 'Abd al-Awal al-Ṣabāḥ, Abū 'Alī (الحسن بن هانئ بن عبد الأول بن الصباح ،ِابو علي), known as Abū Nuwās al-Salamī (أبو نواس السلمي) or just Abū Nuwās (أبو نواس Abū Novās); c. 756 – c. 814) was a classical Arabic poet. He was born in Persia.
title: Abu Nuwas

text: Hans Christian Andersen (2 April 1805 – 4 August 1875) was a Danish writer.
title: Hans Christian Andersen

text: Jane Austen (16 December 1775 – 18 July 1817) was an English novelist. She wrote many books of romantic fiction about the gentry.
title: Jane Austen

text: Matsuo Munefusa, known as Matsuo Bashō (Japanese: 松尾芭蕉, 1644 - November 28, 1694) was a Japanese poet. He is known as the greatest maker of haiku, a kind of poetry with 17 syllables.
title: Matsuo Basho

text: Jorge Luis Borges (August 24, 1899 – June 14, 1986) was an Argentine writer. He was best known in the English-speaking world for his short stories and fictive essays.
title: Jorge Luis Borges

text: George Gordon Byron, 6th Baron Byron (22 January 1788 – 19 April 1824) was an English peer, nobleman, politician, and poet. He was christened George Gordon Byron, but changed his name later in life.
title: Lord Byron

text: Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra (29 September 1547 – 23 April 1616) was a Spanish writer. His most famous book was Don Quijote de la Mancha.
title: Miguel de Cervantes

text: Geoffrey Chaucer (c. 1343–25 October 1400) was an English writer, poet, and philosopher. He is most famous for writing Canterbury Tales, his estate satire about a group of pilgrims traveling from London to Canterbury and telling tales to pass the time.
title: Geoffrey Chaucer

text: Anton Pavlovich Chekhov (January 29, 1860 - July 15, 1904) was a Russian writer who wrote short stories and plays.
title: Anton Chekhov

text: Charles Dickens (7 February 1812 – 9 June 1870) was an English writer and a social critic who is regarded as one of the great English writers of the 19th century.
title: Charles Dickens

text: Fyodor Mikhailovich Dostoyevsky (11 November 1821 – 9 February 1881) was a Russian novelist. His most popular novels are Crime and Punishment, The Idiot and The Brothers Karamazov.
title: Fyodor Dostoyevsky

text: Gabriel José de la Concordia García Márquez, also known as Gabo (March 6, 1927 – April 17, 2014) was a Colombian novelist, short-story writer, screenwriter, and journalist. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982.
title: Gabriel García Márquez

text: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (August 28, 1749 – March 22, 1832) was a German writer, poet, novelist, and playwright. He also worked as an actor, administrator, scientist, geologist, botanist, and philosopher.
title: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

text: Khwajeh Shams al-Din Muhammad Hafez-e Shirazi (also spelled Hafiz) (born between 1310 and 1337, believed to have died at age 69) (Persian: خواجه شمس الدین محمد حافظ شیرازی) or Hafez is a Persian poet. Hafez was born in Shiraz, Iran.
title: Hafez

text: Homer is the name of the Greek poet who wrote the epic poems the Iliad and the Odyssey. These are the earliest works of Greek literature which have survived to the present day, and are among the greatest treasures of the ancient world.
title: Homer

text: Victor Marie Hugo (26 February 1802 – 22 May 1885) was a French poet, playwright, novelist, statesman and human rights activist. He played an important part in the Romantic movement in France.
title: Victor Hugo

text: James Augustine Aloysius Joyce (Irish: Séamus Seoighe) (2 February 1882 – 13 January 1941) was an Irish writer and poet of the modernist movement. He was from Dublin, Ireland.
title: James Joyce

text: Franz Kafka (born Prague July 3, 1883 – died near Vienna June 3, 1924) was a Czech-born, German-speaking writer. His best known works are The Metamorphosis and the novels The Trial and The Castle.
title: Franz Kafka

text: Kālidās (Devanāgarī: कालिदास) was an Indian Sanskrit playwright and the author of Meghadoot, Shākuntal and other Sanskrit works. He has a similar place in Sanskrit as a poet and a dramatist, as Shakespeare in English.
title: Kalidasa

text: Li Bai (also Li Bo or Li Po, Chinese: 李白; pinyin: Lǐ Bái / Lǐ Bó; 701–762) was a Chinese poet. His fellow poet Du Fu counted him to the group of Chinese scholars that he called the "Eight Immortals of the Wine Cup" in a poem.
title: Li Bai

text: Molière (1622 – 17 February 1673) was a French actor, director and writer. His real name was Jean-Baptiste Poquelin, Molière was his stage name.
title: Molière

text: Publius Ovidius Naso. better known as Ovid in the English-speaking world, was an Ancient Roman poet. He was born on March 20, 43 BC in Sulmona, then called Sulmo.
title: Publius Ovidius Naso

text: Marcel Valentin Louis Eugène Georges Proust (10 July 1871 – 18 November 1922) was a French writer. People say his name like "mar-SEL proost".
title: Marcel Proust

text: Alexander Sergeyevich Pushkin was born 6 June (26 May, Old Style) 1799, Moscow, and died 10 February 1837 (29 January, New Style), St Petersburg. He was a Russian poet, novelist, dramatist and writer of short stories.
title: Alexander Pushkin

text: William Shakespeare (c. 23 April 1564 – 23 April 1616) was an English dramatist, poet and theatre actor. He wrote 40 known plays (with about half of them considered comedies) and two long poems in his lifetime.
title: William Shakespeare

text: Sophocles (497 BC, 496 BC, or 495 BC – 406 BC) was an Ancient Greek writer who wrote over 100 plays, according to the Suda. Only seven of his tragedies have survived complete.
title: Sophocles

text: Count Lev Nikolayevich Tolstoy (9 September 1828 – 20 November 1910) was a Russian novelist and anarchist, famous for writing the books War and Peace and Anna Karenina, and many other works. He was a Christian and believed in non-violence and practiced simple living.
title: Leo Tolstoy

text: Samuel Langhorne Clemens (November 30, 1835 – April 21, 1910), more widely known as Mark Twain, was an American writer. He was born in Florida, Missouri.
title: Mark Twain

text: Roald Amundsen was a Norwegian explorer who focused on the poles. He led the first expedition to reach the South Pole and the first that could prove it made it to the North Pole.
title: Roald Amundsen

text: Neil Alden Armstrong (August 5, 1930 – August 25, 2012) was an American astronaut, and engineer, and is known as the first person to walk on the moon. On July 20, 1969, Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed on the moon in a small spacecraft that had been sent to the moon using the Saturn V rocket.
title: Neil Armstrong

text: Jacques Cartier was a French trader and explorer. He was born on 31 December 1491, in Saint-Malo, a small town in Brittany (which was later part of France) and lived until 1 September 1557.
title: Jacques Cartier

text: Christopher Columbus (1451–1506) was an Italian trader, explorer, and navigator. The consensus view is that he was born in Genoa in the year 1451, the son of a weaver named Domenico Colombo and a seamstress named Susanna Fontanarossa.
title: Christopher Columbus

text: Captain James Cook, FRS (27 October 1728 (O.S.) – 14 February 1779) was a British explorer, navigator and cartographer. He sailed through the Pacific Ocean three times, mapped many areas and recorded several islands and coastlines on European maps for the first time.
title: James Cook

text: Hernán Cortés (1485 - 2 December 1547) was an explorer and Conquistador from Spain. Between 1519 and 1521, he conquered the Aztec Empire of emperor Montezuma II where Mexico is today.
title: Hernán Cortés

text: Yuri Alexeyevich Gagarin (Russian: Юрий Алексеевич Гагарин; March 9, 1934 – March 27, 1968) was a Soviet and Russian cosmonaut (astronaut). He was the first person to travel into space.
title: Yuri Gagarin

text: Vasco da Gama (c. 1462 – December 24, 1506) was a Portuguese sailor. He was the first European who went to India through the Cape of Good Hope at the southern end of Africa.
title: Vasco da Gama

text: Ibn Battuta (1304 – 1368 or 1369) was a Moroccan explorer. He is known for the account of his journeys called the Rihla ("Voyage").
title: Ibn Battuta

text: Ferdinand Magellan (1480 – 27 April 1521) was a Portuguese explorer. He became the first European to sail the Pacific Ocean, and the first to sail around the world.
title: Ferdinand Magellan

text: Marco Polo was born in 1254 and died on January 8, 1324. He was an Italian trader and explorer.
title: Marco Polo

text: This is a Chinese name; the family name is Zheng.
title: Zheng He

text: Atheism is the idea that rejects the belief in a God or gods.
title: Atheism

text: Beauty is a property of certain things. Something is beautiful if it is nice to look at it, hear it, feel it, taste it, smell it or think about it.
title: Beauty

text: Confucianism is the philosophy based on the teachings of Confucius (551 BC - 479 BC), who was an important Chinese philosopher. Confucianism is a system of moral, social, political, and religious thought, and has had a large influence on the history of Chinese civilization.
title: Confucianism

text: In philosophy, dialectic is a debate or an argument between different individuals. In medieval Europe, dialectics (or logic) was one of the three beginning liberal arts known as the trivium altogether, while the others were grammar and rhetoric.
title: Dialectic

text: Ethics is the study of good and bad behavior. It is one of the main parts of philosophy.
title: Ethics

text: Free will is being able to choose between different actions. If we judge an action (for example, as good or bad) it only makes sense if the action is freely chosen.
title: Free will

text: Knowledge is the collection of facts, skills, and understanding that people gain through learning, experience, thinking, or discovery. It can come from things we are taught, things we figure out ourselves, or things we observe in the world.
title: Knowledge

text: Logic is the study of reasoning. The rules of logic let philosophers make logical deductions about the world.
title: Logic

text: Materialism is the philosophical belief that the world is made of material, and that there are no other types of entity (things). Everything is composed of material.
title: Materialism

text: Philosophy is the study of wisdom. Philosophia is the Ancient Greek word for the "love of wisdom".
title: Philosophy

text: Reality means anything that exists. An event that has actually happened, or a thing which really exists is said to have "reality." Something close to reality is realistic.
title: Reality

text: The truth is what is true. It may be everything that is true (reality) or just a part of it (a fact).
title: Truth

text: Fundamentalism was used at first to describe some people in the Protestant community in the United States in the early 20th century. These people had a set of well-defined ("fundamental") values.
title: Fundamentalism

text: God is a being or spirit worshipped as a deity. God is considered to be the creator of the universe in some religions.
title: God

text: Monotheism is the belief in only one god, rather than the two (dualism) or more (polytheism) as in Ancient Greece, Ancient Rome, Ancient India and Ancient Egypt.
title: Monotheism

text: Polytheism means believing in many gods. A person that believes in polytheism is called a polytheist.
title: Polytheism

text: A myth is a story about the remote past which is considered true within the society in which it is told. Creation myths take place long ago, during the first existing period of time: the primordial age.
title: Mythology

text: Reincarnation is the name of the idea that people are born again in another body after they die and this cycle continues over many lifetimes. Rebirth or "transmigration" is the preferred term for those believers who do not believe in eternal souls.
title: Reincarnation

text: Religion is a set of beliefs and social-cultural systems, including certain practices, morals, beliefs and worldviews, that relate humanity to supernatural or spiritual elements—though there is no current fully agreed definition on what a religion exactly is.
title: Religion

text: Many philosophies and religions say that a soul is a supernatural essence of a living human being that lives after death. It is usually said to be immortal.
title: Soul

text: Buddhism is a dharmic religion that originated in ancient India, based on the teachings of Siddhartha Gautama better known as The Buddha "the Awakened one".
title: Buddhism

text: Christianity is a Abrahamic monotheistic world religion which is based on the life and teachings of Jesus, his crucifixion and death, and his resurrection, and on his apostles, disciples, and followers.
title: Christianity

text: The Roman Catholic Church is the largest Christian church in the world. It has over one billion members, and is the world's largest religious group.
title: Catholic Church

text: Protestantism is a form of Christian faith and practice. It began in northern Europe in the early 16th century.
title: Protestantism

text: Islam is an Abrahamic religion. It believes in one God.
title: Islam

text: Shia Islam (Arabic: شِيعَةٌ) is a sect of Islam which believes that Prophet Muhammad was commanded by Allah to choose Ali as caliph, his successor, Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law, and his descendants, and that Muhammad publicly declared it during his last sermon after the Hajj at Ghadir Khumm.
title: Shia Islam

text: Sunni Islam (Arabic: أَهْلُ السُّنَّةِ) is the biggest branch of Islam and came through the Rashidun Empire, which started with Abu Bakr and ended by Ali ibn Abi Talib. Sunni beliefs are based on the Qur'an and the Kutub al-Sittah.
title: Sunni Islam

text: Jainism is a dharmic religion which originated in ancient India.
title: Jainism

text: Judaism (Hebrew: יהדות) is the religion of Jewish people, and also the world's oldest Abrahamic monotheistic religion. It was created around the 6th century BCE in Canaan, and it is based on the Torah.
title: Judaism

text: Shinto (Japanese: 神道) is a form of Japanese animism. It has many kami, translated as gods or nature spirits.
title: Shinto

text: Sikhism (ਸਿੱਖ ਧਰਮ) is a monotheistic-dharmic religion and philosophy that originated in the Punjab region of the Indian subcontinent around the beginning of the 16th century. It is one of the newest major religions, ranking as the fifth-largest worldwide, with about 25–30 million followers known as the Sikhs.
title: Sikhism

text: Taoism or Daoism (道教) is both a philosophy and religion originated in China, which has 2,500 years of history.
title: Taoism

text: Zoroastrianism is an ancient Iranian religion created by Zoroaster, who lived in eastern ancient Iran around 1000 BC. Other names for Zoroastrianism are Mazdaism and Parsiism.
title: Zoroastrianism

text: Society is the term to describe human beings together as a collective entity – the sum of their social networks and social interactions.
title: Society

text: Civilization (or civilisation) comes from the Latin word civis meaning someone who lives in a city. The Romans usually wanted conquered people to live in towns.
title: Civilization

text: Education is about learning skills and knowledge. It also means helping people to learn how to do things and support them to think about what they learn.
title: Education

text: Behavior (or behaviour) is what a person or animal does and how they act. Behaviors may be conscious or unconscious.
title: Behavior

text: Emotions are what people feel. They are very ancient, and can be seen in all mammals.
title: Emotion

text: Love is a mix of feelings and actions that shows a deep liking for someone or something. Love involves caring for another.
title: Love

text: The mind is a general term for the way a person thinks, reasons, perceives, wills, has ideas, and has emotion. For science, what others call the mind is entirely caused by workings of the brain.
title: Mind

text: Psychology is the study of the mind and brain. It studies thoughts, feelings, and behaviors in humans and animals.
title: Psychology

text: Thought is the operation of the brain in conscious activity. It may or may not be goal-directed, aimed at solving specific problems.
title: Thought

text: A family is a group of people who, in most cases, live together. They share their money and food and are supposed to take care of one another.
title: Family

text: A child (the plural is children) is a person below the age of puberty (biologically) or, at least in English-speaking countries, below the age of majority or in other contexts below the age of consent. A person can be called his or her parent's child, regardless of the person's age.
title: Child

text: A man is an adult male human. Culturally, he is considered the opposite of a woman.
title: Man

text: Marriage is a contract by which two people agree to live together as a couple for an extended period of time or for the rest of their lives, often with the aim of starting a family by having or adopting children.
title: Marriage

text: A woman is an adult female human. The plural of "woman" is "women".
title: Woman

text: Politics (from Ancient Greek πολιτικά (politiká) 'affairs of the cities') is the way that people living in groups make planned decisions.
title: Politics

text: Colonialism occurs when a country or a nation takes control of other countries, regions, or territories outside of its borders (boundaries of the country) by turning those other countries, regions, or territories into a colony.
title: Colonialism

text: Diplomacy is about relations between countries. For example, countries can make an agreement together, such as a treaty.
title: Diplomacy

text: A government is a group of people that have the power to rule in a territory, according to the administrative law. This territory may be a country, a state or province within a country, or a region.
title: Government

text: A dictatorship is a form of government, where one person effectively has all the power to run a country without having elections. This person is called a dictator.
title: Dictatorship

text: A monarchy is a kind of government where a monarch, a kind of hereditary ruler (someone who inherits their office), is the head of state. Monarchs usually rule until they die or pass down (when a monarch resigns it is called abdication).
title: Monarchy

text: A republic is a form of government that has no monarchy and no hereditary aristocracy, and instead the head of state (the highest political authority) is an elected office It originates from Rome.
title: Republic

text: An ideology is a collection of ideas or beliefs shared by a group of people. It may be a connected set of ideas, or a style of thought, or a world-view.
title: Ideology

text: Anarchism is an idea and philosophy that says no one should be forced into any kind of hierarchy. For example, anarchism says that the government and capitalism are harmful and not needed.
title: Anarchism

text: Capitalism is an economic system in which the means of production are privately owned and operated with the goal of earning profit.
title: Capitalism

text: Communism is an idea in politics based on equality, that seeks a world without different social class groups. They say that things like factories, tools and farms (the relations of production) are owned by the bourgeoisie.
title: Communism

text: Conservatism is a type of political belief that supports emphasis on traditions and relies on the individual to maintain society. The term was first used by François-René de Chateaubriand in 1818, during the Bourbon Restoration, which wanted to roll back the policies of the French Revolution.
title: Conservatism

text: Fascism is a far-right form of government where most of the country's power is held by one ruler or a small group, under one political party.
title: Fascism

text: Liberalism is a type of political thinking about politics and government. It emphasizes the idea of freedom, and believes that the greatest countries are the ones that contain unconfined liberties.
title: Liberalism

text: Marxism is the name for a set of political and economic ideas.
title: Marxism

text: Nationalism is the idea of promoting the interests of a particular nation. Mostly it includes interests in the sovereignty of their own country or homeland.
title: Nationalism

text: Socialism is an economic system in which industries are owned by workers rather than by private businesses. It is different from capitalism, where private actors, like business owners and shareholders, own the means of production.
title: Socialism

text: Imperialism is a policy (way of governing) in which large or powerful countries seek to extend their authority beyond their own borders. The policy of imperialism aims at the creation of an empire.
title: Imperialism

text: A political party is an organized group of people or bodies who seek to capture political power through an election in order to run the affairs of a country. It often puts forward candidates for public office.
title: Political party

text: Propaganda is a form of communication to distribute information. It is usually biased.
title: Propaganda

text: Economics is the social science which studies economic activity: how people make choices to get what they want. It has been called "the study of scarcity and choice" (scarcity is when there is not a lot of something).
title: Economics

text: Capital has a number of related meanings in economics, finance and accounting.
title: Capital (economics)

text: Currency is a unit of money used for buying and selling goods and services, commonly backed by a country or a union of countries.
title: Currency

text: Euro or € is the currency of the countries in the eurozone. One euro is divided into 100 cent (officially) (singular) or "cents" (unofficially).
title: Euro

text: The United States dollar (or American dollar) is the official currency (money) of the United States of America. It is also used in some other countries outside the US.
title: United States dollar

text: In economics, different kinds of manufacturing and services are broken down into groups called industries. The word comes from a Latin word meaning "working diligently at a task".
title: Industry

text: Money, also sometimes called currency, can be defined as anything that people use to buy goods and services. Money is what many people receive for selling their own things or services.
title: Money

text: Tax is money that people have to pay to the government.
title: Tax

text: To trade is to willingly give things or services and get other things or services in return. For example, a person giving a thing must find another person who wants to get that thing.
title: Trade

text: Law is a set of rules made by a particular place or authority to keep society safe and peaceful.
title: Law

text: The constitution of a country (or a state) is a special type of law document that tells how its government is supposed to work.
title: Constitution

text: The African Union (AU) is a continental union consisting of fifty-five member countries located in Africa.
title: African Union

text: The Arab League is an organization made up of countries in the Arab world in Northern Africa and Southwest Asia. Most, though not all of these countries use Arabic as their official language.
title: Arab League

text: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is an international organization. On 8th August 1967, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore, and the Philippines formed the ASEAN.
title: Association of Southeast Asian Nations

text: The Commonwealth of Nations (also known only as "Commonwealth") is a voluntary organisation of countries. Originally, it was called the British Commonwealth which was founded in 1926 when the British Empire began to break up.
title: Commonwealth of Nations

text: The European Union (abbreviation: EU) is a union of 27 member countries in Europe on the landmass of Eurasia. It was created by the Maastricht Treaty in 1993.
title: European Union

text: The International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement is a movement to save human life and health. Its headquarters are in Geneva, Switzerland.
title: International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement

text: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization (sometimes known as the North Atlantic Alliance, the Atlantic Alliance or the Western Alliance), also simply called NATO, is a military alliance that is mostly in Europe and North America.
title: NATO

text: Every year, the Nobel Prizes (Swedish: Nobelpriset) are given to people and institutions around the world. These prizes are for the study of science and for world peace.
title: Nobel Prize

text: OPEC, the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries is an international organization. Since 1965, the headquarters of OPEC has been in Vienna, Austria.
title: OPEC

text: The United Nations (UN) is an organization between countries established on 24 October 1945 to promote international cooperation. It was founded to replace the League of Nations following World War II and to prevent another conflict.
title: United Nations

text: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is an international organization. 189 countries are members of the International Monetary Fund.
title: International Monetary Fund

text: UNESCO is the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (French: L'Organisation des Nations unies pour l’éducation, la science et la culture). It is an agency of the United Nations (UN).
title: UNESCO

text: The World Health Organization (WHO) is part of the United Nations (UN), working on international public health, with its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland. The WHO was established by the UN on April 7, 1948.
title: World Health Organization

text: The World Bank is an international bank that lends money and other help to developing nations for infrastructure. The World Bank has the goal of reducing poverty.
title: World Bank

text: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is a large international organization to regulate trade that was established in 1995. As of 2018, there are 164 members and 23 observer nations.
title: World Trade Organization

text: Military forces (often called the military when specific to a certain group) are groups of people that are given power to defend a country or territory with weapons. They are armed, so they are called the armed forces.
title: Military

text: Peace is a time without any fights or wars. In a larger sense, peace (or peacefulness) can mean a state of harmony, quiet or calm that is not disturbed by anything at all, like a still pond with no ripples.
title: Peace

text: Terrorism is the use of fear and violence for political, religious or ideological reasons. Many different types of social or political organizations might use terrorism to try to achieve their goals.
title: Terrorism

text: War is a situation or a period of fighting between countries or groups of people. A war generally involves the use of weapons, a military organization and soldiers.
title: War

text: A civil war is a type of war that takes place between two or more groups in one country. While civil wars can take place for many reasons, there are two common reasons.
title: Civil war

text: An abortion is a medical procedure (also called induced abortion) that ends a pregnancy before birth. It can be done surgically or with medicine.
title: Abortion

text: The death penalty, also called capital punishment, is when a government or state executes (kills) someone. Usually (but not always) this is punishment for committing a serious crime.
title: Death penalty

text: Discrimination is when someone is treated unfairly or differently because the person is one of a particular group. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights affirms that all persons must be protected against any kind of discrimination, or even its inciting.
title: Discrimination

text: Racism is the belief that one race, culture or tribe is better than others. It means judging or treating people badly for belonging to a certain race or ethnic group.
title: Racism

text: Feminism is a social, political, and economic movement. It is about changing the way that people see male and female rights and campaigning for equal rights.
title: Feminism

text: Globalization is the spread of products, technology, information, and jobs across nations.
title: Globalization

text: Human rights are rights and freedoms that all people should have.
title: Human rights

text: Poverty means not having enough money for basic needs such as food, drinking water, shelter, or toiletries. Many people in different countries live in poverty, especially in developing areas of West and Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, Caribbean and some parts of Asia.
title: Poverty

text: Slavery is when a person is treated as the property of another person. This person is usually called a slave, and the owner is called a slavemaster.
title: Slavery

text: Language is the normal way humans communicate. Only humans use language, though other animals communicate through other means.
title: Language

text: Arabic (اَلْعَرَبِيَّةُ, al-ʿarabiyyah) is a Central Semitic language that first appeared in the mid-ninth century BCE in Northern Arabia and Sahara southern Levant. It is related to other Semitic languages like Hebrew and Aramaic.
title: Arabic language

text: Bengali is an eastern Indo-Aryan language. It developed from a language called Pali.
title: Bengali language

text: The Chinese language is the group of languages used by Chinese people in China and elsewhere. It forms part of a language family called the Sino-Tibetan family of languages.
title: Chinese language

text: English is a language that started as the language of the Anglo-Saxons, in England. It is in the Germanic language family (the same family as German, Dutch, Swedish and others), but it was influenced a lot by Old French, so many words are similar to words in Romance languages (such as French, Spanish, or Romanian).
title: English language

text: German (German: Deutsch) is a West Germanic language. It is spoken in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and Luxembourg; natively by around 100 million people.
title: German language

text: The Greek language, also referred to as the Grecian language, is an Indo-European language that is the official language of Greece (Hellas) and Cyprus. It was first spoken in Greece and was also once spoken along the coast of Asia Minor (now part of Turkey) and in southern Italy.
title: Greek language

text: The Hebrew language, also referred to as the Hebraic language, is a Northwest Semitic language and is related to Arabic. It is the only dead language that has been revived.
title: Hebrew language

text: Hindustani is an Indo-Aryan language. It is widely spoken in India and Pakistan.
title: Hindustani language

text: Korean is spoken mainly in North and South Korea. It is spoken by more than 78 million people (most are North or South Koreans).
title: Korean language

text: Japanese (Japanese: 日本語, romanized: Nihongo) is the official language of Japan, in East Asia. Japanese belongs to the Japonic language family, which also includes the endangered Ryukyuan languages.
title: Japanese language

text: Latin is an Italic language that was developed in Ancient Rome. Short Latin texts have been found from about the 5th century BC and longer texts from about the 3rd century BC.
title: Latin

text: Persian, also called Farsi, is a Western Iranian language. It is one of the co official languages of Iran, Afghanistan and Tajikistan and is also spoken by some people in Pakistan and Uzbekistan.
title: Persian language

text: Portuguese (Portuguese: português) is a Romance language. It originated from Galician-Portuguese, which was first spoken in Northwestern Iberia.
title: Portuguese language

text: Russian (Russian: русский язык, transliterated as: russkiy yazyk) is a Slavic language. It is the main language spoken in Russia.
title: Russian language

text: Sanskrit (संस्कृत) is an ancient Indo-European language. Many languages in the Indian subcontinent today are derived from Sanskrit.
title: Sanskrit

text: Spanish (Spanish: español, pronounced "Eh-span-yole", IPA: /espaɲol/), also called Castilian, is a Romance language. It is the most spoken Romance language in the world.
title: Spanish language

text: The Swahili language is a language widely spoken in East Africa. In the language, its name is Kiswahili.
title: Swahili language

text: Turkish (Türkçe) is a language that is officially spoken in Turkey and Cyprus. Turkish is the 18th most-spoken language in the world.
title: Turkish language

text: Linguistics is the study of language. People who study language are called linguists.
title: Linguistics

text: Grammar is the study of words, how they are used in sentences, and how they change in different situations. The Ancient Greeks used to call it grammatikē tékhnē, the craft of letters.
title: Grammar

text: A word is something spoken by the mouth that is meaningful. It is usually part of a sentence which makes the meaning clear.
title: Word

text: Phonemes are the units of sound (speech) that distinguish one word from another in a particular language. Most varieties (accents and dialects) of spoken English have about 23 consonant phonemes and 21 vowel phonemes (altogether 44 phonemes) but only 26 letters in writing.
title: Phoneme

text: A syllable is a unit of pronunciation uttered without interruption, loosely, a single sound. All words are made from at least one syllable.
title: Syllable

text: A writing system (also called a script) is a system of symbols used to represent language. There are different kinds of writing systems, with symbols that represent different things.
title: Writing system

text: Chinese characters are symbols used to write the Chinese and Japanese languages. In the past, other languages like Korean and Vietnamese also used them.
title: Chinese characters

text: The Cyrillic script, sometimes called the Slavonic script or Slavic script, is a writing system. It is used to write Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian, Rusyn, Bulgarian, Macedonian and most South Slavic languages.
title: Cyrillic script

text: The modern Greek alphabet has 24 letters. It is used to write the Greek language.
title: Greek alphabet

text: The Latin or Roman script is a writing system used to write many modern-day languages including English. It is the most used writing system in the world today.
title: Latin script

text: Literacy means the ability to read and write. Being able to read and write is an important skill in modern societies.
title: Literacy

text: Translation means to copy writing or speech from one language into a different language.
title: Translation

text: Literature is a group of works of art that are made of words. Most are written, but some are shared by word of mouth.
title: Literature

text: Prose is the ordinary form of the written, or spoken, language. It is not poetry.
title: Prose

text: The Art of War (Chinese: 孫子兵法; pinyin: Sūnzĭ bīngfǎ) is an ancient Chinese military text that was written by Sun Tzu, a high-ranking military general, strategist, and Taoist philosopher over 2,500 years ago. The text contains 13 chapters, each of which covers an aspect of warfare.
title: The Art of War

text: Fiction is any story created by humans, originating from the depths of human imagination. It is not based on real-life events or actual people, but rather represents a departure from reality, allowing for the exploration of ideas, emotions, and scenarios that may not exist in the real world.
title: Fiction

text: One Thousand and One Nights is an old cycle (or group) of stories that mostly come from Arabia and Persia, and a few also from India, Central Asia and China. All these stories were later collected together.
title: One Thousand and One Nights

text: Novels are books that have one long story written in them. They are works of prose fiction and are longer than short stories and novellas.
title: Novel

text: The Tale of Genji (源氏物語, Genji Monogatari) is a classic work of Japanese literature.
title: The Tale of Genji

text: Poetry is written, spoken or sung language that is used in stronger or more original ways than prose is used. Poetry uses the meanings of words as prose does; but it also uses the sounds of words as if they were music, especially rhymes, other repeating sounds, and rhythms (beats or meters).
title: Poetry

text: The Epic of Gilgamesh is an epic poem from ancient Mesopotamia. It is one of the earliest works of literary fiction known.
title: Epic of Gilgamesh

text: The Iliad is the oldest surviving work of Greek literature. It was an oral epic poem.
title: Iliad

text: The Shahnameh or Shāhnāma (Book of Kings, Persian: شاهنامه) is a large poetic opus by the Persian poet Ferdowsi. The book was written between c. 977 to 1010 AD.
title: Shahnameh

text: The Bible, also known as the Holy Bible, is a group of religious texts central to Judaism and Christianity. The Christian Bible contains both the Old Testament and the New Testament.
title: Bible

text: Measurement means compare to a fix standard value. To measure something is to give a number to some property of the thing.
title: Measurement

text: The International System of Units is the standard modern form of the metric system. The name of this system can be shortened or abbreviated to SI, from the French name Système International d'unités.
title: International System of Units

text: The kilogram is the base unit of mass in the International System of Units (SI). It is widely used in science, engineering, and commerce worldwide.
title: Kilogram

text: The litre (international spelling) or liter (American spelling) (symbol: l or L) is one of the metric units of volume. It is not a basic SI unit, but it is a supplementary unit.
title: Litre

text: The metre (British spelling) or meter (American spelling) (symbol: m) is the basic unit of length in the SI measurement system. The symbol for the metre is m.
title: Metre

text: A calendar is a tool for organizing days. People use calendars to say when something happened, and for planning things that have not happened yet.
title: Calendar

text: The Gregorian calendar is the calendar that is used throughout most of the world. It began being used in 1582.
title: Gregorian calendar

text: A clock is a device that tells the time. Some clocks can only show the time.
title: Clock

text: The second (symbol: s), is a unit of time. There are 60 seconds in a minute, 60 minutes in an hour, and 24 hours in a day.
title: Second

text: A day is the time it takes the Earth to spin around once. It is daytime on the side of the Earth that is facing the Sun.
title: Day

text: The year (symbol: y or a, also known as the annum or annus) is about 365 days (except in a leap year). It is the time it takes the Earth to go completely around (orbit) the sun once.
title: Year

text: Time zones give specific areas on the Earth a time of day that is earlier or later than the neighboring time zones. This is because when it is daytime on one side of the earth, it is night-time on the other side.
title: Time zone

text: Science is what we do to find out about the natural world. There are different kinds of science.
title: Science

text: The words nature and natural are used for all the things that are normally not made by humans. The word comes from the Latin natura meaning "birth".
title: Nature

text: Astronomy is the scientific study of celestial bodies. It is a major branch of space science.
title: Astronomy

text: An asteroid is a minor planet that orbits within the inner solar system. It is a small object in the Solar System that travels around the Sun.
title: Asteroid

text: The Big Bang is a physical theory about how the universe started expanding, and then made the stars and galaxies we see today. The Big Bang is the name that scientists use for the most common theory of the universe, from the very early stages to the present day.
title: Big Bang

text: A black hole is a place in space where gravity is so strong that nothing can escape from it, even light. This idea comes from Albert Einstein's general theory of relativity.
title: Black hole

text: A comet is a ball of mostly ice that moves around in outer space. Comets are often described as "dirty snowballs".
title: Comet

text: A galaxy is a group of many stars, with gas, dust, and dark matter. The name 'galaxy' is taken from the Greek word galaxia meaning milky, a reference to our own galaxy, the Milky Way.
title: Galaxy

text: The Milky Way is our home galaxy. It contains around 400 billion stars, including our Sun.
title: Milky Way

text: The Moon, also known as Luna, is Earth's only natural satellite (the only object which orbits the Earth and is not man-made). It is usually visible in the night sky, but is sometimes seen during the day.
title: Moon

text: A planet is a large object such as Venus or Earth that orbits a star. Planets do not make light but can reflect light.
title: Planet

text: Mercury is the first planet from the Sun. It is the second hottest planet, and the smallest in the Solar System.
title: Mercury (planet)

text: Venus is the second planet from the Sun. Venus is the only planet in the Solar System that has a day longer than a year.
title: Venus

text: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only known place where life exists. One big reason life can exist here is that Earth has a lot of water on its surface, being the only planet in our Solar System with liquid water.
title: Earth

text: Mars, also known as The Red Planet, is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second-smallest planet in the Solar System, after Mercury.
title: Mars

text: Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System. It is the fifth planet from the Sun.
title: Jupiter

text: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun in our solar system. On average, Saturn is about 9.57 astronomical units (1,432 Gm; 1.432×109 km; 890,000,000 mi) away from the Sun.
title: Saturn

text: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun in our Solar System. Like Neptune, it is an ice giant.
title: Uranus

text: Neptune is the eighth and farthest planet from the Sun in the Solar System. It is an ice giant and the fourth-largest planet in the system.
title: Neptune

text: The Solar System is a group of space objects that are held together by gravity, with the Sun in the center. The Sun is a huge ball of hot glowing gas that gives off light and heat.
title: Solar System

text: Spaceflight is when an object (or spacecraft) made by man flies into outer space. A spaceflight can occur with or without humans on board.
title: Spaceflight

text: A star is a very large ball of bright, glowing, hot matter in space. That matter is called plasma.
title: Star

text: The Sun, also known as Sol, is a star at the center of the solar system. It is a white star that gives off different types of energy such as infrared energy (heat), ultraviolet light, radio waves and light.
title: Sun

text: The universe is space and everything in it. It is made of billions of stars, planets, and enormous clouds of gas separated by huge voids of space.
title: Universe

text: Biology is the science that studies life, living things, and the evolution of life. Living things include animals, plants, fungi (such as mushrooms), and microorganisms such as bacteria and archaea.
title: Biology

text: DNA, short for deoxyribonucleic acid, is the molecule that contains the genetic code of living organisms. This includes animals, plants, protists, archaea and bacteria.
title: DNA

text: An enzyme is a protein molecule in cells which works as a biological catalyst. Enzymes speed up chemical reactions but do not get used while doing so, so they can be used over and over again.
title: Enzyme

text: Hormones are the chemical messengers of the endocrine system. Hormones are the signals which adjust the body's internal working, together with the nervous system.
title: Hormone

text: Proteins are long-chain molecules built from small units known as amino acids, which are joined in a sequence by peptide bonds. Every sequence of amino acids becomes a specific final shape, allowing living things to use proteins as tiny machines to do work.
title: Protein

text: Botany is the study of plants. It is a science.
title: Botany

text: Death is the end of a life in an organism. All biological and living activity of the living thing stops, including the mind and the senses.
title: Death

text: Ecology is the branch or aspect of biology that studies the biota (living things), the environment, and their interactions. It comes from the Greek oikos = house; logos = study.
title: Ecology

text: An endangered species is a group of animals or plants which is threatened by becoming extinct. This could happen because there are few of that animal left, its predators have grown in number, or the climate that it lives in is changing, or the places it lives in have been destroyed.
title: Endangered species

text: Life is matter that can make more of itself. It is separated by non-living matter.
title: Life

text: Biological classification is how biologists group organisms.
title: Biological classification

text: A species is a kind of organism. It is a basic unit of biological classification, and a formal rank in taxonomy.
title: Species

text: Metabolism is the chemical reactions which keep us alive. It happens in the cells of living organisms.
title: Metabolism

text: Digestion is the process of breaking down food to absorb it. Food is broken down into smaller pieces, which are soluble in water.
title: Digestion

text: Photosynthesis is a process in which green plants make their own food from sunlight, using the help of leaves to produce sugar. It is the process by which these organisms convert light energy into chemical energy, which is used to produce food.
title: Photosynthesis

text: Evolution is a biological process. It is how living things change over time and how new species develop.
title: Evolution

text: Pregnancy is when an individual with a uterus has an unborn baby (a prenatal foetus) inside of them. Humans give birth to live young.
title: Pregnancy

text: An organism is any individual living thing. It is easy to recognize a living thing but, not so easy to define it.
title: Organism

text: Animals (or Metazoa) are living creatures with many cells that make up the kingdom Animalia.
title: Animal

text: The nematodes or roundworms are one of the most diverse of all animal phyla. They are one of the protostome phyla.
title: Nematode

text: Mollusks are an important phylum of invertebrate animals. Most of them are marine animals, which means they live in the ocean.
title: Mollusc
