text: Arthropods (Greek language for "joint-legged") are a large group of invertebrate animals. Insects, spiders, crabs, shrimp, millipedes, and centipedes are all arthropods.
title: Arthropod

text: Insects are a class in the phylum Arthropoda. They are small terrestrial invertebrates which have a hard exoskeleton.
title: Insect

text: Ants are a species of insect that live together in large colonies. They are in the family Formicidae. it is an authentic animal for organisation.
title: Ant

text: Bees are flying insects of the Hymenoptera, which also includes ants, wasps and sawflies. There are about 20,000 species of bees.
title: Bee

text: A mosquito is the common name of a family of flies in the order Diptera.
title: Mosquito

text: Spiders (class Arachnida, order Araneae) are air-breathing arthropods. They have eight legs, and mouthparts (chelicerae) with fangs that inject venom.
title: Spider

text: Amphibians are members of the class Amphibia. The living ones are frogs (including toads), salamanders (including newts) and caecilians.
title: Amphibian

text: Birds (Aves) are a group of animals with backbones. Birds are the only dinosaurs that survived the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction, and are part of the theropod group of dinosaurs.
title: Bird

text: Chicken refers to the domesticated subspecies of the red junglefowl. It is raised in many places for its meat and eggs.
title: Chicken

text: Pigeons or doves are in the bird family Columbidae.
title: Dove

text: Fish (plural: fish or fishes) are a group of animals which live in water and respire (get oxygen) from their gills. As a group, they are much older than other vertebrates.
title: Fish

text: Sharks are a superorder of fish. This superorder is also known by its scientific name Selachimorpha.
title: Shark

text: Mammals are in the class Mammalia. They are a group of vertebrate animals.
title: Mammal

text: Camels are mammals of the Camelidae family. Camels form the genus Camelus.
title: Camel

text: Cats, also called domestic cats (Felis catus), are small, carnivorous (meat eating) mammals, of the family Felidae. Cats have been domesticated (tamed) for nearly 10,000 years.
title: Cat

text: Cattle is a word for certain mammals that belong to the genus Bos. Cattle may be cows, bulls, oxen, or calves.
title: Cattle

text: The order Cetacea are marine mammals that live in oceans, seas and even a few rivers around the world. Whales, dolphins and porpoises are part of this group.
title: Cetacea

text: Dogs are mammals, usually to be kept as pets, or work on farms or for the police. Some dogs are trained to be rescue dogs and join teams such as mountain rescue.
title: Dog

text: Horses are a group of animals of the family Equidae.
title: Horse

text: A domestic sheep (Ovis aries) is a domesticated mammal related to wild sheep and goats. Sheep are owned and looked after by a sheep farmer.
title: Domestic sheep

text: Rodents (from Latin rodere, "to gnaw"), are mammals of the order Rodentia, which are characterized by a single pair of continuously growing incisors in each of the upper and lower jaws.
title: Rodent

text: Pigs or domestic pigs are mammals in the genus Sus. Pigs are in the Suidae family of even-toed ungulates.
title: Pig

text: Primates are an order of mammals. It includes all lemurs, tarsiers, lorises, galagos, monkeys and apes (including humans).
title: Primate

text: A human, or human being, is a member of the species Homo sapiens, which means 'wise man' in Latin. Carolus Linnaeus put humans in the mammalian order of primates.
title: Human

text: Reptile is the common name for one of the main groups of land vertebrates. It is not used so much by biologists, who use more accurate terms.
title: Reptile

text: Dinosaurs are a group of Archosaur reptiles of the clade Dinosauria. Dinosaurs eventually gave rise to birds.
title: Dinosaur

text: Snakes, otherwise known as serpentes, are reptiles. They are part of the order Squamata.
title: Snake

text: Algae (singular: alga, plural: algae) are plant-like living things. They make food from sunlight by photosynthesis.
title: Algae

text: The Archaea (or Archea) are a group of single-celled organisms. The name comes from Greek αρχαία, "old ones".
title: Archaea

text: Bacteria (singular: bacterium) are very small organisms. They are prokaryotic microorganisms.
title: Bacteria

text: A fungus (plural: fungi) is a type of living organism that includes yeasts, molds, mushrooms and others. Fungi are a category of organism as large and varied as the animals or plants.
title: Fungus

text: Plants are one of six big groups (kingdoms) of living things. They are autotrophic eukaryotes, this means they have complex cells, and make their own food.
title: Plant

text: A flower is the reproductive part of flowering plants. Flowers are also called the bloom or blossom of a plant.
title: Flower

text: In botany, a fruit is a plant structure that contains the plant's seeds.
title: Fruit

text: A tree is a tall plant with a trunk and branches made of wood.
title: Tree

text: Protists are single-celled eukaryotes (which are organisms with a nucleus). The term Protista was first used by Ernst Haeckel in 1866.
title: Protist

text: Anatomy is the study of the bodies of people and other animals. Anatomy is the study of the inside of the body and outside the body.
title: Anatomy

text: In biology, the cell is the basic structure of organisms. All living things are made up of cells, from the organs in the human body to the parts of plants.
title: Cell

text: The circulatory system (also called the cardiovascular system) is the body system that moves blood around the body. It consists of the heart and blood vessels.
title: Circulatory system

text: Blood is a liquid in humans and many animals. There are about 5 litres of blood in the human body.
title: Blood

text: The heart is a hard-working, fist-sized muscle found in people and animals. It pumps out blood through tube-like structures called blood vessels.
title: Heart

text: The endocrine system includes those organs of the body which produce hormones.
title: Endocrine system

text: The digestive system is a part of the body that digests food. It is called the gastrointestinal system.
title: Human digestive system

text: The Large intestine is also called the colon or large bowel. It connects the small intestine to the rectum and anus.
title: Large intestine

text: The small intestine is between the stomach and the large intestine, and is where most of the digestion and absorption happen. In humans over five years old, the small intestine is about 7.5 metres long.
title: Small intestine

text: The liver is an organ in the abdomen. It is part of the digestive system.
title: Liver

text: Muscle is a tissue in animal bodies. Muscles are basically tissue which may contract (shorten).
title: Muscle

text: The nervous system is a body system which sends signals around the body. It lets animals respond to what is around them.
title: Nervous system

text: The brain is the part of the body which lets living beings think. It does some bodily functions, such as telling the rest of the body what to do.
title: Brain

text: A nerve is a group of special nerve cells grouped together in parallel. Another word for nerve cell is neuron.
title: Nerve

text: The sensory system is the way animals find out about their nearby environment and their bodies. To do this they have special devices for collecting data called sense organs.
title: Sensory system

text: The ear is the part of the body which allows animals (including people) to hear. People and most mammals have ears.
title: Ear

text: A nose is a body part which allows animals to smell things. The nose also helps animals breathe.
title: Nose

text: The eye is a round organ for sensing light so organisms can see. It is the first part of the visual system.
title: Eye

text: Taste is one of the five main senses that helps people and animals enjoy and understand the food they eat. It allows us to notice different flavors, such as sweet, salty, sour, bitter, and umami (a savory taste).
title: Taste

text: A skeleton is the hard structure that protects the internal organs of a living thing. Skeletons can be inside the body or outside the body.
title: Skeleton

text: The skin is the outer covering of mammals and some other animals. It has many important jobs.
title: Skin

text: Medicine is the science that treats and prevents diseases in humans. Medical workers treat injuries, infections, and sickness.
title: Medicine

text: Dentistry is a specialty in medicine, which is practiced by a dentist. Dentists find out what's wrong, fix, and help prevent problems with teeth.
title: Dentistry

text: A disease or medical condition is an unhealthy state where something bad happens to the body or mind. Diseases can cause pain, parts of the body to stop working the right way, or death.
title: Disease

text: Medication (also called medicine or pharmaceutical drugs) is the use of legal drugs to treat or cure an illness.
title: Medication

text: An antibiotic (or antibacterial) is a chemical compound is made to kill bacteria or slow their growth. They are used as medicines to treat and cure disease caused by bacteria.
title: Antibiotics

text: Health is a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being, and not merely the absence of disease according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Physical health is about the body.
title: Health

text: The immune system is the set of tissues which work together to resist infections. The immune mechanisms help an organism identify a pathogen, and neutralize its threat.
title: Immune system

text: A pandemic (from Greek παν pan all + δήμος demos people) is an epidemic (an outbreak of an infectious disease) that spreads across a large region (like a continent), or even worldwide.
title: Pandemic

text: A vaccine is a biological preparation. It is given to prevent a specific infectious or malignant disease.
title: Vaccine

text: A virus is a tiny parasite. Viruses reproduce inside other living things; they are not free-living.
title: Virus

text: Addiction is when the body or mind badly wants or needs something in order to work right. When you have an addiction to something it is called being addicted or being an addict.
title: Addiction

text: Ethanol, also known as ethyl alcohol, grain alcohol or just alcohol, is a flammable, colorless chemical compound whose chemical formula is C2H5OH, also written as C2H6O. It is the active part of alcoholic drinks, which are drunk in most cultures worldwide.
title: Ethanol

text: Tobacco is a product prepared from the leaves of the tobacco plant by curing them. The plant is part of the genus Nicotiana and of the Solanaceae (nightshade) family.
title: Tobacco

text: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a brain disease that slowly destroys brain cells. As of now, there is no cure for Alzheimer's disease.
title: Alzheimer's disease

text: Cancer is a type of disease where cells grow out of control, divide and invade other tissues. In a person without cancer, cell division is under control.
title: Cancer

text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), also known as chronic obstructive lung disease (COLD), and chronic obstructive airway disease (COAD), is a collection of obstructive pulmonary diseases which make breathing gradually more difficult.
title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

text: The common cold is caused by viruses. It spreads easily, so it is very infectious.
title: Common cold

text: A disability is a condition that a person has which limits them in some way. These conditions may be congenital (present at birth), cognitive (associated with the brain), developmental (appears as the person develops) and physical, which can be caused by an accident or infection.
title: Disability

text: Blindness is to not see anything. Some people are called blind, even though they can see a little bit.
title: Blindness

text: Deafness is when someone cannot hear at all, or cannot hear well. Deafness is also known as 'hearing loss'.
title: Deafness

text: A mental illness is an illness of the mind. It can be a psychiatric disorder, a psychological disorder, mental disease, mental breakdown, nervous breakdown, or mental health conditions.
title: Mental illness

text: Epilepsy is a chronic condition of the brain. It is characterized by seizures that do not seem to have an obvious cause.
title: Epilepsy

text: Gastroenteritis is a medical term for inflammation of the stomach and intestines. It causes diarrhea, vomiting and stomach pain.
title: Gastroenteritis

text: A headache is when the head hurts. It is not head pain caused by hitting the head with something and causing injury, making it hurt that way.
title: Headache

text: A myocardial infarction, also and commonly called a heart attack, happens when a blood vessel in the heart suddenly becomes blocked. Blood vessels carry blood and oxygen.
title: Myocardial infarction

text: Influenza, better known as the flu and sometimes called the grippe, is a common childhood illness, but is not as common among adults. It is not limited to humans, most mammals and many birds can also catch influenza.
title: Influenza

text: Malaria is an infectious disease caused by a parasite, known as plasmodium. It is one of the most common diseases in the world.
title: Malaria

text: Obesity is the condition of being much too heavy for one's height so that one's health is affected. In other words, it means to be too overweight.
title: Obesity

text: Pneumonia is a disease of the lungs and the lower respiratory system. The lung contains many small bulbs, or sacs, called alveoli.
title: Pneumonia

text: Poliomyelitis, or polio, is a virus that causes a serious disease. It is spread from person to person.
title: Poliomyelitis

text: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome or Acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS) is a disease caused by a virus called HIV.
title: AIDS

text: Smallpox was a dangerous disease with a high mortality rate. It no longer exists as an epidemic disease.
title: Smallpox

text: A stroke is an illness in which part of the brain loses its blood supply. This can happen if an artery that feeds blood to the brain gets clogged, or if it tears and leaks.
title: Stroke

text: Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease caused by bacteria. In the past, people called it consumption or the white death.
title: Tuberculosis

text: Diabetes mellitus is a medical condition that results when there is not enough of the insulin hormone in the blood, or when the body cannot properly use the insulin it produces (insulin resistance). People with diabetes mellitus are called diabetics.
title: Diabetes mellitus

text: Chemistry is the science that studies what everything is made of and how it changes. It looks at matter, which is anything that takes up space.
title: Chemistry

text: Inorganic chemistry is the branch of chemistry which studies the elements, and inorganic compounds.
title: Inorganic chemistry

text: Biochemistry is the study of chemical reactions in living beings, and of biological molecules in general. It is important to cell biology and physiology.
title: Biochemistry

text: A chemical compound is a substance made of two or more different elements joined together by chemical bonds in a fixed ratio. Many compounds are made of separate molecules.
title: Chemical compound

text: An acid is a type of chemical compound. The definition of an acid has changed as people discovered more about chemistry.
title: Acid

text: A base is a substance that can accept a hydrogen ion (H+) from another substance. A chemical can accept a proton if it has a negative charge, or if the molecule has an electronegative atom like oxygen, nitrogen, or chlorine that is rich in electrons.
title: Base (chemistry)

text: In chemistry, a salt is any neutral chemical compound made of cations (positive ions) attached to anions (negative ions). The most common example of a salt is sodium chloride, with the chemical formula NaCl - this is the table salt that people use in food.
title: Salt

text: A chemical element is a substance that is made up of only one type of atom. Atoms are made up of protons, neutrons, and electrons.
title: Chemical element

text: The periodic table is a table that puts all known chemical elements in a specific order. Elements that have similar characteristics are often put near each other.
title: Periodic table

text: Aluminium (in American English: aluminum) is a chemical element. The symbol for aluminium is Al, and its atomic number is 13.
title: Aluminium

text: Carbon is a very important chemical element, with a chemical symbol of C. All known life on Earth needs it to survive. Carbon has atomic mass 12 and atomic number 6.
title: Carbon

text: Copper is a chemical element. It is the 29th element in the periodic table.
title: Copper

text: Gold is a soft, dense, bright yellow metal. It is a chemical element.
title: Gold

text: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe. It is the simplest element and the first in the periodic table.
title: Hydrogen

text: This article is about iron the metal. For the tool called iron, see ironing.
title: Iron

text: Nitrogen is a nonmetal chemical element. The atmosphere contains more than 78 percent of nitrogen.
title: Nitrogen

text: Oxygen is a chemical element. It has the symbol O and atomic number 8.
title: Oxygen

text: Silver (symbol Ag) is a chemical element. In chemistry, silver is element 47, a transition metal.
title: Silver

text: Tin is a chemical element with symbol Sn (for Latin: stannum) and atomic number 50. It is in Group 14 on the periodic table.
title: Tin

text: Organic chemistry is the study of chemical compounds that contain carbon. Carbon has the ability to form a chemical bond with a wide variety of chemical elements and other carbon atoms because of its 4 valence, or outermost, electrons.
title: Organic chemistry

text: In chemistry, alcohol is a general term which refers to many organic compounds used in industry and science as reagents, solvents, and fuels. Common alcohols include rubbing alcohol, grain alcohol, wood alcohol, ethylene glycol, glycerin, and phenol.
title: Alcohol (chemistry)

text: Carbohydrates are chemical compounds that contain only oxygen, hydrogen and carbon. They are made up of joined-up sugars.
title: Carbohydrate

text: A lipid is a type of organic molecule found in living things. It is oily or waxy.
title: Lipid

text: A molecule is the smallest amount of a chemical substance that can exist. If a molecule were split into smaller pieces, it would be a different substance.
title: Molecule

text: Analytical chemistry is the part of chemistry that focuses on finding out what a substance is, how much of it there is, and what it is made of. It helps scientists figure out exactly what’s in a sample and in what amounts through analysis.
title: Analytical chemistry

text: Physical chemistry uses physics to study chemical systems. It studies them at macroscopic, atomic, subatomic, and particulate levels.
title: Physical chemistry

text: Climate means the usual condition of the temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, wind, rainfall, and other meteorological patterns in an area of the Earth's surface for a long time. In simple terms, climate is the average condition for about thirty years.
title: Climate

text: The water cycle, or hydrological cycle, is the cycle that water goes through on Earth.
title: Water cycle

text: Global warming or global heating is the rise in temperature of Earth’s air and oceans. It is happening mainly because humans burn coal, oil, natural gas, and cut down forests.
title: Global warming

text: An earthquake is when Earth's tectonic plates shake and move Earth's surface. Strong earthquakes damage buildings.
title: Earthquake

text: Geology is the study of the nonliving things that the Earth is made of. Geology is the study of rocks in the Earth's crust.
title: Geology

text: Minerals are substances that are formed naturally in the Earth. Minerals vary in composition, from pure elements and simple salts to very complex silicates with thousands of known forms.
title: Mineral

text: A diamond (from the ancient Greek αδάμας – adámas "unbreakable") is a mineral made out of carbon atoms.
title: Diamond

text: Plate tectonics is a theory of geology. It explains movement of the Earth's lithosphere.
title: Plate tectonics

text: Rocks are a naturally occurring solid. Some rocks are man made which means they are created in a factory like concrete or ceramic pipes.
title: Rock (geology)

text: A natural disaster is a major event caused by the natural processes of the Earth. Examples are floods, hurricanes, tornadoes, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, tsunamis and other geologic processes.
title: Natural disaster

text: A flood is an overflow of water. Floods are very hard to deal with.
title: Flood

text: A tsunami (from Japanese, meaning “harbor wave”) is a natural disaster, a series of fast-moving waves in the ocean caused by powerful earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, landslides, or a meteor impact in the ocean. A tsunami starts as a small wave and builds up into a larger wave, and starts suddenly.
title: Tsunami

text: A volcano is a mountain that has lava (hot, liquid rock) coming out from a magma chamber under the ground, or did have in the past. Volcanoes are formed by the movement of tectonic plates.
title: Volcano

text: Weather is the day-to-day or hour-to-hour change in the atmosphere. Weather includes wind, lightning, storms, hurricanes, tornadoes, rain, hail, snow, and lots more.
title: Weather

text: A cloud is water vapour in the atmosphere (sky) that has condensed into very small water droplets or ice crystals that appear in visible shapes or formations above the ground.
title: Cloud

text: Rain is a kind of precipitation. Precipitation is any kind of water that falls from clouds in the sky, like rain, hail, sleet and snow.
title: Rain

text: Snow is a form of ice. Snow forms when water in the atmosphere becomes frozen.
title: Snow

text: A tornado is an area of fast spinning winds made by a strong rotating thunderstorm that touches the ground. Tornadoes can be anywhere between a few hundred feet wide and several thousand feet wide.
title: Tornado

text: A tropical cyclone is a circular air movement that begins over the warm ocean waters in the warm part of Earth near the equator. Most tropical cyclones create fast winds and heavy rain.
title: Tropical cyclone

text: Wind is the flow of gases. On Earth, wind is mostly the movement of air.
title: Wind

text: Physics is the science of how things move in space and time and how the universe works. It studies matter and forces.
title: Physics

text: Acceleration is a measure of how fast velocity changes. Acceleration is the change of velocity divided by the change of time.
title: Acceleration

text: An atom is an extremely small piece of matter. All normal matter – everything that has mass – is made of atoms.
title: Atom

text: This article refers to the law of conservation of energy in physics. For energy resources sustainably, see: Energy conservation.
title: Conservation of energy

text: Electromagnetic waves are waves that contain an electric field and a magnetic field and carry energy. They travel at the speed of light (299,792,458 meters per second).
title: Electromagnetic radiation

text: Infrared (IR) radiation is a type of electromagnetic radiation (a wave with electricity). The wave is longer than light which humans can see and shorter than microwaves.
title: Infrared

text: Ultraviolet is the part of the electromagnetic spectrum shown on the left side of the picture below as black—because humans cannot see light of such short wavelength (or high frequency). Many animals such as some insects, some reptiles, crocodiles, salamanders, and small birds can see things that reflect this light.
title: Ultraviolet

text: Light is a form of electromagnetic radiation. It is natural agent that stimulates sight and makes things easier to see.
title: Light

text: Color (or colour in Commonwealth English; see spelling differences) is a property of light.
title: Color

text: Classical mechanics is the part of physics that describes how everyday things move and how their motion changes because of forces. If we know how things are moving now, classical mechanics allows us to predict how they will move in the future and how they were moving in the past.
title: Classical mechanics

text: In physics, a force is a push or pull or a twist between objects. It is called an interaction because if one object acts on another, its action is matched by a reaction from the other object.
title: Force

text: The magnetic field is a vector field around a magnet in which there is magnetic force. Moving electric charges can make magnetic fields.
title: Magnetic field

text: Gravity, or gravitation is one of the fundamental forces of the universe. It is an attraction, or pull, between any two objects with mass.
title: Gravity

text: The strong interaction or strong nuclear force is one of the four fundamental forces in physics.
title: Strong interaction

text: Weak interaction, the weak force or weak nuclear force, is one of the four fundamental forces in the universe.
title: Weak interaction

text: A magnet is made of magnetic metals such as iron, nickel, or cobalt, and sometimes certain rare earth metals like neodymium. When a magnet goes near one of these magnetic metals or another magnet, and the poles (sides) touching are opposite, it will pull, or attract the other object closer.
title: Magnet

text: The mass of an object is a measure of how much of it there is. For example, A mountain has more mass than a rock.
title: Mass

text: Some chemical elements are called metals. Most elements in the periodic table are metals.
title: Metal

text: Steel is iron mixed with carbon and sometimes other metals. It is harder and stronger than iron.
title: Steel

text: Nuclear fission, is a kind of nuclear reaction. It is when an atom splits apart into smaller atoms.
title: Nuclear fission

text: There are four common states of matter (or phases) in the universe: solid, liquid, gas, and plasma.
title: States of matter

text: A gas is one of the main forms, or states, of matter, like solids, liquids, and plasmas. What makes gases special is that they do not have a fixed shape or a set volume.
title: Gas

text: A liquid is a form of matter. It is settled between solid and gas.
title: Liquid

text: Solid is one of the four common states of matter. The molecules in solids are closely bound together, so they can only vibrate.
title: Solid

text: Quantum mechanics explains how the universe works with things that are even smaller than atoms. It is also called quantum physics or quantum theory.
title: Quantum mechanics

text: General relativity is a theory of space and time. The theory was published by Albert Einstein in 1915.
title: General relativity

text: Special relativity (or the special theory of relativity) is a theory (Well supported idea) in physics that was developed and explained by Albert Einstein in 1905. It applies to all physical phenomena, so long as gravitation is not significant.
title: Special relativity

text: A semiconductor is a material that in some cases will conduct electricity but not in others. Good electrical conductors, like copper or silver, easily allow electricity to flow through them.
title: Semiconductor

text: Sound can also mean a body of water, like a bay or channel.
title: Sound

text: Velocity is a measure of how fast something moves in a particular direction. To define it needs both magnitude and direction.
title: Velocity

text: The speed of light, in any medium, which is usually denoted by c, is a physical constant important in many areas of physics. It is denoted by "c0" especially in vacuum medium, although the symbol 'c' can be used to refer to that in any medium.
title: Speed of light

text: Temperature is how hot or cold something is. The human body can feel the difference between something which is hot and something which is cold.
title: Temperature

text: Time is the continued proсess of existence and events. It happens in an apparently irreversible way from the history, through the now and to the future.
title: Time

text: Thermodynamics is a branch of physics that studies the relations between heat, temperature, and energy. A branch of math called statistics is often used in thermodynamics to look at the motion of particles.
title: Thermodynamics

text: A vacuum is a place where there is no matter, not even air. Sound cannot move in a vacuum.
title: Vacuum

text: Mathematics is the study of numbers, shapes, and patterns and letters. The word comes from the Greek μάθημα (máthema), meaning "science, knowledge, or learning", and is sometimes shortened to math or maths.
title: Mathematics

text: In mathematics, arithmetic is the basic study of numbers. The four basic arithmetic operations are addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, although other operations such as exponentiation and roots are also studied in arithmetic.
title: Arithmetic

text: Logarithms or logs are a part of mathematics. They are related to exponential functions.
title: Logarithm

text: Number theory is a part of mathematics. It explains what some types of numbers are, what properties they have, and ways that they can be useful.
title: Number theory

text: Algebra is a part of mathematics. It uses variables to represent a value that is not yet known or can be replaced with any value.
title: Algebra

text: A complex number is a number, but is different from common numbers in many ways. A complex number is made up using two numbers combined.
title: Complex number

text: A mathematical equation is a mathematical object containing two or more expressions connected by equals signs (=). The equals sign says that all of the expressions describe the same mathematical object.
title: Equation

text: Linear algebra is a branch of mathematics. It came from mathematicians trying to solve systems of linear equations.
title: Linear algebra

text: Geometry (from Ancient Greek: Γεωμετρία (romanized: Geometria (English: "Land measurement") derived from Γη (romanized: Ge; English: "Earth" or "land") and also derived from Μέτρον) (romanized: Métron; English: "A measure")) is a branch of mathematics that studies the size, shapes, positions and dimensions of things.
title: Geometry

text: When two straight lines come together, they make an angle. The two lines are called the sides of the angle, and they meet at a point.
title: Angle

text: Area is the amount of space a two dimensional (flat) surface takes up. It is useful because it is how much of a material is needed to make a hollow container.
title: Area

text: A coordinate system is a system of numbers used to uniquely determine the position of a point. For two-dimensional systems, the numbers (scalars) are in ordered pairs.
title: Coordinate system

text: In mathematics, the Pythagorean theorem or Pythagoras's theorem is a statement about the sides of a right triangle.
title: Pythagorean theorem

text: Symmetry is a property of some geometrical objects. Objects with symmetry appear the same when reflected along an axis or when rotated around a point.
title: Symmetry

text: Trigonometry (from the Greek trigonon = three angles and metron = measure) is a part of elementary mathematics dealing with angles, triangles and trigonometric functions such as sine (abbreviated sin), cosine (abbreviated cos) and tangent (abbreviated tan).
title: Trigonometry

text: Mathematical analysis is a part of mathematics. It is often shortened to analysis.
title: Mathematical analysis

text: Probability is a part of applied mathematics. It has to do with chance, the study of things that might happen or might not happen.
title: Probability

text: Statistics is a branch of applied mathematics that deals with collecting, organizing, analyzing, reading and presenting data. Descriptive statistics make summaries of data.
title: Statistics

text: In mathematics, a function is a mathematical object that produces an output, when given an input (which could be a number, a vector, or anything that can exist inside a set of things).
title: Function (mathematics)

text: Infinity (∞) is a mathematical concept which is about things that never end. It is written in a single digit.
title: Infinity

text: A mathematical proof is a way to show that a mathematical theorem is true. To prove a theorem is to show that theorem holds in all cases (where it claims to hold).
title: Mathematical proof

text: Set theory is the study of sets in mathematics. Sets are collections of objects.
title: Set theory

text: Farming is growing crops and keeping animals for food and raw materials. Farming is a significant part of agriculture.
title: Farming

text: Irrigation is when people add water to plants, to help them grow when there is not enough rain. Irrigation water can be pumped from rivers, natural lakes or lakes created by dams, from wells or allowed to flow to the fields by or open canals.
title: Irrigation

text: A plow or plough is a tool or machine used for several jobs, like farming and snow removal. It is pushed or pulled across the ground.
title: Plow

text: Domestication is a change that happens in wild animals or plants, when they are kept by humans for a long time. The Latin term literally means "to make it suitable for home".
title: Domestication

text: Food is what people and apes eat to live. Every organism needs energy to carry on with the process of living which comes from food.
title: Food

text: Bread is a type of baked food. It is mainly made from dough, which is made mainly from flour and water.
title: Bread

text: Cereal usually refers to a type of grass that is grown to be eaten. Some, such as wheat, are mostly used to feed people.
title: Cereal

text: Barley is a member of the grass family of plants. Its seeds are a cereal grain.
title: Barley

text: Maize or Indian corn (called corn in some countries) is Zea mays, a member of the grass family Poaceae. It is a cereal grain which was first grown by people in ancient Central America.
title: Maize

text: Rice (Oryza sativa) is a type of cereal and food. In origin, it is a swamp grass.
title: Rice

text: Wheat (Genus: Triticum) is a cereal grain. People eat it most often in the form of bread.
title: Wheat

text: Chocolate is a food made from cacao beans. It is used in many desserts like pudding, cakes, candy, ice cream, and Easter eggs.
title: Chocolate

text: Honey is a food made by honeybees from nectar. They put the honey into a honeycomb, which for them is a storage unit.
title: Honey

text: The apple tree comes from southern Kazakhstan; Kyrgyzstan; Uzbekistan; Turkey; and the northwestern part of China. Apples have been grown for thousands of years in Asia and in Europe.
title: Apple

text: A banana is the common name for a type of fruit and also the name for the herbaceous plants that grow it. These plants belong to the genus Musa.
title: Banana

text: Citrus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs in the rue family, Rutaceae.
title: Citrus

text: Grapes are the fruit of a woody grape vine. Grapes can be eaten raw, or used for making wine, juice, and jelly/jam.
title: Grape

text: A nut is a hard-shelled fruit of some plants. They are an important part of the diet.
title: Nut (fruit)

text: The soybean (or soya bean) is a plant with fruit called beans, from Eastern Asia. The height of a grown soybean is between less than 20 centimetres and up to 2 metres.
title: Soybean

text: Meat is animal flesh which is used for food. Most often, it is used to describe skeletal muscles and fats that are found with it.
title: Meat

text: Sugar is the common name for several chemical substances, some of which taste sweet. Mostly, it refers to sucrose, lactose, or fructose.
title: Sugar

text: Spice is an ingredient that adds flavor to food. It is usually used to enrich or alter the quality of something.
title: Spice

text: Table salt is a mineral composed mainly of sodium chloride (NaCl). This is a chemical compound, one of many salts.
title: Table salt

text: Vegetables are a health food that are eaten by humans as part of a meal. This meaning is often used: it is applied to plants to mean all edible plant matter, including the flowers, fruits, stems, leaves, roots, and seeds.
title: Vegetable

text: A potato is a vegetable, the Solanum tuberosum. It is a small plant with big leaves.
title: Potato

text: Coffee is a caffeinated drink prepared from roasted coffee beans. It's also a plant (Coffea) and the name of the drink that is made from this plant.
title: Coffee

text: Juice is a liquid that comes from plants, animals or fruit. The juice from fruit is often made into a drink.
title: Juice

text: Milk is a white liquid made by mammals, like cows, dogs, and humans. It is made in the mammary glands (breasts, udders, or teats) of female mammals.
title: Milk

text: Tea is a caffeinated drink made from steeping the leaves of the Camellia sinensis plant. Tea can have other herbs, spices, or fruit flavors in it, like lemon.
title: Tea

text: Water (H2O) is a simple chemical compound made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. It is clear, has no taste or smell, and is almost colorless.
title: Water

text: Wine is an alcoholic drink. It is made from the juice of grape.
title: Wine

text: Technology is the skills, methods, and processes used to achieve goals. The word has been in use since the 17th century.
title: Technology

text: Biotechnology is a technology that involves the use of living organisms. Biotechnology is mainly used in agriculture, food science, and medicine.
title: Biotechnology

text: Clothing are items used to cover the human body. Humans are the only animals that wear clothing.
title: Clothing

text: Cotton is a soft, natural fiber that grows with the seeds of the cotton plant. (Fiber is long and thin, like hair.) After the cotton fiber is gathered from the plant, it can be spun into cotton thread. The cotton thread can then be made into cloth.
title: Cotton

text: Engineering is the use of science and math to design or make things. People who do engineering are called engineers.
title: Engineering

text: A machine is a thing that is created by people to make work easier. It is a tool or invention which multiplies the effect of human effort.
title: Machine

text: A robot is a machine that can move and do certain tasks and work.
title: Robot

text: A wheel is a disc or circle-shaped mechanical device. Its main purpose is to allow things to roll; in other words, the wheel spins, and object on the wheels moves more easily along the ground.
title: Wheel

text: Metallurgy is the study of metals. Alloys (mixtures of metals) are also studied.
title: Metallurgy

text: Nanotechnology is a part of science and technology about the control of matter on the atomic and molecular scale.
title: Nanotechnology

text: The word "information" is used in many different ways. Originally, it comes from a word that meant to give a form to something.
title: Information

text: An encyclopedia is a collection, usually a book or website, of information. Some are known as encyclopedic dictionaries.
title: Encyclopedia

text: Journalism is a type of writing. It includes writing for newspapers, news shows on television, news shows on radio, and news magazine.
title: Journalism

text: A newspaper is a publication printed on paper and issued regularly, usually once a day or once a week. It gives information and opinions about current events and news.
title: Newspaper

text: A library is a place where many books are kept. Most libraries are public and let people take the books to use in their home.
title: Library

text: A book is a set of printed sheets of paper held together between two covers. The sheets of paper in a book are called pages.
title: Book

text: Printing is putting words and images on paper by mechanical means. Books and newspapers are made by printing.
title: Printing

text: A telephone, also known as a phone, is a communication tool. People use it to talk with people far away.
title: Telephone

text: Electronics is the study of electricity (the flow of electrons) and how to use that to build things like computers. It uses circuits that are made with parts called components and connecting wires to do useful things.
title: Electronics

text: Frequency is how often an event repeats itself over a set amount of time.
title: Frequency

text: A capacitor (also called condenser, which is the older term) is an electronic device that stores electric energy. It is similar to a battery, but can be smaller, lightweight and a capacitor charges or discharges much quicker.
title: Capacitor

text: An inductor is an electrical device used in electrical circuits because it acts like inertia in the electrical circuit. Just like inertia opposes the change in state of motion, inductor opposes the change in electric current.
title: Inductor

text: A transistor is an electronic component that can be used as part of an amplifier, or as a switch. It is made of a semiconductor material.
title: Transistor

text: A diode is an electronic component with two electrodes (connectors) that allows electricity to go through it in one direction and not the other direction.
title: Diode

text: A resistor limits the electric current that flows through a circuit. Resistance is the restriction of current.
title: Resistor

text: A transformer is a device that transfers electrical energy from one electrical circuit to another, without sharing any wires. This happens because the first circuit creates a magnetic field as its power rises and falls.
title: Transformer

text: A computer is a machine that uses electronics to input, process, store, and output data. Data is information such as numbers, words, and lists.
title: Computer

text: A hard disk drive (HDD), hard disk or hard drive, is a data storage device for computers which uses magnetic storage to store data. The capacity of a hard drive is usually measured in gigabytes (GB), however hard disk capacity can also be measured in terabytes when the capacity is over 1000 or 1024 gigabytes.
title: Hard disk

text: A central processing unit (CPU) is an important part of every computer. The CPU sends signals to control the other parts of the computer, almost like how a brain controls a body.
title: Central processing unit

text: Information technology (or IT) is a word referring to all forms of technology used to create, store, exchange and use information in its various forms, such as data, voice, photos, business, conversations, still images, motion pictures, multimedia presentations.
title: Information technology

text: An algorithm is a list of steps that can be followed to solve a problem using a limited number of steps. For example, a recipe is an algorithm to prepare a dish in a limited amount of time.
title: Algorithm

text: The Internet is the world’s largest global communication network for computers and other devices.
title: Internet

text: Electronic mail (or e-mail or email) is an Internet service that allows people who have an e-mail address (accounts) to send and receive electronic letters. Those are much like postal letters, except that they are delivered much faster than snail mail when sending over long distances, and are usually free.
title: E-mail

text: "The Web" redirects here. For other uses, see Web (disambiguation).
title: World Wide Web

text: An operating system (OS) is a kind of computer program that helps a computer to interact with other machines or with people. An OS is not actually one single program but a group of small programs, like file managers, device drivers, and kernels.
title: Operating system

text: A programming language is a type of written language that tells computers what to do. Languages are often of two types, compiled or interpreted.
title: Programming language

text: Computer software, also called software, is a set of instructions and documentation that tells a computer what to do or how to perform a task. Software includes all different programs on a computer, such as applications and the operating system.
title: Software

text: Renewable energy comes from renewable resources. It is different from fossil fuels as it does not produce as many greenhouse gases and other pollutants as fossil fuel combustion.
title: Renewable energy

text: Electricity is the presence and flow of electric current. Using electricity, we can transfer energy in ways that make machines work.
title: Electricity

text: Nuclear power is the controlled use of nuclear energy. Nuclear energy can be released by nuclear reactions in a machine called a nuclear reactor.
title: Nuclear power

text: Fossil fuels are fuels that come from old life forms that decomposed over a long period of time. The three most important fossil fuels are coal, petroleum, and natural gas.
title: Fossil fuel

text: An internal combustion engine is an engine in which combustion, or the burning of fuel, occurs on the inside. This differs from external combustion engines where the fire is outside the engine, such as a steam engine.
title: Internal combustion engine

text: A steam engine is an engine that uses steam from boiling water to make it move. The steam pushes on the engine parts to make them move.
title: Steam engine

text: Fire is a chemical reaction that gives off light and heat. Fire happens when a material rapidly oxidizes, or loses electrons, and gives off a great amount of energy.
title: Fire

text: Glass is a hard material that can be made in many shapes. It is usually transparent, but it can also be made in colours.
title: Glass

text: Paper is a thin material of (mostly) wood fibres pressed together. People write on paper with a pencil or pen, and books are made of paper.
title: Paper

text: A plastic is a synthetic material that can change its shape easily. Many things are made of plastics, usually because making them to the right shape is easy.
title: Plastic

text: Wood is what keeps trees and shrubs upright, and what transports water from the roots to the leaves. The two main chemical substances in wood are cellulose and lignin.
title: Wood

text: Transport, or transportation, is moving people or things from one place to another place. Transport can be divided into infrastructure, vehicles and operations.
title: Transport

text: A bicycle (or bike) is a small, human powered land vehicle with a seat, two wheels, two pedals, and a metal chain connected to cogs on the pedals and rear wheel. A frame gives the bike strength, and the other parts are attached to the frame.
title: Bicycle

text: A car, or an automobile, is a motor vehicle with wheels. Most definitions of cars state that they run primarily on roads, seat 1-8 people, have four wheels, and mainly transport people rather than cargo but are relatively smaller than a truck/lorry (to carry goods) or a bus (to carry people).
title: Automobile

text: A submarine (or sub) is a vessel that goes underwater. Most large submarines are war vessels.
title: Submarine

text: A ship is a large vehicle used to travel on water. It is bigger than a boat.
title: Ship

text: A train (or rail train) is a set of railway cars (also called vehicles) that are tied together with or without a locomotive. Trains are used to carry people, and also things like raw material, finished goods, cargo, and waste.
title: Train

text: A weapon is an object that can be used to attack or injure a person or animal. People have used weapons since ancient times.
title: Weapon

text: A sword is a hand-held weapon made for cutting. It is often made of metal.
title: Sword

text: A gun (also called a firearm) is a weapon used to shoot one or more metal projectiles called bullets. Guns made of wood or bamboo are thought to have been made in China around 1000 AD.
title: Gun

text: A machine gun is a weapon that can fire one bullet after another as long as the trigger is pulled and there are bullets ready to fire. This is called automatic fire.
title: Machine gun

text: A nuclear weapon (also called a nuclear bomb or nuke) is a weapon that suddenly releases the energy in the nucleus of certain types of atoms. When triggered, the device releases a huge amount of energy in the form of a nuclear explosion.
title: Nuclear weapon

text: A tank is an armored fighting vehicle, typically armed with a gun mounted on a gun turret and a few machine guns.
title: Tank

text: Explosives are chemical compounds that cause explosions; they flare up and burst with a loud sound. Explosive material has many special characteristics: it is a chemically unstable material, it changes its form very fast and, while changing its form, it explodes by bursting and making loud sounds.
title: Explosive material

text: Gunpowder (or gun powder) is a mix of chemical substances (75% saltpeter, 15% charcoal and 10% sulfur). It is used primarily in firearms, burns very quickly, and creates gases.
title: Gunpowder

text: Culture is a word for the 'way of life' of groups of people, meaning the way they do things. Different groups may have different cultures.
title: Culture

text: Art is a creative activity. It produces a product, an object.
title: Art

text: In comics, stories or information are given using pictures, or pictures and words together. A story is told with pictures, mostly in panels.
title: Comics

text: Painting is using colors to make visual art. It is also the word for a painted work of art.
title: Painting

text: Photography is a way of making a picture using a camera. A person who makes pictures using a camera is called a photographer.
title: Photography

text: Sculpture is a type of art. It must be three-dimensional (meaning it must have height, width, and depth like a cube).
title: Sculpture

text: Pottery is the ceramic material which makes up potteryware. Major types include earthenware, stoneware and porcelain.
title: Pottery

text: Dance is a performing art. It is described in many ways.
title: Dance

text: Fashion is the form of clothing, accessories, and furniture. It includes the way we wear clothes in a particular time and place.
title: Fashion

text: Theatre (British English and also American English), or Theater (mostly American English), has several meanings.
title: Theatre

text: Calligraphy is the art of writing. The word is from the Greek language and means "beautiful writing".
title: Calligraphy

text: Architecture is the process of designing structures and buildings. It uses both art and engineering.
title: Architecture

text: An arch is an opening in a building that is curved on top to distribute the weight. The curved part can be round, like part of a circle, or pointed, like two parts of circles next to each other.
title: Arch

text: A bridge is a structure to cross an open space or gap. Bridges are mostly made for crossing rivers, valleys, or roads.
title: Bridge

text: A canal is a waterway made by humans. For many centuries, canals have been built as a way of transporting heavy goods in barges or boats.
title: Canal

text: A dam is a large wall or barrier that blocks or stops the flow of water, forming a reservoir or a lake. Most dams have a section called a spillway or weir over which, or through which, water flows, either sometimes or always.
title: Dam

text: A dome is a building or roof that usually looks like the upper half of a sphere.
title: Dome

text: A house is a building that is made for people to live in. It is usually built for a family (parents and their children).
title: House

text: Angkor Wat (Khmer: អង្គរវត្ត) is a temple in Siem Reap, Cambodia. It was built in the early 12th century by the Hindu king Suryavarman II as his state temple and capital city, built for the god Vishnu.
title: Angkor Wat

text: The Colosseum, also known as the Flavian Amphitheatre, is a large artefact or structure in the city of Rome. The construction of the Colosseum started around 70–72 AD and was finished in 80 AD.
title: Colosseum

text: The Great Wall of China (traditional Chinese: 萬里長城; simplified Chinese: 万里长城; pinyin: Wànlǐ Chángchéng, literally "ten thousand li long wall") is a series of fortifications in China.
title: Great Wall of China

text: The Empire State Building is a skyscraper in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. It is 1,454 feet (443 m) tall and has 102 floors.
title: Empire State Building

text: Hagia Sophia (Greek: Ἁγία Σοφία, meaning the Holy Wisdom) is a mosque in the eastern Bosporus of Istanbul, Turkey. It was originally a Byzantine Eastern Orthodox cathedral and was turned into a mosque after the conquest of Constantinople by the Ottoman Empire.
title: Hagia Sophia

text: The Parthenon is a temple in the middle of the Acropolis in Athens, Greece (Europe). It was a temple to honor the goddess Athena for nearly 900 years from the 5th century BC to the 5th century AD, and originally had a huge idol to her.
title: Parthenon

text: Giza Necropolis (also called the Giza pyramid complex) is a necropolis on the Giza Plateau near the city of Cairo, Egypt. It is about 8 kilometres (5 mi) inland into the desert from the ancient town of Giza on the Nile, and about 25 kilometres (15 mi) southwest of Cairo city centre.
title: Giza Necropolis

text: St. Peter's Basilica, which is called "Basilica di San Pietro in Vaticano" in Italian, is a large church in Vatican City, an independent country within Rome, Italy. It is often called “the greatest church in Christendom".
title: St. Peter's Basilica

text: The Statue of Liberty (officially named Liberty Enlightening the World and sometimes referred to as Lady Liberty) is a monument symbolising the United States. The statue is placed on Liberty Island, near New York City Harbor.
title: Statue of Liberty

text: The Taj Mahal is a Mughal Historical Site, mosque and tomb in India. It was built in the 17th century by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan as a mausoleum in memory of his wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
title: Taj Mahal

text: The Three Gorges Dam (Chinese: 长江三峡大坝) is a dam in the Three Gorges region on the Yangtze River in Sandouping, in the country of China.
title: Three Gorges Dam

text: A pyramid is a structure, usually made of stone, built in the shape of a pyramid. From ancient to modern times people in many different parts of the world have built such structures.
title: Pyramid

text: A tower is a tall structure. Towers are different from buildings because people do not live in them.
title: Tower

text: A movie or film is a type of visual art that uses images and sounds to tell stories, express ideas, or teach people something. Most people watch movies to entertain themselves or to have fun.
title: Movie

text: Animation is a way of making a movie from many images that don’t move. The images are put together one after another, and then played at a fast speed to make it look like movement.
title: Animation

text: Radio is a way to send electromagnetic signals over a long distance. It is mainly used to deliver information from one place to another.
title: Radio

text: A television set (also known as a television receiver or televisor or simply a television, TV set, TV receiver or TV) is a machine with a screen or set of lenses. Televisions receive broadcasting signals and change them into pictures and sound.
title: Television

text: Music is a form of art that uses sound organised in time. Music is also a form of entertainment that puts sounds together in a way that people like, find interesting or dance to.
title: Music

text: A song is a piece of music which contains lyrics and words. Songs may be made by songwriters.
title: Song

text: The blues is a form of music that started in the United States during the start of the 20th century. It was started by former African slaves from spirituals, praise songs, and chants.
title: Blues

text: Classical music is a very general term which normally refers to the standard music of countries in the western world. It is music that has been composed by musicians who are trained in the art of writing music (composing) and written down in music notation so that other musicians can play it.
title: Classical music

text: Opera is a drama set to music. An opera is like a play in which everything is sung instead of spoken.
title: Opera

text: A symphony is a piece of music written for an orchestra to play. It may be quite a long piece.
title: Symphony

text: Electronic music is music which is made with electronic equipment such as synthesizers or computers. Sometimes electronic music artists create special sounds using tape recorders too.
title: Electronic music

text: Flamenco is a style of baile. It is a form of entertainment with song, music and dance.
title: Flamenco

text: Hip hop is a type of culture/art style that started in the 1970s in The Bronx. It began in Jamaican American, African American, and Puerto Rican/Hispanic and Latino American urban areas in some of the larger cities of the United States.
title: Hip hop

text: Jazz is a type of music which was invented in the United States. Jazz music combines African-American music with European music.
title: Jazz

text: Reggae is a music genre that is from Jamaica that was developed in the late 1960s. Most music from Jamaica comes from the reggae style.
title: Reggae

text: Rock music is a genre of popular music. It developed in the late 1900s, chiefly in the United States.
title: Rock music

text: Samba is a kind of music, dancing, and singing, originally from Brazil. It began as a music/dance movement in the 1920s.
title: Samba

text: A drum is a musical instrument. It is played with the hands, sometimes using a drum stick (a stick for hitting a drum).
title: Drum

text: The flute is a musical instrument. A person who plays the flute is called a flautist.
title: Flute

text: The guitar is a string instrument which is played by plucking the strings. The main parts of a guitar are the body, the fretboard, the headstock and the strings.
title: Guitar

text: The piano is an acoustic, keyboard, stringed and percussive instrument in which the strings are struck by wooden hammers that are coated with a softer material (modern hammers are covered with dense wool felt; some early pianos used leather).
title: Piano

text: A trumpet is a brass instrument used mainly in Classical music and jazz music. The most common type of trumpet is a B♭ trumpet, meaning that if the player plays a C, it will sound like a B♭ in concert pitch.
title: Trumpet

text: The violin is a string instrument which has four strings and is played with a bow. The strings are usually tuned to the notes G, D, A, and E. It is held between the left collar bone (near the shoulder) and the chin.
title: Violin

text: A game is something that people often do for fun. It is different from work.
title: Game

text: Backgammon is a game played by two players. Each player moves pieces around a board.
title: Backgammon

text: Chess is a board game for two players. It is played on a square board, made up of 64 smaller squares, with eight squares in each row and column.
title: Chess

text: Go is a board game for two players. It is called Wei-k'i (or Wei-chi) in Chinese, Patok or Baduk in Korean and I-go in Japanese.
title: Go (board game)

text: A video game is an electronic game played on a video screen (normally a television, computer monitor, or built-in screen when played on a handheld machine).
title: Video game

text: Gambling is a contest where a player bets on the result of an event. The bet is generally in the form of money.
title: Gambling

text: A martial art is any form of fighting and an art that has a set way of practice. There are many martial arts that come from certain countries.
title: Martial arts

text: Judo (柔道, jūdō) is a modern Japanese martial art and Olympic sport. It was developed in 1882 by Jigorō Kanō.
title: Judo

text: The Olympic Games (French: Jeux olympiques) is an important international event featuring summer and winter sports. Summer Olympic Games and Winter Olympic Games are held every four years.
title: Olympic Games

text: Sport usually means athletic games that involve a degree of competition, such as football, basketball or cross-country Olympic skiing. Some games and many kinds of racing are called sports.
title: Sport

text: Athletics is an exclusive collection of sporting events that include competitive running, jumping, throwing, and walking. The most common types of athletics competitions are track and field, road running, cross country running, and race walking.
title: Athletics (sport)

text: Baseball is a bat-and-ball sport played on a field by two teams against each other. In baseball, a player on one team throws a small round ball at a player on the other team, who tries to hit it with a bat.
title: Baseball

text: Basketball is a team sport where two teams (usually consisting of five players) + Bench players making up the rest of the roster. They play against each other on a basketball court it a rectangular playing surface consisting of four straight boundaries arranged into two pairs of parallel lines.
title: Basketball

text: Cricket is a sport. It is an outdoor bat-and-ball game played by two teams of eleven players on a large, grassy field.
title: Cricket

text: Rugby football is a sports that is played in many countries and is populary known as rugby or rugger.
title: Rugby football

text: Tennis is a sport played with a felt-covered rubber ball, a tennis racket, and a court. It is quite popular, and many people enjoy watching it.
title: Tennis

text: Swimming is the movement of the body through water using arms and legs. People can swim in the sea, swimming pools, rivers and lakes.
title: Swimming

text: A toy is something to play with. Toys are for children, adults, and animals.
title: Toy

text: Ancient Egypt was a society that began around 3150 BCE and lasted until 30 BCE, when it was invaded by the Romans.
title: Ancient Egypt

text: Ancient Greek civilization, also commonly called Ancient Greece, was a large area, mostly along the northeast shore of the Mediterranean Sea, where people spoke the Greek language. The area was much larger than today's country of Greece.
title: Ancient Greece

text: The Bronze Age is a period in human prehistory when people made tools from bronze, an alloy (mixture) of metals.
title: Bronze Age

text: The Gupta Empire was an Indian empire which lasted from around 320 to 550 AD. It managed to unify large parts of the Indian subcontinent.
title: Gupta Empire

text: The Han dynasty came to power in 202 BC. They followed the laws of Confucianism and legalism.
title: Han dynasty

text: The Iron Age is the period after the Bronze Age in Europe, Asia, and parts of Africa. Iron production took place in Anatolia at least as early as 1200 BC, with some evidence pointing to even earlier dates.
title: Iron Age

text: The Maya civilization was a pre-Colombian Central American civilization from around 2000 BC to 1698 CE.
title: Mayan civilization

text: Mesopotamia (Ancient Greek: Μεσοποταμία - "land between rivers") is a historical region in the Middle East. It included most of today’s Iraq, and parts of modern-day Iran, Syria and Turkey.
title: Mesopotamia

text: Prehistory (or better known as Pre-history) is the time before people began to write. It lasted from around 4.5 billion BC – 3000 BC, during the Stone Age.
title: Prehistory

text: The Roman Empire ruled the Mediterranean and much of Europe, Western Asia and North Africa. The Romans conquered most of this during the Republic, and it was ruled by emperors following Octavian's assumption of effective sole rule in 27 BC.
title: Roman Empire

text: Sumer is the earliest known civilization in southern Mesopotamia, in what is now southern Iraq. Sumer may have been one of the first civilizations in the world, along with Ancient Egypt and the Indus Valley.
title: Sumer

text: The Stone Age was a prehistoric time when people made tools from stone such as flint. It began when people created the first stone tools about 3.3 million years ago.
title: Stone Age

text: The Tang dynasty (Chinese: 唐朝; pinyin: Tángcháo) (June 18, 618 – June 4, 907) was an imperial dynasty of China.
title: Tang dynasty

text: The Abbasid Caliphate was the third Arab Islamic caliphate. It overthrew the Umayyad caliphs from all but Al-Andalus.
title: Abbasid Caliphate

text: The Aztecs were Native American people who lived in Mesoamerica. They ruled the Aztec Empire from the 14th century to the 16th century.
title: Aztecs

text: The Byzantine Empire, also formally called the Eastern Roman Empire, was the continuation of the Roman Empire primarily in its eastern provinces that survived into the Late Antiquity and the Middle Ages.
title: Byzantine Empire

text: The Crusades were a series of religious wars initiated, supported, and sometimes directed by the Christian Latin Church in the medieval period.
title: Crusades

text: The Holy Roman Empire (Latin: Sacrum Imperium Romanum; German: Heiliges Römisches Reich), occasionally but unofficially referred to as the Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation, was a polity in Western and Central Europe under the rule of an emperor, who was elected by the princes and the magistrates of its regions and cities.
title: Holy Roman Empire

text: The Inca were a pre-Columbian country and empire in the Andes of South America. The word 'Inca' can also mean the emperor or king of the Inca people.
title: Inca Empire

text: The Mali Empire was a West African realm from 1267 to 1641. The Mandinka people lived there they still are in some parts of Africa today.
title: Mali Empire

text: The Middle Ages were a period of about 1000 years in European history. They took place between the end of the Western Roman Empire in 476 CE when Romulus Augustulus was deposed, and the beginning of the Renaissance around 1400 - 1500 CE.
title: Middle Ages

text: The Ming dynasty was the family of emperors who led China from AD 1368 to 1644. The name is also used to talk about the Ming Empire that they led and the 276 years in Chinese history that it lasted.
title: Ming dynasty

text: The Mongol Empire existed in the 13th and the 14th centuries and was one of the largest land empires in history.
title: Mongol Empire

text: The Renaissance is a period in European history that followed the Middle Ages and ended in the 17th century. Renaissance is a French word for “cultural rebirth.” During this period, there was a “rebirth” of classical learning.
title: Renaissance

text: The Vikings were Scandinavian people from Northern Europe who were known as great seamen and warriors. The Scandinavian countries include Norway, Sweden and Denmark.
title: Vikings

text: The Age of Enlightenment was an 18th-century intellectual movement in Europe to make people more aware about science rather than religion and tradition. It was heavily influenced by philosophers like Locke, Voltaire, Diderot and Kant.
title: Age of Enlightenment

text: The American Civil War (1861–1865) was a civil war in the United States of America. It was fought when 11 Southern states left the United States and formed the Confederate States of America (also called the Confederacy).
title: American Civil War

text: The Arab–Israeli conflict is a term used to describe the political tensions and open hostilities between the Arab countries of the Middle East and North Africa and the State of Israel. The conflict has gone on since 1948.
title: Arab–Israeli conflict

text: Apartheid was a racist political and social system in South Africa and South West Africa (now Namibia) during the era of white minority rule (1910-1994). Apartheid enforced racial segregation and it existed from 1948 to 1994.
title: Apartheid

text: The British Empire was the largest empire in world history and for a century was the largest global power. It included British dominions, colonies, protectorates, mandates, and other territories.
title: British Empire

text: The Cold War (1947-1991) was the fighting between the United States and its allies and the Soviet Union and its allies between the end of World War II and the fall of the Soviet Union. It is called the "Cold" War because the Americans and the Soviets never actually fought each other directly.
title: Cold War

text: The French Revolution was a revolution in France from 1789 to 1799. It ended the French monarchy.
title: French Revolution

text: The Great Depression was the global economic crisis that started after the U.S. stock market crash in 1929. The prices on the Wall Street stock market greatly fell from October 24 to 29, 1929.
title: Great Depression

text: The Holocaust was the genocide of Jews in Europe by Nazi Germany, other Axis powers and their local collaborators in occupied territories between 1933 and 1945. At least 6,000,000 (six million) Jews (67% pre-war European Jews) were killed.
title: The Holocaust

text: The Industrial Revolution is the name of the time when there was a big change in the way things were made. Instead of things being hand-made in small workshops, they were made more cheaply in large quantities by machines in factories.
title: Industrial Revolution

text: Nazi Germany (officially known as the German Reich from 1933 to 1943, later known as the Greater German Reich from 1943 to 1945; commonly simply called Germany), was the period of Germany between 1933 and 1945.
title: Nazi Germany

text: The Meiji Restoration (明治維新) was a time of great change in Japan. In the Japanese language, Meiji-ishin is the term for the Meiji Restoration.
title: Meiji Restoration

text: The Protestant Reformation was a series of events that happened in the 16th century in the Catholic Church. Because the Catholic Church had been accused of corruption, some people wanted changes to the way the Church worked.
title: Protestant Reformation

text: The Russian Revolution was a period of political and social reform in Russia, starting in 1917. This period saw Russia abolish its monarchy and adopt a socialist form of government following two successful revolutions and a civil war.
title: Russian Revolution

text: The Qing Dynasty or the Qing Empire (Chinese: 清朝; pinyin: Qīng cháo) was a dynasty of rulers of China from 1644 to 1912. The dynasty was founded by the Manchus and so its other name is the Manchu dynasty.
title: Qing dynasty

text: The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (Russian: Союз Советских Социалистических Республик, tr.
title: Soviet Union

text: The Vietnam War (also known as the Second Indochina War, Vietnamese-American War or the American War in Vietnam) is a war fought between North Vietnam and South Vietnam, and their allies, from 1 November 1955 to 30 April 1975.
title: Vietnam War

text: World War I (WWI or WW1), also called the First World War, or the Great War, began on 28 July 1914 and lasted until 11 November 1918. It was a global conflict and lasted exactly 4 years, 3 months and 2 weeks.
title: World War I

text: World War II, or the Second World War, was a global conflict (1 September 1939 – 2 September 1945) which involved fighting between the Allies and the Axis.
title: World War II

text: Geography (from Greek: γεωγραφία, geographia, literally "earth description") is the study of earth and its people. It is one of the social sciences.
title: Geography

text: A city is a place where many people live close together.
title: City

text: A forest is a piece of land with many trees. Forests are important and grow in many places around the world.
title: Forest

text: A mountain is a large natural rise of the Earth's surface that usually has a "summit" (the name for a mountain's top, which can also be called a peak). It is usually steeper and taller than a hill.
title: Mountain

text: A desert is an arid (dry) biome. They get less than 25 cm (9.8 inches) of rainfall a year.
title: Desert

text: The North Pole is the point that is farthest north on Earth. It is the point on which axis of Earth turns.
title: North Pole

text: An ocean is a large body of water between continents. Oceans are extremely big and they join smaller seas together.
title: Ocean

text: A river is a stream of water that flows through a channel on the surface of the ground. The passage where the river flows is called the riverbed and the earth on each side is called a riverbank.
title: River

text: A sea is a large body of salt water. It may be an ocean, or may be a large saltwater lake which like the Caspian Sea, lacks a natural outlet.
title: Sea

text: The South Pole is the most southern point on the Earth. It is in Antarctica and is the center of the Southern Hemisphere.
title: South Pole

text: Africa is the second largest continent on Earth. It makes up about one-fifth of the world's total land area.
title: Africa

text: Antarctica is the Earth's southernmost and the continent with the least people. It is on the South Pole.
title: Antarctica

text: Asia is the largest continent on Earth by area and number of people. It is mainly in the northern hemisphere.
title: Asia

text: Europe is the western part of the continent of Eurasia, often thought of as its own continent. It is separated from Asia by the Ural Mountains in Russia and the Bosporus strait in Turkey.
title: Europe

text: The Middle East is a large area of land in the eastern hemisphere. The lands of the Arabian Peninsula and some of the lands of the eastern Mediterranean are part of the Middle East.
title: Middle East

text: North America is a large continent in the Northern and Western Hemispheres of Earth. It is to the east of the Pacific Ocean, the west of the Atlantic Ocean, the south of the Arctic Ocean, and it is the northern part of the Americas.
title: North America

text: Oceania is a large geographical region in the Pacific Ocean. It is made up of 14 countries in the surrounding area.
title: Oceania

text: South America is the continent to the south of North America. These two continents are separated by the Panama Canal.
title: South America

text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (French: République démocratique du Congo), commonly referred to as DR Congo, Congo-Kinshasa or the DRC, is a country in central Africa. It was known as Zaïre from 1971 to 1997.
title: Democratic Republic of the Congo

text: Egypt, officially the Arab Republic of Egypt, is a country in the Middle East and the Eastern Mediterranean, located in North Africa and Western Asia.
title: Egypt

text: Ethiopia has one of the longest known histories as a country in Africa. Ethiopia was one of the few countries in Africa that escaped the Scramble for Africa.
title: Ethiopia

text: Nigeria, officially Federal Republic of Nigeria, is a country in Africa.
title: Nigeria

text: South Africa, officially called the Republic of South Africa, is a country in the southern region of Africa. About fifty-seven million people live there.
title: South Africa

text: Sudan is a country in East Africa. The official name of Sudan is The Republic of the Sudan.
title: Sudan

text: Tanzania is a country in East Africa. The official languages are Kiswahili and English.
title: Tanzania

text: Afghanistan, officially the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan is a country in Asia. It borders Pakistan in the south and east (border with India is disputed), Iran in the west, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan in the north, and China in the far northeast.
title: Afghanistan

text: Bangladesh, officially called the People's Republic of Bangladesh (Bengali: গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ), is a country in South Asia. It is the eighth most populated country in the world and one of the most tightly packed, with more than 170 million people living in an area of 148,460 square kilometres (57,320 sq mi).
title: Bangladesh

text: The People's Republic of China (PRC) (simplified Chinese: 中华人民共和国; traditional Chinese: 中華人民共和國) is a Communist one-party state in East Asia governed by the Communist Party of China (CPC). It was founded on 1 October 1949 after the Kuomintang (KMT) fled to Taiwan.
title: People's Republic of China

text: India (भारत (Hindi) Bhārat Gaṇarājya), officially the Republic of India, also known as Hindustān, is a country in South Asia. It is the world's seventh-largest country by area.
title: India

text: Iran, officially the Islamic Republic of Iran and also known as Persia, is a country in Western Asia. Prior to 1935, the country was referred to by majority in the Western world as Persia.
title: Iran

text: Iraq is a country in southwestern Asia. Iraq borders Saudi Arabia and Kuwait to the south, Turkey to the north, Syria to the northwest, Jordan to the west, and Iran to the east.
title: Iraq

text: Israel (Hebrew: יִשְׂרָאֵל), officially the State of Israel (Hebrew: מְדִינַת יִשְׂרָאֵל), is a country in southwestern Asia on the eastern side of the Mediterranean Sea. Its capital city is Jerusalem.
title: Israel

text: Japan (Japanese: 日本 にほん; Romanized as Nihon or Nippon) is a country in East Asia. It is a group of islands close to the east coast of Korea, China and Russia.
title: Japan

text: Pakistan, officially the Islamic Republic of Pakistan (Urdu: Islāmī Jumhūriyah Pākistān), is a country in South Asia. It shares its border with other countries India, Iran, Afghanistan and China (disputed with India).
title: Pakistan

text: The Philippines is an island country in Southeast Asia in the Pacific Ocean. It has 7,641 islands.
title: Philippines

text: Saudi Arabia (Arabic: السعودية as-Su‘ūdiyyah or as-Sa‘ūdiyya), officially known as the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) (Arabic: المملكة العربية السعودية al-Mamlakatu 'l-‘Arabiyyatu 's-Su‘ūdiyyah), is a country in West Asia including most of the Arabian Peninsula.
title: Saudi Arabia

text: South Korea is a country in the southern part of the Korean peninsula, in East Asia.
title: South Korea

text: Turkey, officially the Republic of Türkiye, is a transcontinental country located mainly on the Anatolian Peninsula in Western Asia, with a small portion on the Balkan Peninsula in Southeast Europe.
title: Turkey

text: The Socialist Republic of Vietnam (or just Vietnam) (Vietnamese: Cộng hòa Xã hội chủ nghĩa Việt Nam) is a country in Southeast Asia. The neighboring countries are Cambodia, China, and Laos.
title: Vietnam

text: Germany is a country in the western region of Central Europe. The country's full name is sometimes shortened to the FRG (or the BRD, in German).
title: Germany

text: The Netherlands (also referred to as Holland) is a country that is part (of a constituent country) of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Most of it is in Western Europe, but there are also some parts in the Caribbean.
title: Netherlands

text: Poland is a country in the eastern region of Central Europe. Its official name is Republic of Poland.
title: Poland

text: Portugal (Portuguese: República Portuguesa) is a country in Southern Europe on the Iberian Peninsula. It is bordered by the North Atlantic Ocean to the west and south and by Spain to the north and east.
title: Portugal

text: Spain is a country in Europe that controls much of the Iberian Peninsula and nearby islands. The people of Spain are called Spaniards, and in 2026, the population of Spain was about 49.8 million.
title: Spain

text: Switzerland (German: Schweiz; French: Suisse; Italian: Svizzera; Romansh: Svizra; Swiss German: Schwiz) is a country in Western Europe. Switzerland is a federation of 26 cantons.
title: Switzerland

text: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, often shortened to the United Kingdom (UK), or just Britain, is a sovereign country in Northwestern Europe. It is a constitutional monarchy of four countries: England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
title: United Kingdom
