text: Canada is a country in North America. Its land reaches from the Atlantic Ocean to the east to the Pacific Ocean to the west.
title: Canada

text: Cuba is an island country in the Caribbean Sea. The country is made up of the big island of Cuba, the Isla de la Juventud island (Isle of Youth), and many smaller islands.
title: Cuba

text: Mexico, officially the United Mexican States, is a country in North America. It borders the United States to the north, and Guatemala and Belize to the southeast; while having maritime boundaries with the Pacific Ocean to the west, the Caribbean Sea to the southeast, and the Gulf of Mexico to the east.
title: Mexico

text: The United States of America (USA or U.S.A.), also known as the United States (U.S. or US) or America, is a country that is located in North America. It is made of 50 states, a federal district (Washington, D.C., the District of Columbia), and some other territories and insular areas.
title: United States

text: Argentina, officially the Argentine Republic, is a country in South America. Argentina is the second-largest country in South America and the eighth-largest country in the world.
title: Argentina

text: Brazil, officially the Federative Republic of Brazil, is a country in South America. It is the world's fifth-largest country by area, behind Russia, Canada, the United States, and China, with a total area of 8,514,877 square kilometers (3,287,612 sq mi).
title: Brazil

text: Colombia officially the Republic of Colombia, is a tropical equatorial country in northern South America. It is in the northwest part of the continent, and it has an area of 1 141 748 km2 (440 839 sq mi).
title: Colombia

text: Australia, officially the Commonwealth of Australia, is an island country and sovereign state located in the southern hemisphere, in Oceania. Its capital city is Canberra, and its largest city is Sydney.
title: Australia

text: Cairo (Arabic: القاهرة, usually transliterated as Al-Qāhirah) is the capital and largest city of Egypt and the Cairo Governorate. The city name can be translated as the one who won.
title: Cairo

text: Cape Town is the second largest city of South Africa. It is also home to the South African Parliament where the country's representatives assemble.
title: Cape Town

text: Kinshasa is the capital city of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (once called Zaire). It is the third largest city in the continent of Africa (after Lagos and Cairo).
title: Kinshasa

text: Lagos is the second largest city in Africa and the most populous city in Nigeria and in West Africa. There are about 12.5 million to 18 million people living in Lagos, which makes it one of the biggest cities in Africa.
title: Lagos

text: Nairobi is the capital and largest city of Kenya. Its name comes from The Masaai word 'Enkare Nyorobi' meaning 'place of cool waters'.
title: Nairobi

text: Baghdad (Arabic: بغداد, transliterated Baghdād) is the capital city and largest city in Iraq. It is the second-largest city in Southwest Asia after Tehran.
title: Baghdad

text: Bangkok (Thai: กรุงเทพมหานคร) is the capital city of Thailand. In 2010, the city had a population of 9,100,000 people.
title: Bangkok

text: Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China. The city used to be known as Peking.
title: Beijing

text: Damascus (Arabic: دمشق) is the capital city of Syria. In Arabic, its name is Dimashq (دمشق).
title: Damascus

text: Dhaka is the capital and largest city of Bangladesh. Dhaka is a megacity, and has a population of 10.2 million residents as of 2022, and a population of over 22.4 million residents in Greater Dhaka.
title: Dhaka

text: The city of Dubai is the largest and most populated city in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and the capital city of the emirate of Dubai, UAE. The city is sometimes called "Dubai City" to prevent it from being mixed up with the emirate.
title: Dubai

text: Jakarta, officially the Special Capital Region of Jakarta (Indonesian: Daerah Khusus Ibukota Jakarta shortened DKI Jakarta), is the largest and the capital city of Indonesia. It is on the northwest coast of the island of Java, it has an area of 661.52 km² and a population of 10,562,088 as of 2020.
title: Jakarta

text: Karachi (Sindhi: ڪراچي), (Urdu: کراچی) is the largest city in Pakistan and the capital of the province of Sindh. Until 1958, it was also the capital of Pakistan.
title: Karachi

text: Kolkata (spelled Calcutta before 1 January 2001) is the capital city of the Indian state of West Bengal. It is the second largest city in India after Mumbai .
title: Kolkata

text: Mecca or Makkah (officially: Makkah al-Mukarramah; Arabic: مكة المكرمة) is a city in Saudi Arabia and the holiest city in Islam. As of the 2004 census, 1,294,169 people lived there.
title: Mecca

text: Mumbai is a natural harbour on the west coast of India, and is the capital city of Maharashtra state.
title: Mumbai

text: Seoul (Korean: 서울) is the biggest city of the Republic of Korea (South Korea), and its capital. Its official name is Seoul Special City (Korean: 서울특별시 Seoul Teukbyeolsi).
title: Seoul

text: Singapore, officially the Republic of Singapore, is a sovereign country. It is nicknamed as 'The Lion City', 'The Garden City' or 'The Little Red Dot'.
title: Singapore

text: Tehran is the capital and largest city of Iran. It is also the capital of Tehran province and the administrative center for Tehran County and its Central District.
title: Tehran

text: This article is about metropolitan Tokyo. For more information, see Tokyo (disambiguation).
title: Tokyo Metropolis

text: Amsterdam is the capital and largest city in the European country of the Netherlands. Amsterdam is famous for its canals.
title: Amsterdam

text: Athens is one of the most famous cities in the world. It is the capital city of Greece and the most important financial, industrial, maritime, political, and cultural center of the country.
title: Athens

text: Brussels (French: Bruxelles, Dutch: Brussel, German: Brüssel) is the capital city of Belgium and the European Union.
title: Brussels

text: Istanbul, formerly known as Constantinople, is a mega city that sits in both Europe and Asia, divided by the Bosporus. Although it is the largest city of Turkey, it is not the capital.
title: Istanbul

text: London is the capital and largest city of both England and its surrounding area.
title: London

text: Madrid (pronounced: “mah-drid or /məˈdrɪd/) is the capital and largest city of Spain. Madrid is in the middle of Spain, in the Community of Madrid.
title: Madrid

text: Paris (nicknamed the "City of light") is the capital city of France, and the largest city in France. The area is 105 square kilometres (41 square miles), and around 2.15 million people live there.
title: Paris

text: Rome (Latin: Roma) is the capital city of Italy. It is also the capital and largest city in the region of Lazio, and the geographical region of Latium.
title: Rome

text: Saint Petersburg (Russian: Санкт-Петербу́рг, romanized: Sankt-Peterburg) is a Russian city in northwestern Russia, near the Gulf of Finland of the Baltic Sea. Over five million people live in St. Petersburg as of 2015, and it is the second biggest city in Russia.
title: Saint Petersburg

text: Los Angeles (L.A.), officially the City of Los Angeles, is the largest city in California, in the United States. There are many ethnicities of people living in the city, and over 18 million people in the Greater Los Angeles region.
title: Los Angeles

text: Mexico City is the capital and largest city of Mexico. It's also the most populous city in North America.
title: Mexico City

text: New York, often called New York City (NYC), is the most populous city in the U.S. state of New York, and the largest city in the United States. It is at the southern end of the U.S. state of New York.
title: New York City

text: Washington, D.C. (also known as simply Washington or D.C., and officially as the District of Columbia) is the capital city of the United States of America. It is a federal district.
title: Washington, D.C.

text: Bogota is the capital city of Colombia. As of 2009, more than 7 million people live in Bogota, which makes it the largest city in Colombia.
title: Bogotá

text: Buenos Aires is the capital and largest city in the South American country of Argentina. It has its own executive, legislative and judicial powers.
title: Buenos Aires

text: Rio de Janeiro is the second largest city in Brazil. It is the capital of the state of Rio de Janeiro.
title: Rio de Janeiro

text: São Paulo (Portuguese for Saint Paul) is the capital of the Brazilian state of the same name. It is the most populous city city in Brazil, South America, and the Southern Hemisphere, and the second-most populous city in the Western Hemisphere, after Mexico City, Mexico.
title: São Paulo

text: Sydney (Dharuk: Gadi, also Warrang) is a city on the east coast of Australia which is the capital city of New South Wales. About five and a half million people live in Sydney which makes it the biggest city in both Australia and Oceania.
title: Sydney

text: The Amazon River (also called Rio Amazonas in Portuguese and Spanish) is the largest river in the world by the amount or volume of water it carries. It flows through the tropical forests of South America, mainly in Brazil.
title: Amazon River

text: The Arctic Ocean is the ocean around the North Pole. The most northern parts of Eurasia and North America are around the Arctic Ocean.
title: Arctic Ocean

text: The Atlantic Ocean is the world's second largest ocean. It covers a total area of about 106,400,000 square kilometres (41,100,000 square miles), about 20 percent of the Earth's surface.
title: Atlantic Ocean

text: The Baltic Sea is a sea in northern Europe between Scandinavia, Finland, Russia, the Baltic countries, Poland, and Germany.
title: Baltic Sea

text: The Black Sea is a sea in Eurasia between Europe, Caucasus, and Anatolia. Many important rivers flow to the Black Sea, including the Don, the Danube, the Dniester and the Dnieper.
title: Black Sea

text: The Caribbean Sea is a tropical sea in the center of the Caribbean area. The body of water is part of the Atlantic Ocean.
title: Caribbean Sea

text: The Caspian Sea is the largest lake on Earth by both area and volume. It has a surface area of 371,000 square kilometres (143,000 square miles).
title: Caspian Sea

text: The Congo River (also known as Zaire River) is the largest river in Africa. Its overall length of 4,700 km (2,922 miles) makes it the second longest in Africa (after the Nile).
title: Congo River

text: The Danube (Latin name Hister) is the second-longest river in Europe (the Volga is the longest). It is the longest river of the European Union.
title: Danube

text: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef stretching over 1,400 miles. It is near the coast of Queensland, Australia.
title: Great Barrier Reef

text: The Great Lakes are five large lakes in east-central North America. They hold 21% of the world's surface fresh water.
title: Great Lakes

text: The Indian Ocean is the world's third-largest ocean, at 73,400,000 square kilometres (28,300,000 sq mi). It is surrounded by Asia to the north, Australia and the Pacific Ocean to the east, the Southern Ocean to the south, and Africa and the Atlantic Ocean to the west.
title: Indian Ocean

text: The Indus River or Indus (from Sanskrit: सिन्धु) is a river in Asia. It flows through Tibet, Kashmir and Pakistan.
title: Indus River

text: Lake Baikal is a huge lake in Siberia, Russia. It is the biggest fresh water reservoir in the world.
title: Lake Baikal

text: Lake Victoria or Victoria Nyanza (also known as Ukerewe and Nnalubaale) is a lake in Africa. It is bordered and governed by the countries of Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.
title: Lake Victoria

text: The Mediterranean Sea is the body of water that separates Europe, Africa and Asia.
title: Mediterranean Sea

text: The Mississippi River is a river in the United States. It is the 11th longest river in the world.
title: Mississippi River

text: The Niger River is the main river of western Africa. It is over 4180 km (2500 miles) long.
title: Niger River

text: The Nile (النيل an-nīl) is a river in Africa. It is the longest river on Earth (estimated as 6,682 km or 4,152 miles), though other rivers carry more water.
title: Nile

text: The North Sea is a sea that is part of the Atlantic Ocean in northern Europe. The North Sea is between Norway and Denmark in the east, Scotland and England in the west, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium and France in the south.
title: North Sea

text: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean and covers one third of the surface of the entire world. The body of water is between Asia and Australia in the west, the Americas in the east, the Southern Ocean to the south, and the Arctic Ocean to the north.
title: Pacific Ocean

text: The Panama Canal is a waterway (a canal) in the country of Panama in Central America, that connects the Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean. Because of the way Panama twists, the entrance to the Pacific Ocean is farther east than the entrance to the Atlantic Ocean.
title: Panama Canal

text: The Rhine River (German: Rhein, French: Rhin, Dutch: Rijn) is 1,230 kilometres (760 mi) long. Its name comes from the Celtic word "renos", which means 'raging flow'.
title: Rhine River

text: The South China Sea is an ocean region in the south of China. It is a marginal sea of the Western Pacific Ocean; a vital area for shipping, fishing, and natural resources, and strategically important for regional security.
title: South China Sea

text: The Suez Canal (Arabic: قناة السويس, Qanā al-Suways, French: Le Canal de Suez) is a canal in Egypt. It lies west of the Sinai Peninsula.
title: Suez Canal

text: The Southern Ocean, also called the Antarctic Ocean, is the ocean around the continent of Antarctica. The fourth-largest sea by area, at 20,327,000 km², it has a coastline 17,968 km long and is surrounded by the waters of the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans.
title: Southern Ocean

text: The Volga is the longest river in Europe. In Russian it is called Волга, in the Tatar language its name is İdel.
title: Volga

text: The Yangtze River, or Yangzi (Simple Chinese: 扬子江 / Traditional Chinese: 揚子江), or Chang Jiang (Simple Chinese: 长江 / Traditional Chinese: 長江), is the longest River in China and Asia, as well as the world's fourth longest river (after the Amazon, the Nile and the Mississippi-Missouri-Jefferson river system).
title: Yangtze River

text: The Yellow River (Huáng Hé 黄河) is the second longest river in China (after Yangtze River) and the sixth longest in the world. The river is 5464 km long and it drains at the Bohai Sea, a gulf of the Yellow Sea.
title: Yellow River

text: The Alps (Italian: Alpi, French: Alpes, German: Alpen, Bavarian: Oipm, Romansh: Alps, Slovene: Alpe, Occitan: Aups, Alps) is the greatest mountain range of Europe. It reaches from Austria and Slovenia in the east; through Italy, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and Germany; to France in the west.
title: Alps

text: The Andes are a mountain range along the western coast of South America.
title: Andes

text: The Himalayas (from Sanskrit हिमालय) are a mountain range located north of the Indian subcontinent.
title: Himalayas

text: Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth. Mount Everest is in the Himalayas, a tall mountain range in Asia.
title: Mount Everest

text: Kilimanjaro (or Kilimanjaro, which means "shining mountain" in Swahili), formerly Kaiser-Wilhelm-Spitze, is a mountain in northeastern Tanzania.
title: Mount Kilimanjaro

text: The Rocky Mountains, often called The Rockies, are a range of mountains in the western United States and Canada. They stretch from the northernmost part of British Columbia, in Western Canada, to New Mexico, in the Southwestern United States.
title: Rocky Mountains

text: The Sahara, in North Africa, is the largest desert in the world except for Antarctica. The Sahara is the largest hot desert.
title: Sahara

text: A capital city, or capital town or capital, is a city or town, specified by law or constitution, by the government of a country, or part of a country, such as a state, province, or county. It usually serves as the location of the government's central meeting place and offices.
title: Capital city

text: A country is a distinct territory with defined borders, boundaries, people and government. Most countries are sovereign states while others make up one part of a larger state.
title: Country

text: Exploration is the act of searching an unfamiliar area in order to learn about it. It involves the discovery of new information.
title: Exploration

text: The border between two regions is a line, where one region is next to the other. If the regions are countries, the border can only be crossed at certain points.
title: Border

text: Rural areas are areas which are not towns or cities. They are often farming or agricultural areas.
title: Rural area

text: A suburb is an area of a town or city, a little away from the downtown (city center), where there are fewer big buildings and mainly houses, schools and shops. Such places are called suburban areas or suburban districts.
title: Suburb

text: A village is a place where people live, normally in the countryside. It is usually larger than a hamlet and smaller than a town or city.
title: Village

text: An atlas is a collection of maps or manifolds, traditionally bound into book form, but also found in multimedia formats.
title: Atlas

text: Contour lines or isolines are used when plotting a function of 2 variables. All the points where the function has the same value are connected.
title: Contour line

text: A geodetic datum is used to locate a given position when using a set of reference, such as a map. That way a set of coordinates might reference an exact location on the map.
title: Geodetic datum

text: A geographical coordinate system is a coordinate system. This means that every place can be specified by three sets of three numbers, called coordinates.
title: Geographic coordinate system

text: The latitude of the Earth gives the distance north or south of the equator. It is measured in degrees.
title: Latitude

text: Longitude is a way to say where a place is on the Earth.
title: Longitude

text: The geoid is a shape like the surface of the Earth. It is a 3-D geometrical shape like an orange.
title: Geoid

text: A globe is most commonly, a scale model of the earth with the shape of a sphere. Globes can be scale models of the Earth (terrestrial globes) or of other planets.
title: Globe

text: A great circle is the largest possible circle that can be drawn on a sphere, one that divides the surface into equal halves, called hemispheres. It is a circle that has the same diameter as the sphere it was drawn on.
title: Great circle

text: A map projection is a way of showing the surface of a three-dimensional sphere on a flat surface. Such projections are necessary to create maps.
title: Map projection

text: The Mercator projection is a cylindrical map projection which is widely used in cartography today. It was developed by Gerardus Mercator in 1569.
title: Mercator projection

text: A reference ellipsoid is an ellipsoid which is used as a frame of reference for geodetic calculations. It is a figure like the shape of the Earth.
title: Reference ellipsoid

text: A map scale is the size of an object compared to the size of the object's smaller representative on a map. This can be shown by a scale bar and a ratio 1:n.
title: Scale (map)

text: Cardinal directions or cardinal points are the four main directions or points of the compass: north, east, south and west. These direction are also written in short form as N, E, S and W.
title: Cardinal direction

text: North is one of the 4 main directions on a compass. North is usually up on most maps.
title: North

text: East is one of the 4 main directions on a compass (called cardinal directions). East is normally to the right on most maps.
title: East

text: South is one of the 4 cardinal directions on a compass. South is normally down on the bottom of most maps.
title: South

text: West is one of the 4 main directions on a compass. West is normally to the left on most maps.
title: West

text: The Antarctic Circle is one of the five major circles of latitude that mark maps of the Earth. It is the parallel of latitude at 66° 33′ 39″ south of the Equator, crossing mostly the Southern Ocean.
title: Antarctic Circle

text: The Arctic Circle is one of the five major circles of latitude (imaginary lines around the Earth) that are often marked on maps of the Earth. This is the parallel of latitude that (in 2000) runs 66° 33' 39" north of the Equator.
title: Arctic Circle

text: On the Earth, a circle of latitude is an imaginary east-west circle that connects all locations with a given latitude. A location's position along a circle of latitude is given by its longitude.
title: Circle of latitude

text: The equator is a line which is not real drawn around a sphere or planet, such as the Earth. It is one of the lines known as a line of latitude, or circle of latitude.
title: Equator

text: A meridian is an imaginary line of longitude drawn along the surface of the earth from the North Pole to the South Pole.
title: Meridian

text: The Tropic of Cancer is one of the five major circles of latitude (imaginary lines around the Earth) that are often marked on maps of the Earth. This is the parallel of latitude that is 23° 26' 22" north of the Equator.
title: Tropic of Cancer

text: The Tropic of Capricorn, or Southern tropic, is one of the five major circles of latitude of a map of the Earth. It is 23° 26′ 22″ south of the Equator.
title: Tropic of Capricorn

text: The Americas (or America) are lands in the Western Hemisphere that are also known as the New World. Comprising the continents of North America and South America, along with their associated islands, they cover 8.3% of the Earth's total surface area (28.4% of its land area).
title: Americas

text: The continent of Australia, sometimes known technically as Sahul, Australia-New Guinea, Australinea, or Meganesia to distinguish it from the country of Australia, is a continent located in the Southern and Eastern hemispheres.
title: Australia (continent)

text: Eurasia is the combined landmass of Europe and Asia in the northern part of Earth. It has the Atlantic Ocean on its west, and the Pacific Ocean to the east.
title: Eurasia

text: Baffin Bay (Inuktitut: Saknirutiak Imanga,) is a marginal sea of the North Atlantic Ocean. It is between Baffin Island and the southwest coast of Greenland.
title: Baffin Bay

text: The Barents Sea is a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean. It is north of Norway and Russia.
title: Barents Sea

text: The Beaufort Sea is a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean, north of the Northwest Territories, the Yukon, and Alaska, west of Canada's Arctic islands. The sea is named after hydrographer Sir Francis Beaufort.
title: Beaufort Sea

text: Chukchi Sea is a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean. It is bounded on the west by the De Long Strait, off Wrangel Island, and in the east by Point Barrow, Alaska, beyond which is the Beaufort Sea.
title: Chukchi Sea

text: The East Siberian Sea is a marginal sea in the Arctic Ocean. It is between the Arctic Cape to the north, the coast of Siberia to the south, the New Siberian Islands to the west and Cape Billings, close to Chukotka, and Wrangel Island to the east.
title: East Siberian Sea

text: The Greenland Sea is a body of water. It borders Greenland to the west, the Svalbard archipelago to the east, Fram Strait and the Arctic Ocean to the north, and the Norwegian Sea and Iceland to the south.
title: Greenland Sea

text: The Hudson Bay is a bay that goes into East-central Canada. It is the fourth largest sea in the world with an area of 316,000 square miles (819,000 square kilometres).
title: Hudson Bay

text: The Kara Sea (Russian: Ка́рское мо́ре) is part of the Arctic Ocean. It lies north of Siberia.
title: Kara Sea

text: The Laptev Sea is a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean. It is between the northern coast of Siberia, the Taimyr Peninsula, Severnaya Zemlya and the New Siberian Islands.
title: Laptev Sea

text: The White Sea is a southern inlet of the Barents Sea. It is on the northwest coast of Russia.
title: White Sea

text: The Gulf of Bothnia is the northernmost arm of the Baltic Sea. It is situated between Finland's west coast and Sweden's east coast.
title: Gulf of Bothnia

text: The Bay of Biscay is a gulf of the northeast Atlantic Ocean south of the Celtic Sea. It is along the western coast of France from Brest south to the Spanish border, and the northern coast of Spain west to Cape Ortegal.
title: Bay of Biscay

text: The Gulf of Guinea is off West Africa. It is in the northeast of the tropical Atlantic Ocean.
title: Gulf of Guinea

text: The Irish Sea (sometimes called the Manx Sea) is a body of water that separates Ireland and Great Britain. It is known to be one of the most polluted seas in the world including the North Sea and the Mediterranean Sea.
title: Irish Sea

text: The Labrador Sea (French: mer du Labrador) is an arm of the North Atlantic Ocean between the Labrador Peninsula and Greenland. The sea is surrounded by continental shelves to the southwest, northwest, and northeast.
title: Labrador Sea

text: The Norwegian Sea is a marginal sea in the North Atlantic Ocean, northwest of Norway. It is between the North Sea and the Greenland Sea.
title: Norwegian Sea

text: The Sargasso Sea is a region in the gyre in the middle of the North Atlantic Ocean. It is bounded on the west by the Gulf Stream; on the north, by the North Atlantic Current; on the east, by the Canary Current; and on the south, by the North Atlantic Equatorial Current.
title: Sargasso Sea

text: The Sea of Azov (Russian: Азо́вское мо́ре - Azovskoye more; Ukrainian: Озівськe or Азо́вське мо́ре - Ozivs'ke or Azovs'ke more) is the world's shallowest sea, linked by the Strait of Kerch to the Black Sea to the south.
title: Sea of Azov

text: The Gulf of Mexico is an ocean basin or bay of the Atlantic Ocean that is a marginal sea of North America. The United States, Mexico, and Cuba are the countries around it.
title: Gulf of Mexico

text: The Gulf of Saint Lawrence (French: golfe du Saint-Laurent) is the outlet of North America's Great Lakes via the Saint Lawrence River into the Atlantic Ocean. It is the world's largest estuary.
title: Gulf of Saint Lawrence

text: The Adriatic Sea is a body of water and is a part of the Mediterranean Sea. The Italian Peninsula from the Balkan Peninsula was separated by the sea.
title: Adriatic Sea

text: The Aegean Sea, part of the Mediterranean Sea, is between Greece and Anatolia. It is connected in the north to the Sea of Marmara and the Black Sea by the Dardanelles and Bosporus.
title: Aegean Sea

text: The Ionian Sea is an arm of the Mediterranean Sea, south of the Adriatic Sea. It is bordered by southern Italy including Calabria, Sicily and the Salento peninsula to the west, and by southwestern Albania.
title: Ionian Sea

text: The Ligurian Sea is an arm of the Mediterranean Sea. It is between the Italian Riviera (Liguria and Tuscany) and the island of Corsica.
title: Ligurian Sea

text: The Sea of Marmara, also known as the Sea of Marmora or the Marmara Sea, is the inland sea that connects the Black Sea to the Aegean Sea and separates Turkey's Asian and European parts. The Bosphorus is a strait that connects it to the Black Sea and the Dardanelles to the Aegean.
title: Sea of Marmara

text: The Tyrrhenian Sea (Italian: Mar Tirreno) is part of the Mediterranean Sea.
title: Tyrrhenian Sea

text: The Andaman Sea or Burma Sea is a body of water to the southeast of the Bay of Bengal. It is south of Burma, west of Thailand and east of the Andaman Islands, India.
title: Andaman Sea

text: The Arabian Sea is the northwest part of the Indian Ocean. To its west are the Guardafui Channel, Somali Sea and the Arabian Peninsula.
title: Arabian Sea

text: The Bay of Bengal is a bay in the northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, west of the Malay Peninsula and east of India. It looks like a triangle.
title: Bay of Bengal

text: The Persian Gulf is the name of a geographical place. Its location is in the Middle East.
title: Persian Gulf

text: The Red Sea is a sea between the Arabian Peninsula of Asia in the northeast and Africa in the southwest. It is a part of the Indian Ocean.
title: Red Sea

text: The Timor Sea is a relatively shallow sea. It is bounded to the north by the island of Timor, to the east by the Arafura Sea, to the south by Australia and to the west by the Indian Ocean.
title: Timor Sea

text: The Arafura Sea is west of the Pacific Ocean. It overlys the continental shelf between Australia and New Guinea.
title: Arafura Sea

text: The Bering Sea is a marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean. It has a deep water basin, which then rises through a narrow slope into the shallower water above the continental shelves.
title: Bering Sea

text: The Celebes Sea is a sea of the western Pacific Ocean. It is bordered on the north by the Sulu Archipelago and Sulu Sea and Mindanao Island of the Philippines.
title: Celebes Sea

text: The Coral Sea is a small sea off the north east coast of Australia. It has Queensland on its west side and the islands of Vanuatu and New Caledonia on its east.
title: Coral Sea

text: The East China Sea is a marginal sea east of China. It is a part of the Pacific Ocean and covers an area of 1,249,000 km².
title: East China Sea

text: The Flores Sea covers 93,000 square miles (240,000 square kilometres) of water in Indonesia.
title: Flores Sea

text: The Gulf of Alaska is an arm of the Pacific Ocean. The borders are the southern coast of Alaska, stretching from the Alaska Peninsula (Kabuch Point) and Kodiak Island in the west to the Cape Spencer in the east, south of which Glacier Bay and the Inside Passage are found.
title: Gulf of Alaska

text: The Gulf of California (also called Sea of Cortez or Sea of Cortés; and nearby is known in the Spanish language as Mar de Cortés or Mar Bermejo or Golfo de California) is an area of water that is in between the Baja California Peninsula and Mexican mainland.
title: Gulf of California

text: The Gulf of Carpentaria (14°00′S 139°00′E) is a large, shallow sea surrounded on three sides by northern Australia. Its north edge is the Arafura Sea; the sea between Australia and New Guinea.
title: Gulf of Carpentaria

text: The Gulf of Thailand is a shallow arm of the South China Sea.
title: Gulf of Thailand

text: The Java Sea is a large shallow sea on the Sunda Shelf. It is 320,000 km².
title: Java Sea

text: The Molucca Sea is in the western Pacific Ocean, within the country of Indonesia. The region is rich in coral and has many diving sites.
title: Molucca Sea

text: The Philippine Sea is the body of water east of the Philippines and Taiwan. It is a part of the western end of the Pacific Ocean.
title: Philippine Sea

text: The Sea of Japan is a sea in the western Pacific Ocean. It is bordered by Korea to the west, Russia to the north and Japan to the east and south.
title: Sea of Japan

text: The Sea of Okhotsk is a marginal sea of the western Pacific Ocean.
title: Sea of Okhotsk

text: The Solomon Sea is a sea in the Pacific Ocean. It is between Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands.
title: Solomon Sea

text: Sulu Sea has a number of islands. The Cuyo Islands and Cagayan Sulu are part of the province of Palawan while Mapun and the Turtle Islands are part of the province of Tawi-Tawi.
title: Sulu Sea

text: The Tasman Sea is the sea between Australia and New Zealand. It was named after Dutch explorer Abel Tasman.
title: Tasman Sea

text: The Yellow Sea is the northern part of the East China Sea. It is between Mainland China and the Korean peninsula.
title: Yellow Sea

text: The Amundsen Sea is an arm of the Southern Ocean off Marie Byrd Land in western Antarctica. It is bounded by Cape Flying Fish, the northwestern tip of Thurston Island to the east and Cape Dart on Siple Island to the west.
title: Amundsen Sea

text: The Great Australian Bight is a large bight, or open bay. It is off the central and western parts of the southern coastline of mainland Australia.
title: Great Australian Bight

text: The Ross Sea is a deep bay of the Southern Ocean in Antarctica between Victoria Land and Marie Byrd Land.
title: Ross Sea

text: The Scotia Sea is partly in the Southern Ocean and mostly in the South Atlantic Ocean.
title: Scotia Sea

text: The Weddell Sea is part of the Southern Ocean and has the Weddell Gyre. The easternmost point is Cape Norvegia at Princess Martha Coast, Queen Maud Land.
title: Weddell Sea

text: The Bab-el-Mandeb, meaning "Gate of Tears" in Arabic, is a strait between Yemen on the Arabian Peninsula, Djibouti and Eritrea, north of Somalia, in the Horn of Africa, and connecting the Red Sea to the Guardafui Channel and Gulf of Aden. It is sometimes called the Mandab Strait in the English language.
title: Bab-el-Mandeb

text: Bass Strait is a sea strait separating Tasmania from the south of the Australian mainland, specifically the state of Victoria. The strait was named after George Bass who travelled it in 1798.
title: Bass Strait

text: The Bering Strait (Russian: Берингов пролив) is a sea strait between Cape Dezhnev, Russia, the easternmost point (169°43' W) of the Asian continent and Cape Prince of Wales on the edge of the Seward Peninsula, Alaska, the westernmost point (168°05' W) of the North American continent, with latitude of about 65° 40' north, slightly south of the Arctic Circle.
title: Bering Strait

text: The Bosporus or Bosphorus (Turkish: İstanbul Boğazı, lit. 'Istanbul strait') is a strait which is straddled by the city of Istanbul that forms part of the boundary between the European part of Turkey and its Asian part (Anatolia).
title: Bosporus

text: Cook Strait (Māori: Te Moana-o-Raukawa) is the body of water between the North and South Islands of New Zealand. It connects the Tasman Sea on the west with the South Pacific Ocean on the east.
title: Cook Strait

text: Davis Strait is a northern arm of the Labrador Sea. It is between mid-western Greenland and Nunavut, Canada's Baffin Island.
title: Davis Strait

text: The Denmark Strait or Greenland Strait is an oceanic strait between Greenland (to its northwest) and Iceland (to its southeast). The Norwegian island of Jan Mayen is northeast of the strait.
title: Denmark Strait

text: The Dardanelles is the narrow strait in northwestern Turkey that connects the Aegean Sea to the Sea of Marmara. It marks the division between Asia, to the east, and Europe, to the west.
title: Dardanelles

text: The Strait of Dover or Dover Strait is the strait at the narrowest part of the English Channel.
title: Strait of Dover

text: The Drake passage is a body of water. It lies between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
title: Drake Passage

text: The English Channel is a body of water that separates the island of Great Britain from the rest of Europe.
title: English Channel

text: The Straits of Florida (or Florida Straits) is a strait between the Florida Keys and Cuba. It connects the Gulf of Mexico to the Atlantic Ocean.
title: Straits of Florida

text: The Strait of Gibraltar is the only water passage between the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea. It is between Europe and Africa; on one side is the southern tip of Spain and Gibraltar, and on the other is northern Morocco and Ceuta.
title: Strait of Gibraltar

text: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow, strategically important strait between the Gulf of Oman in the southeast and the Persian Gulf. On the north coast is Iran and on the south coast is the United Arab Emirates and Musandam, an exclave of Oman.
title: Strait of Hormuz

text: Hudson Strait links the Atlantic Ocean to Hudson Bay in Canada. It is between Baffin Island and the northern coast of Quebec.
title: Hudson Strait

text: Kattegat is a sea in the northern part of Europe between the Danish peninsula Jutland, the Danish island Zealand, and the western coast of Sweden.
title: Kattegat

text: The Korea Strait (Korean: 대한해협, Daehan Haehyeop), also known as the Tsushima Strait, is a narrow body of water between Japan and South Korea. The name is used in two ways.
title: Korea Strait

text: The Strait of Magellan is a passageway from the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific. It is just south of mainland South America and north of Tierra del Fuego.
title: Strait of Magellan

text: The Strait of Malacca is a marine strait. It links the Andaman Sea and the Java Sea, and separates Malaya and Sumatra.
title: Strait of Malacca

text: The Mozambique Channel is a part of the Indian Ocean. Its between the Somali Sea to the north, the island nation of Madagascar in the east, and Mozambique in the west.
title: Mozambique Channel

text: The Strait of Otranto connects the Adriatic Sea with the Ionian Sea. It separates Italy from Albania.
title: Strait of Otranto

text: Palk Strait is a strait between the Tamil Nadu state of India and the Mannar district of the Northern Province of Sri Lanka. It connects the Bay of Bengal in the northeast with the Palk Bay and then with the Gulf of Mannar in the southwest.
title: Palk Strait

text: Skagerrak is a sea in the northern part of Europe between Norway and Denmark. Skagerrak is a part of the North Sea.
title: Skagerrak

text: Sunda Strait is the strait that is between the islands of Java and Sumatra in Indonesia.
title: Sunda Strait

text: The Taiwan Strait or Formosa Strait is a 180 km-wide strait between mainland China and the island of Taiwan. The strait is part of the South China Sea and attaches to East China Sea to the northeast.
title: Taiwan Strait

text: Torres Strait is the narrow sea between Australia's Cape York and New Guinea. It is about 150 km (93 mi) wide and filled with islands, coral reefs and sand banks.
title: Torres Strait

text: The Tsugaru Strait (津軽海峡, Tsugaru Kaikyō) is a channel that is between the islands of Honshu and Hokkaido in northern Japan. It connects the Sea of Japan with the Pacific Ocean.
title: Tsugaru Strait

text: The Yucatán Channel is a strait between Mexico and Cuba. It is also called the Straits of Yucatán.
title: Yucatán Channel

text: Øresund or Öresund, also known as "the Sound" in English, is a strait that acts as the border between Denmark's Zealand and Sweden's Scania. It's about 118 kilometers long and varies in width from 4 to 28 kilometers.
title: Øresund

text: The Kasai River (called Cassai in Angola) is a river in central Africa. The river begins in Angola.
title: Kasai River

text: The Ubangi River, also spelled Oubangui, is a river of Central Africa. It is the largest right-bank tributary of the Congo River.
title: Ubangi River

text: The Limpopo River is a river in Africa. It goes through the countries of South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, and Mozambique and forms part of the border of South Africa.
title: Limpopo River

text: The Benue River is a river in Africa. It is the major tributary of the Niger River.
title: Benue River

text: The Blue Nile is one of the main tributaries of the River Nile. Both the Blue Nile and the White Nile form what is known as Nile near Khartoum.
title: Blue Nile

text: The Orange River (officially called Oranje) is a river in Southern Africa. It is 2,160 kilometres (1,340 mi) long.
title: Orange River

text: The Senegal River is a river in West Africa. It is 1,800 km long and is the border between Senegal and Mauritania.
title: Senegal River

text: The Zambezi River is the fourth largest river in Africa. It is also the largest river that enters the Indian Ocean.
title: Zambezi River

text: The Colorado River is a river in the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. It is approximately 1,450 miles (2,330 km) long.
title: Colorado River

text: The Columbia River is a river in British Columbia, Canada, and the U.S. states of Washington and Oregon. The Columbia River is about 1,243 miles long.
title: Columbia River

text: The Mackenzie River is a major river in northern Canada. It is named after famous explorer, Alexander Mackenzie.
title: Mackenzie River

text: The Missouri River is a river in the western United States. It is a tributary of the Mississippi River.
title: Missouri River

text: The Ohio River is one of the most important tributaries to the Mississippi River. It is 981 miles long and it forms boundaries for the states of Ohio, Kentucky, Illinois, Indiana, and West Virginia before finally going to its headwaters in Pennsylvania.
title: Ohio River

text: The Río Grande, or Río Bravo (del Norte), is a river in the United States and Mexico. The name "Río Grande" means "great river" in Spanish.
title: Rio Grande

text: The Saint Lawrence River (French: fleuve Saint-Laurent; Tuscarora: Kahnawáʼkye; Mohawk: Kaniatarowanenneh, meaning "big waterway") is a big river in eastern North America. It flows between the Canadian province of Quebec & Ontario and the American state of New York, and through the major Canadian city of Montreal.
title: Saint Lawrence River

text: The Yukon River is a river in northwestern North America. It starts in British Columbia, continues through the Yukon Territory, and ends in Alaska.
title: Yukon River

text: The Madeira River (Portugese: Rio Madeira) is a river in Brazil. It is also a tributary which flows in Bolivia.
title: Madeira River

text: The Rio Negro is a river which flows through the Amazon rainforest in north-western Brazil, in the state of Amazonas.
title: Rio Negro (Amazon)

text: The Tocantins River is a river that flows through the northeastern part of Brazil. It rises in the district with a lot of mountains known as the Pireneus.
title: Tocantins River

text: The Magdalena River is the most important river in the western part of Colombia. It has a length of 1,538 kilometres (956 mi).
title: Magdalena River

text: The Orinoco is a main river in northern South America. It is one of the longest rivers in South America, at 2,140 kilometres (1,330 miles).
title: Orinoco

text: The Paraná River is a river in south Central South America. It goes through Brazil, Paraguay and Argentina.
title: Paraná River

text: The Uruguay River is a river in South America. It goes through the countries of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay.
title: Uruguay River

text: The São Francisco River is a river in Brazil. It is around 3,100 kilometers long.
title: São Francisco River

text: The Mekong River is a river in southeast Asia. It flows through many countries: China, Burma, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, and finally Vietnam.
title: Mekong River

text: The Lena River is a river in Siberia, flowing into the Arctic Ocean. With a length of 4,472 km (2,779 mi), it is the tenth longest river in the world.
title: Lena River

text: The Yenisei (Енисе́й) is a river in Siberia. It belongs to the greatest river system that flows into the Arctic Ocean.
title: Yenisei

text: The Angara is a river in Siberia, Russia, close to the Jenissei. It is nearly 1,779 kilometres (1,105 miles) long.
title: Angara River

text: The Ob is a river in Siberia. Together with the Lena and the Yenisei, it is one of the most important rivers of Siberia.
title: Ob (river)

text: The Irtysh River (Russian: Иртыш; Kazakh: Ertis / Ертiс; Chinese: 额尔齐斯河 / É'ěrqísī hé; Mongolian: Эрчис мөрөн, "Twirl"; Tatar: Cyrillic Иртеш, Latin İrteş) is a river in Siberia and Kazakhstan. It is the main tributary of the Ob River.
title: Irtysh River

text: The Brahmaputra ( son of brahma ), also called Tsangpo in Tibet, is one of the main rivers in Asia. It has its origin in the Himalayas of Tibet.
title: Brahmaputra River

text: The Amur River is a river extending from northeastern China to the Russian Far East. It is the tenth longest river in the world.
title: Amur River

text: The Songhua River is one of the main rivers in China. It is about 1,434 kilometres (891 mi) long.
title: Songhua River

text: The Euphrates is the western of the two rivers that define the borders of Mesopotamia. The other is the Tigris, which joins the Euphrates to form the Shatt-al-Arab and flow into the Persian Gulf.
title: Euphrates

text: The Amu Darya (Persian: آمودریا, Āmūdaryā; Arabic: جيحون, Jihôn or Jayhoun; Hebrew: גּוֹזָן, Gozan ), also called Oxus and Amu River, is a major river in Central Asia. It is formed by the junction of the Vakhsh and Panj.
title: Amu Darya

text: The Yamuna (Sanskrit: यमुना), sometimes called Jamuna (Hindi: जमुना, Urdu: جمنا) or Jumna, is a major river in North India. It is the largest branch of a bigger river called the Ganges.
title: Yamuna

text: Salween River is a major river in Southeast Asia. It flows through parts of China, Thailand, and Burma for 2,815 kilometres (1,749 miles).
title: Salween River

text: The Ural River is a river in the European country of Russia. It is 1,509 miles (2,428 kilometers) long.
title: Ural (river)

text: The Syr Darya is a river in Central Asia. Its name, which comes from Persian, means Syr Sea or Syr River.
title: Syr Darya

text: The Irrawaddy River or Ayeyarwady River is a river that flows from north to south through Myanmar. It is the country's largest river and most important commercial waterway.
title: Irrawaddy River

text: The Kolyma River is a river in northeastern Siberia, Russia. It flows through parts of the Sakha Republic, Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, and Magadan Oblast.
title: Kolyma River

text: Pearl River is the name of a river in southern China. The river flows into the South China Sea near Macau.
title: Pearl River (China)

text: The Tigris is a river in the Middle East. It is the eastern of two rivers that define Mesopotamia.
title: Tigris

text: Indigirka River (Russian: Индиги́рка; Yakut: Индигиир) is a significant river in the Sakha Republic (Yakutia) in the Russian Far East. It is one of the major rivers in northeastern Siberia.
title: Indigirka River

text: The Godavari, also known as Dakshina Ganga, is the second longest river in India which flows for 1,465 kilometers and covers about 10% of India's total area. It originates in Trimbakeshwar, Nashik, Maharashtra, and flows through several states, ultimately emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
title: Godavari River

text: The Krishna River is the fifth longest river in India. It is 1,300 kilometres (810 miles) long.
title: Krishna River

text: The Liao River (simplified Chinese: 辽河; traditional Chinese: 遼河; pinyin: Liáo Hé) is the biggest river in northeastern China (Manchuria). It has a length of 1,390 kilometres (860 mi).
title: Liao River

text: The Dnipro River is one of the major rivers in Europe. It flows from Russia, through Belarus and Ukraine, to the Black Sea.
title: Dnieper

text: The Don (Дон) is one of the major rivers of Russia. It starts in the town of Novomoskovsk 60 km southeast from Tula, southeast of Moscow, and flows for a distance of about 1,870 km (1,162 miles) to the Sea of Azov.
title: Don (river)

text: The Pechora is a river in northern Russia. It is over 1,800 kilometres (1,100 mi) long, and navigable for most of its length.
title: Pechora River

text: The Vistula (Polish: Wisła) is the longest river in Poland. It is 1,047 km (678 miles) long.
title: Vistula

text: The Daugava (Latgalian: Daugova) or Western Dvina is a river rising in the Valdai Hills, Russia, flowing through Russia, Belarus, and Latvia and into the Gulf of Riga. The total length of the river is 1,020 km (630 mi): 325 km (202 mi) in Russia, 338 km (210 mi) in Belarus, and 352 km (219 mi) in Latvia.
title: Daugava

text: The Loire River is the longest river in France. It is 1,006 km long.
title: Loire River

text: The Oder River (German: Oder; Czech/Polish: Odra) is a river in Central Europe. It starts in the Czech Republic and flows through Poland and Germany.
title: Oder

text: The Murray River is the longest river in Australia, about 2,508 km (1,558 mi). It starts high in the Snowy Mountains and flows mainly west.
title: Murray River

text: The African Great Lakes (Swahili: Maziwa Makuu) are a series of lakes making up the part of the Rift Valley lakes in and around the East African Rift. It is bordered by Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi and Tanzania.
title: African Great Lakes

text: Lake Tanganyika is a large lake in the Great Rift Valley of central Africa. The lake is divided between four countries – Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Tanzania and Zambia.
title: Lake Tanganyika

text: Lake Malawi (or Lake Nyasa, Lake Niassa) is a lake in Africa. It is the southernmost lake in the East African Rift system.
title: Lake Malawi

text: Lake Turkana, formerly known as Lake Rudolf, is a lake in the Great Rift Valley in northwest Kenya. Its far northern end crosses into Ethiopia.
title: Lake Turkana

text: Lake Albert, or Albert Nyanza, is a lake in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is one of the African Great Lakes.
title: Lake Albert (Africa)

text: Lake Mweru is a freshwater lake on the Congo River. It is on the border between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia.
title: Lake Mweru

text: Lake Chad is a large, shallow, endorheic lake in the African Sahel. It has varied in size over the centuries.
title: Lake Chad

text: Lake Superior is a lake in Canada and the United States.
title: Lake Superior

text: Lake Michigan is one of the five Great Lakes in North America. It has a surface area of 22,300 sq mi (58,000 km2).
title: Lake Michigan

text: Lake Huron is one of North America's five Great Lakes. It is the third one up from the mouth.
title: Lake Huron

text: Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes in North America. It is the second to the last in the Great Lake system before water flows into the St. Lawrence River.
title: Lake Erie

text: Lake Ontario (French: Lac Ontario) is the smallest of the Great Lakes in North America, but its maximum depth (802ft; 244m) is deeper than lake Erie's (210ft) and Lake Huron's (750ft).
title: Lake Ontario

text: Great Bear Lake is a lake in the Northwest Territories, Canada. It is the largest lake that is entirely inside Canada.
title: Great Bear Lake

text: Great Slave Lake (French: Grand lac des Esclaves) is the second-largest lake in the Northwest Territories of Canada. It is the deepest lake in North America at 614m, and the ninth-largest lake in the world.
title: Great Slave Lake

text: Lake Winnipeg is a big lake in the province of Manitoba, Canada. It is north of the city of Winnipeg.
title: Lake Winnipeg

text: Lake Nicaragua is the biggest lake in Central America. It lies in the south of Nicaragua, close to the border with Costa Rica.
title: Lake Nicaragua

text: Lake Maracaibo (Spanish: Lago de Maracaibo) is a large brackish tidal bay (or tidal estuary) in Venezuela. It is an "inlet of the Caribbean Sea".
title: Lake Maracaibo

text: Lake Titicaca (Quechua: Titiqaqa Qucha, "Titiqaqa Lake") is a large, deep lake in the Andes mountains. The eastern part is in Bolivia and the western part of it is in Peru.
title: Lake Titicaca

text: Lake Vostok is the biggest of the seventy lakes in Antarctica that are under sheets of ice. It is at 77° S 105° E. It is under Russia's Vostok Station.
title: Lake Vostok

text: Lake Balkhash (Kazakh: Балқаш Көлі, Balqash kóli) is located in Kazakhstan. It is one of the largest lakes in Asia and 15th largest in the world (en).
title: Lake Balqash

text: Issyk-Kul (also Ysyk-Köl, Kyrgyz: Ысык-Көл, romanized: Ysyk-Köl, lit. 'warm lake' is an endorheic saline lake in the western Tianshan Mountains in eastern Kyrgyzstan.
title: Issyk-Kul

text: Lake Urmia (Persian: دریاچه ارومیه) is a salt lake in northwest of Iran. It is in the provinces of East Azarbaijan and West Azarbaijan, and is southwest of the close shaped Caspian Sea.
title: Lake Urmia

text: Lake Van (Turkish: Van Gölü, Armenian: Վանա լիճ, Kurdish: Gola Wanê) is the largest lake in Turkey, in the far east of the country.
title: Lake Van

text: The Qinghai Lake, or Ch'inghai Lake, is the largest lake in China. It is in the Qinghai Province, which is where the lake gets its name.
title: Qinghai Lake

text: Poyang Lake is the largest freshwater lake in China. It is in the Jiangxi Province.
title: Poyang Lake

text: The Aral Sea (Kazakh: Арал теңізі (Aral tengizi), Uzbek: Orol dengizi, Russian: Аральскοе мοре) was a lake in Central Asia. It is between Kazakhstan in the north and Karakalpakstan, an autonomous region of Uzbekistan, in the south.
title: Aral Sea

text: The Dead Sea is a lake in the southwest of Asia. It is the Earth's lowest surface, located 420 meters (1,380 feet) below sea level.
title: Dead Sea

text: Lake Ladoga (Russian: Ладожское, Finnish: Laatokka) is a very large lake in Russia. It is the largest lake in Europe and one of the 20 largest lakes on Earth.
title: Lake Ladoga

text: Vänern is a lake in southern Sweden. It is the largest lake in Sweden.
title: Vänern

text: Saimaa is the largest lake in Finland. It covers 4,380 square kilometres (1,690 sq mi).
title: Saimaa

text: Lake Peipus (Estonian: Peipsi-Pihkva järv, German: Peipussee, Russian: Чудско-Псковское озеро) is a large fresh water lake. It is between Estonia and Russia in Northern Europe.
title: Lake Peipus

text: Lake Eyre (pronounced "air") is the lowest point in Australia, at about 15 m (49 ft) below sea level. When it fills with water, it is the largest lake in Australia, being 144 km (89 mi) long and 77 km (48 mi) wide.
title: Lake Eyre

text: The Erie Canal is a canal in New York State. It runs for 365 miles from the Hudson River to Lake Erie.
title: Erie Canal

text: The Canary Islands are an autonomous community of Spain located off the coast of Africa. Consisting of seven main islands and over 50 smaller islands and islets, this region has a volcanic origin which can be appreciated in every one of them, especially in Tenerife, where we can find El Teide.
title: Canary Islands

text: The Mascarene Islands, (French: Mascareignes) or Mascarenes, is a group of islands in the Indian Ocean east of Madagascar.
title: Mascarene Islands

text: The Zanzibar Archipelago (Funguvisiwa la Zanzibar, in Swahili, Arabic: أرخبيل زنجبار) is a group of islands off the coast of Tanzania in the sea of Zanj. The archipelago is also named the Spice Islands.
title: Zanzibar Archipelago

text: The islands of the Caribbean Sea, collectively known as the West Indies are sorted by size and location into the Bahamas (or Lucayan archipelago), the Lesser Antilles and the Greater Antilles.
title: Greater Antilles

text: Hispaniola is an island in the Caribbean Sea. It is the second largest island (after Cuba) of the West Indies, east of Cuba and west of Puerto Rico.
title: Hispaniola

text: The Lesser Antilles (also known as the Caribbees) are a group of islands between the eastern edge of the Caribbean Sea and the western Atlantic Ocean. They are east and south of the Greater Antilles.
title: Lesser Antilles

text: Greenland is the world's largest island. Greenland is a self-governing territory of the kingdom of Denmark.
title: Greenland

text: The Canadian Arctic Archipelago, also known as just the Arctic Archipelago, is an archipelago north of the Canadian mainland in the Arctic. There are about 36,563 islands which have much of the territory of Northern Canada – most of Nunavut and part of Northwest Territories.
title: Canadian Arctic Archipelago

text: The Queen Elizabeth Islands are a group of islands in the Canadian Arctic Archipelago. They are split between Nunavut and Northwest Territories.
title: Queen Elizabeth Islands

text: Ellesmere Island is part of the Qikiqtaaluk Region of the Canadian territory of Nunavut.
title: Ellesmere Island

text: Banks Island (73°0′N 121°30′W) is one of the bigger members of the Canadian Arctic Archipelago. It is in the Inuvik Region of the Northwest Territories, Canada.
title: Banks Island

text: Baffin Island (French: Île de Baffin) is an island in the territory of Nunavut near the Arctic Circle. It is the largest member of the Canadian Arctic Archipelago.
title: Baffin Island

text: Victoria Island is an island in the Canadian Arctic Archipelago and the border between Nunavut and the Northwest Territories runs through the island.
title: Victoria Island

text: Axel Heiberg Island is the 31st biggest island in the world and Canada's 7th biggest island. According to Statistics Canada, it has an area of 43 178 km² (16,671 square miles).
title: Axel Heiberg Island

text: Melville Island is a member of the Canadian Arctic Archipelago, Canada with an area of 42,149 km2 (16,274 sq mi). No one lives on Melville Island.
title: Melville Island (Canada)

text: Southampton Island is one of the bigger members of the Canadian Arctic Archipelago. It is a big island at the entrance to Hudson Bay, Canada.
title: Southampton Island

text: Prince of Wales Island one of the bigger members of the Canadian Arctic Archipelago. It is an Arctic island in Nunavut, Canada, between Victoria Island and Somerset Island and south of the Queen Elizabeth Islands.
title: Prince of Wales Island (Nunavut)

text: Newfoundland is an island off the east Coast of North America, and is part of the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador. The capital city of Newfoundland is St. John's, on the north-east part of the island.
title: Newfoundland

text: Vancouver Island is an island that is part of the province of British Columbia, Canada. Its area is 31,285 square kilometres (12,079 sq mi).
title: Vancouver Island

text: Easter Island is a Polynesian island in the southeastern Pacific Ocean. The capital city of Easter Island is Hanga Roa.
title: Easter Island

text: The Galápago Islands (Archipiélago de Colón in Spanish) are a group of islands in the Pacific Ocean which now belong to Ecuador.
title: Galápagos Islands

text: Tierra del Fuego is an archipelago at the southern tip of South America. The Magellan Strait sepearates it from the South American Mainland.
title: Tierra del Fuego

text: Marajó is an island in Brazil at the mouth of the Amazon River. It is part of the state of Pará.
title: Marajó

text: The Falkland Islands (Spanish: Islas Malvinas) are a group of islands in the South Atlantic Ocean, off the coast of South America. They are an overseas territory of the United Kingdom.
title: Falkland Islands

text: The Malay Archipelago or Nusantara Archipelago refers to the archipelago between mainland Southeastern Asia and Australia.
title: Malay Archipelago

text: The Maluku Islands (also called the Moluccas, Moluccan Islands or simply Maluku) are an archipelago in Indonesia. They are part of the larger Malay Archipelago.
title: Maluku Islands

text: Luzon is an major island in the Philippines. It is situated at northern portion of the country.
title: Luzon

text: Mindanao is one of the three main island groups in the Philippines. It is the southernmost major island of the Philippines, and is the only island in the Philippines are predominantly Muslim people.
title: Mindanao

text: The Sunda Islands are part of the Malay archipelago. They are divided into the Greater Sunda Islands and the Lesser Sunda Islands.
title: Sunda Islands

text: Borneo is the third largest island in the world. It is in the center of maritime southeast Asia.
title: Borneo

text: Sumatra, known also as Sumatera, is the sixth largest island in the world. It is in western Indonesia.
title: Sumatra

text: Sulawesi (formerly known as Celebes) is one of the four larger Sunda Islands of Indonesia, and is between Borneo and the Maluku Islands.
title: Sulawesi

text: Java (Indonesian: Jawa) is one of the Sunda Islands of Indonesia.
title: Java

text: The Lesser Sunda Islands (or Nusa Tenggara) are a group of islands in southern Southeast Asia, north of Australia. Together with the Greater Sunda Islands to the west they make up the Sunda Islands.
title: Lesser Sunda Islands

text: Timor is an island at the south end of the Malay Archipelago, north of the Timor Sea. It is divided between the independent state of East Timor, and West Timor, belonging to the Indonesian province of East Nusa Tenggara.
title: Timor

text: Hokkaidō (北海道, Hokkaidō), also known as Ezo and Yezo, is a volcanic island in Japan. It is the northernmost of Japan's four main islands.
title: Hokkaidō

text: Severnaya Zemlya is an group of islands of about 30 islands in the Arctic Ocean. The islands were known as Emperor Nicholas II Land.
title: Severnaya Zemlya

text: The New Siberian Islands (Novosibirskiye Ostrova) are an archipelago on the northern Arctic. They are to the extreme North of Russia.
title: New Siberian Islands

text: Shikoku しこく (四国) is the smallest of Japan's four main islands. About 4 million people live there, fewer than on any of the other main islands.
title: Shikoku

text: Taiwan is a medium-sized chain of islands in East Asia at 23°30" N, 121°00" E . It runs through the Tropic of Cancer.
title: Geography of Taiwan

text: The British Isles are an archipelago (a group of islands) in north-western Europe. They have a long geographical and geological history.
title: British Isles

text: Great Britain is an island in the north-west Atlantic Ocean, one of the British Isles. It is the biggest European island, off the coast of Continental Europe.
title: Great Britain

text: Novaya Zemlya (Russian: Но́вая Земля́) is an archipelago in the Arctic Ocean in the north of Russia and the extreme northeast of Europe. The archipelago is made of a north island and a south island; it separates the Barents Sea from the Kara Sea.
title: Novaya Zemlya

text: Spitsbergen (which is also spelled Spitzbergen) is the largest island of the archipelago Svalbard. It was called West Spitsbergen until 1965.
title: Spitsbergen

text: Sardinia (Italian: Sardegna, Sardinian: Sardigna) is the second largest island in the Mediterranean Sea. It is an autonomous region of Italy.
title: Sardinia

text: Franz Josef Land is an archipelago, north of Novaya Zemlya in the Arctic Ocean. It is part of Russia.
title: Franz Josef Land

text: Corsica is an island in the Mediterranean Sea. It is west of Tuscany, southeast of France, south of Liguria and north of the island of Sardinia.
title: Corsica

text: Zealand (Danish: Sjælland) is an island in the eastern part of Denmark. It is just west of Sweden and a strait called the Øresund lies between the two.
title: Zealand

text: New Britain is the largest island in the Bismarck Archipelago of Papua New Guinea. It was named for Otto von Bismarck.
title: New Britain

text: New Guinea is a big island north of Australia. It is the second largest island in the world.
title: New Guinea

text: The North Island is the smaller of the two main islands of New Zealand. It is separated from the South Island by Cook Strait.
title: North Island

text: The South Island is the larger of the two main islands of New Zealand. It is separated from the North Island by Cook Strait.
title: South Island

text: Tasmania (Palawa Kani: lutruwita) is a large island off the southern coast of mainland Australia. It is a state of Australia.
title: Tasmania

text: Alexander Island is also known as Alexander I Island, Alexander I Land, Alexander Land, lexander I Archipelago, and Zemlja Alexandra I. It is near the South Pole.
title: Alexander Island

text: The Horn of Africa (alternatively Northeast Africa, and sometimes Somali Peninsula) is a peninsula in East Africa that sticks out into the Somali Sea and Guardafui Channel, and is along the southern side of the Gulf of Aden.
title: Horn of Africa

text: The Baja California Peninsula (or Lower California) is a peninsula of North America. It is west of Mexico.
title: Baja California Peninsula

text: The Alaska Peninsula is a peninsula of southwestern Alaska. It is between the Pacific Ocean and the Bering Sea.
title: Alaska Peninsula

text: The Labrador Peninsula is a large peninsula in eastern Canada. It is bounded by the Hudson Bay to the west, the Hudson Strait to the north, the Labrador Sea to the east, and the Gulf of Saint Lawrence to the southeast.
title: Labrador Peninsula

text: The Yucatán Peninsula is a peninsula in North America. It separates the Caribbean Sea from the Gulf of Mexico.
title: Yucatán Peninsula

text: The Indian subcontinent is a term mainly used for the geographic region which includes: Bangladesh, Bhutan, the Republic of India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. It is north of the Indian Ocean.
title: Indian subcontinent

text: The Arabian Peninsula or Arabia is a peninsula in Southwesterm Asia at the junction of Africa and Asia. It is east of Ethiopia and northern Somalia, south of Iraq and Jordan, and southwest of Iran.
title: Arabian Peninsula

text: Indochina or the Indochinese Peninsula or the Mainland Southeast Asia is a region in Southeast Asia.
title: Indochina

text: Korea is a peninsula in northeast Asia, Korean Peninsula. Korea became a country (or state) in 918.
title: Korea

text: The Malay Peninsula (Malay: Semenanjung Tanah Melayu) is a large peninsula in Southeast Asia. The place is divided into three political parts.
title: Malay Peninsula

text: The Kamchatka Peninsula (Russian: полуо́стров Камча́тка, poluostrov Kamchatka) is a peninsula in eastern Russia. It is 1,250 km (780 mi) long and covers about 270,000 km2 (100,000 sq mi) between the Pacific Ocean and the Sea of Okhotsk.
title: Kamchatka Peninsula

text: The Sinai Peninsula or Sinai (Arabic: سيناء Sīnā), is a triangular peninsula in Egypt. It is about 60,000 km2 (23,000 sq mi) in area.
title: Sinai Peninsula

text: The Taymyr Peninsula (Russian: Полуостров Таймыр, Таймырский полуостров) is a peninsula in the Far North of Russia.
title: Taymyr Peninsula

text: The Balkans is a geographical region in Southeast Europe, which partially coincides with the Balkan Peninsula. It takes its name from the Balkan Mountains, which run through the center of Bulgaria.
title: Balkans

text: Crimea, (Ukrainian: Крим) sometimes also called The Crimea, is a peninsula in the Black Sea. The peninsula separates the Black Sea from the Sea of Azov.
title: Crimea

text: The Iberian Peninsula, or Iberia, is the southwest part of Europe. Like other peninsulas, it is mostly surrounded by sea.
title: Iberian Peninsula

text: The Italian Peninsula or Apennine Peninsula (Italian: Penisola italiana, Penisola appenninica) is a large peninsula of Southern Europe. It extends into the Mediterranean Sea, with the Ionian and Adriatic Seas on the east and the Tyrrhenian Sea on the west.
title: Italian Peninsula

text: Jutland (Danish: Jylland; German: Jütland) is a peninsula in northern Europe. It forms the mainland part of Denmark and a northern part of Germany.
title: Jutland

text: This article is about the peninsula in the Australian state of Queensland; not the Yorke Peninsula in South Australia, or Cape York, Greenland.
title: Cape York Peninsula

text: The Antarctic Peninsula is the largest peninsula in Antarctica. The peninsula is the northernmost part of the mainland of Antarctica.
title: Antarctic Peninsula

text: The Atlas Mountains (Amazigh: Idurar n Watlas, Arabic: جبال الأطلس) are a mountain range in northwest Africa. They extend about 2,400 km (1,500 miles) through Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia.
title: Atlas Mountains

text: Drakensberg (derived from Afrikaans Drakensberge, literally: Dragon mountains) is the highest mountain range in Southern Africa. The highest peak is in Lesotho, where they are called Maloti.
title: Drakensberg

text: Ethiopian Highlands is the name for a mountain area in Ethiopia and Eritrea. It is also called Abessynian Highlands, named after Abyssinia, a region on the Horn of Africa.
title: Ethiopian Highlands

text: The Great Rift Valley or East African Rift is a continuous geographical trench, about 6,440 kilometres (3,700 mi) in length, that runs from northern Syria in Southwest Asia to central Mozambique in East Africa. The rift is bordered by a series of mountains and active volcanoes.
title: Great Rift Valley

text: The American Cordillera is a chain of mountain ranges. It is the western "backbone" of North America, Central America, South America and Antarctica.
title: American Cordillera

text: The Adirondack Mountains are a mountain range in the northeastern part of New York in the United States.
title: Adirondack Mountains

text: The Appalachian Mountains (French: les Appalaches) are a large group of North American mountains. They are part of the oldest mountain range in North America.
title: Appalachian Mountains

text: The Black Hills are a small mountain range from the Great Plains of North America in South Dakota.
title: Black Hills

text: Bryce Canyon National Park is a national park in southwestern Utah. Its major feature is Bryce Canyon.
title: Bryce Canyon National Park

text: The Canadian Shield, also called the Laurentian Plateau (French: Bouclier canadien), is a large area of exposed Precambrian, igneous and high-grade metamorphic rocks. The geological shield is the ancient geological core of the North American continent (Laurentia, also called the North American Craton).
title: Canadian Shield

text: The Grand Canyon is a famous canyon in Arizona, formed by the Colorado River. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and a National Park of the United States.
title: Grand Canyon

text: The Great Plains is a large space of level land or prairie in the middle and western parts of North America. It is a steppe or grassland.
title: Great Plains

text: The Altiplano (Spanish for "high plain"), Collao (Quechua and Aymara: Qullaw, meaning "place of the Qulla") or Andean Plateau, is the largest high plateau on Earth after the Tibetan Plateau. It is in South America.
title: Altiplano

text: The Iranian plateau, also known as the Persian plateau is a geological formation in Southwest Asia, Southern Asia and the Caucasus region. As a historical region, it includes Parthia, Media and eastern Persia, the heartlands of Greater Persia (mainly Iran, Afghanistan, and Pakistan west of the River Indus).
title: Iranian plateau

text: The Zagros Mountains (Kurdish: Zagros - زاگرۆس, Persian: رشته كوههاى زاگرس), make up Iran's and Iraq's largest mountain range. They have a total length of 1 500 km.
title: Zagros Mountains

text: The Hindu Kush is a range of mountains. It starts near Pamir in the north of Gilgit extending in the southwest deep into the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan, Tirich Mir is here.
title: Hindu Kush

text: The Tian Shan is a large system of mountain ranges in Central Asia. The tallest mountain is Jengish Chokusu, at 7,439 metres (24,406 ft) high.
title: Tian Shan

text: Alborz (also written Alburz, Elburz or Elborz), is a mountain range in northern Iran. Its borders start at Azerbaijan and Armenia in the northwest of Iran and reach to the southern end of the Caspian Sea.
title: Alborz Mountains

text: The Turan Depression, Turan Lowland or Turanian Basin is a low-lying desert basin region stretching from southern Turkmenistan through Uzbekistan to Kazakhstan. The lowland region lies to the east of the Caspian Sea and southeast of the Aral Sea in the vast Aral–Caspian Depression.
title: Turan Depression

text: The North China Plain (simplified Chinese: 华北平原; traditional Chinese: 華北平原; pinyin: Huáběi Píngyuán) is the large space of level land in eastern China. It was made by the Yellow River for the most part.
title: North China Plain

text: The Tibetan Plateau, also known as Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, is a vast and high plateau. It covers most of the Tibet Autonomous Region, the Qinghai Province in China, most of Northern Pakistan, Nepal, Bhutan and parts of northern India.
title: Tibetan Plateau

text: Kunlun is a mountain range in China. Lots of people argue how big the mountain range is.
title: Kunlun Mountains

text: The Mongolian Plateau or Altai Plateau is a plateau in East Asia. This plateau covers about 3,200,000 square kilometers (1,200,000 sq mi).
title: Mongolian Plateau

text: The Altai Mountains (/ɑːlˈtaɪ/), also spelled Altay Mountains, are a mountain range in Central and East Asia, where Russia, China and Mongolia converge, and where the rivers Ob and Irtysh have their headwaters.
title: Altai Mountains

text: The Deccan Plateau is a large plateau that covers most of South India. It is triangular, surrounded by three mountain ranges.
title: Deccan Plateau

text: The Karakoram is a mountain range in Asia. The name is from a Turkic word meaning "black gravel".
title: Karakoram

text: The North Indian Plain or the Indo-Gangetic Plain is the large space of level land that is made by the Indus River and Ganges River in the northern parts of the Indian subcontinent. It is an important part of the countries of India, Pakistan, Nepal, and Bangladesh.
title: North Indian Plain

text: The Western Ghats is a mountain range in India. It is also called, "Sahyadri." The Western Ghats run north to south.
title: Western Ghats

text: The Caucasus Mountains is a mountain range in Eurasia. They are in the Caucasus region between the Black Sea in the west and the Caspian Sea in the east.
title: Caucasus Mountains

text: The Pontic Mountains are a mountain range in Turkey. They are in northern Anatolia, close to the southern coast of the Black Sea.
title: Pontic Mountains

text: For the Taurus Mountains on the moon, see Montes Taurus. For Mount Taurus outside Cold Spring, New York, see Bull Hill.
title: Taurus Mountains

text: Najd is a province in central Saudi Arabia that has a diverse history. It also has a dialect language that spoken in Saudi Arabia.
title: Najd

text: The Apennines are mountains in Italy. Their highest mountain is Corno Grande which is 2,912 metres high.
title: Apennine Mountains

text: The Balkan mountain range (Bulgarian and Serbian: Стара планина, Stara planina, "Old Mountain") is an extension of the Carpathian mountain range, separated from it by the Danube River. The People who lived in the Balkan Mountains are called Balkandjii.
title: Balkan Mountains

text: The Carpathian Mountains are the eastern wing of the great Central Mountain System of Central Europe, curving 1500 km (~900 miles) along the borders of Romania, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland, Ukraine, Austria, Serbia, and northern Hungary.
title: Carpathian Mountains

text: The East European Plain (or the Russian Plain) is a vast plain in Eastern Europe, an integral part of the European Plain.
title: East European Plain

text: The Pyrenees (Catalan: Pirineus; Spanish: Pirineos, French: Pyrénées; Occitan: Pirenèus; Aragonese: Perinés; Basque: Pirinioak) are a range of mountains in southwest Europe that form a natural border between France and Spain.
title: Pyrenees

text: The Scandinavian Mountains are a mountain range that runs through the Scandinavian Peninsula. The western sides of the mountains drop steeply into the North Sea and Norwegian Sea, where they form the fjords of Norway.
title: Scandinavian Mountains

text: The Ural Mountains (Russian: Ура́льские го́ры, romanized: Uralskiye gory), also known simply as the Urals, is a mountain range that runs roughly north and south through western Russia.
title: Ural Mountains

text: The Great Dividing Range, or the Eastern Highlands, is Australia's largest mountain range. It is the fifth longest land-based range in the world.
title: Great Dividing Range

text: The Southern Alps is a mountain range in New Zealand. The mountain range runs along the entire length of the South Island.
title: Southern Alps

text: The Transantarctic Mountains are a mountain range in the continent of Antarctica. It divides the continent into eastern and western region.
title: Transantarctic Mountains

text: Aconcagua is the highest mountain in the Americas, and the highest outside Asia. The altitude is 6,967 meters, or 22,851 feet.
title: Aconcagua

text: Denali, also called Mount McKinley is the highest mountain peak in both the United States and North America, and one of Seven Summits. It is exactly 20,310 feet (6,190 m) high.
title: Denali

text: K2 is the second-highest mountain in the world, standing at 8,611 metres (28,251 ft) tall. It is also known as Mount Godwin-Austen or Chogori (ཆོགོ་རི།).
title: K2

text: Mauna Loa is an active volcano on Hawaii Island, in the state of Hawaii, United States. It is considered to be the largest subaerial (from the bottom of the Pacific Ocean) volcano in the world and the tallest volcano in Hawaii.
title: Mauna Loa

text: Mount Elbrus (Russian: Эльбрус, Kabardian: Ӏуащхьэмахуэ, Karachay-Balkar: Минги тау) is a peak in the western Caucasus mountains and one of Seven Summits. It is in Kabardino-Balkaria and Karachay-Cherkessia, Russia, near the border of Georgia.
title: Mount Elbrus

text: Mount Etna is a volcano on the east coast of Sicily, part of southern Italy. It is the largest active volcano in Europe.
title: Mount Etna

text: Mount Kenya is the highest mountain in Kenya. It is 5,199 metres (17,057 feet) high.
title: Mount Kenya

text: Mount Kosciuszko is the highest mountain in Australia. The mountain is 2,228 m (7,310 ft) above sea level.
title: Mount Kosciuszko

text: Mount Kailash is a 6,638 metres (21,778 ft) mountain in the Gangdise Shan mountain range in Tibet. Mount Kailash is also known as Kangrinboqe and Gongdisi Shan.
title: Mount Kailash

text: Mount Olympus (Greek: Όλυμπος; also transliterated as Ólympos, and on Greek maps, Óros Ólimbos) is the highest mountain in Greece. It is 2,917.727 metres (9,572.60 feet) high.
title: Olympus

text: Mount Parnassus, also Parnassos, is a mountain of limestone in central Greece. It is north of the Gulf of Corinth.
title: Mount Parnassus

text: Mount St. Helens is a volcano in the U.S. state of Washington. It is 96 miles (154 km) south of Seattle and 53 miles (85 km) northeast of Portland, Oregon.
title: Mount St. Helens

text: Mount Vesuvius (Italian: Monte Vesuvio, Latin: Mons Vesuvius) is a stratovolcano on the Gulf of Naples, Italy. It is about 8 kilometres (5 mi) east of Naples.
title: Mount Vesuvius

text: Vinson Massif is the highest mountain of Antarctica. It is in the Sentinel Range of the Ellsworth Mountains.
title: Vinson Massif

text: The Chile Rise or Chile Ridge is a mid-ocean ridge in the Pacific, off the coast of Chile. On the ridge, the Nazca plate and the Antarctic plate meet.
title: Chile Rise

text: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean. It is part of a world-wide system of mid-ocean ridges.
title: Mid-Atlantic Ridge

text: The Mariana Trench is the deepest known submarine trench. It is also the deepest known location on Earth itself.
title: Mariana Trench

text: The Arabian Desert is a desert in western Asia. It is on most of the Arabian Peninsula.
title: Arabian Desert

text: The Kalahari Desert is a large arid to semi-arid sandy area in southern Kgalagadi Africa extending 900,000 km² (362,500 sq. mi.), covering much of Botswana and parts of Namibia and South Africa. It has huge tracts of excellent grazing after good rains.
title: Kalahari Desert

text: The Negev ( NEG-ev; Hebrew: הַנֶּגֶב, romanized: hanNégev) or Negeb (Arabic: النقب, romanized: an-Naqab) is the southern region of Israel. It is a desert that covers about 60% of the current state of Israel.
title: Negev

text: The Taklamakan Desert, also known as Taklimakan and Teklimakan, is a desert in Northwest China, in the southwest part of the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region. It is bounded by the Kunlun Mountains to the south and the desert Pamir Mountains and Tian Shan to the west and north.
title: Taklamakan Desert

text: The Great Victoria Desert is the largest desert in Australia. It consists of sand dunes, small sandhills, grassland plains, areas with closely packed pebbles (called desert pavement or gibber plains) and salt lakes.
title: Great Victoria Desert
