text: The Atacama Desert is a desert. It is on the Tropic of Capricorn in northern Chile and is one of the driest places on earth.
title: Atacama Desert

text: Iguaçu Falls are a series of extremely large waterfalls that lie on the border of Argentina 80% and Brazil 20%. It is fed by the Iguaçu River, which flows into the Paraná River.
title: Iguaçu Falls

text: Niagara Falls is the collective, name of three big waterfalls on the Niagara River in eastern North America, on the border between the United States and Canada. The three waterfalls are: the Horseshoe Falls, sometimes called the Canadian Falls, the American Falls, and the smaller Bridal Veil Falls.
title: Niagara Falls

text: World Heritage Sites are places in the world which are very important from a cultural or natural point of view. A part of the United Nations called UNESCO selects these sites.
title: World Heritage Site

text: The Aïr Mountains is a triangular massif, located in north Niger, inside the Sahara. They rise to more than 1,800 m (5,900 ft) and go over 84,000 km2 (32,000 sq mi).
title: Aïr Mountains

text: Tassili n'Ajjer is a mountain range in the Algerian part of the Sahara Desert. The name means "Plateau of the Rivers".
title: Tassili n'Ajjer

text: The Okapi Wildlife Reserve (French: Réserve de faune à okapis) is a wildlife reserve in the Ituri Forest in the northeast of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is near the country's borders with South Sudan and Uganda.
title: Okapi Wildlife Reserve

text: The Sunderbans National Park is a National Park, tiger reserve, and a Biosphere Reserve in the Sunderban delta. It is in the Indian state of West Bengal.
title: Sundarbans National Park

text: Kaziranga National Park is a national park in India. The park is home to two-thirds of the world's great one-horned rhinoceroses.
title: Kaziranga National Park

text: Lorentz National Park is a national park in Papua, Indonesia. It has an area of about 25,056 kilometres (15,569 mi).
title: Lorentz National Park

text: Białowieża Forest is an ancient woodland. It is on the border between Poland and Belarus.
title: Białowieża Forest

text: The Virgin Komi Forests is a large woodland in the northern part of the Ural mountain range, in Russia. The forests are part of the Komi Republic of Russia.
title: Virgin Komi Forests

text: The Giant's Causeway is an area of about 40,000 interlocking basalt columns. The formation is a result of an ancient volcanic eruption.
title: Giant's Causeway

text: Yellowstone National Park is a national park in the United States. It was the world's first national park.
title: Yellowstone National Park

text: Chaco Culture National Historical Park is a United States National Historical Park. It is in New Mexico.
title: Chaco Culture National Historical Park

text: Mesa Verde National Park is a United States National Park and UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is in Montezuma County, Colorado, United States.
title: Mesa Verde National Park

text: Olympic National Park is a national park in the U.S. state of Washington. It was established on June 29, 1938.
title: Olympic National Park

text: Everglades National Park is an American national park that protects the southern twenty percent of the original Everglades in Florida. The park is the largest tropical wilderness in the United States and the largest wilderness of any kind east of the Mississippi River.
title: Everglades National Park

text: Kluane / Wrangell–St. Elias / Glacier Bay / Tatshenshini-Alsek is a system of parks in Canada and the United States. It is at the border of Yukon and British Columbia (Canada); and Alaska (United States).
title: Kluane / Wrangell–St. Elias / Glacier Bay / Tatshenshini-Alsek

text: Great Smoky Mountains National Park is a national park in Tennessee and North Carolina in the United States. It is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
title: Great Smoky Mountains National Park

text: The Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument is a World Heritage site. It is often called Northwestern Hawaiian Islands Marine National Monument.
title: Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument

text: Te Wāhipounamu (Māori for "the place of greenstone") is a World Heritage Site in the south west corner of the South Island of New Zealand.
title: Te Wahipounamu

text: The Jaú National Park ('Parque Nacional do Jaú') is in the heart of the Amazon rainforest in the Amazonas state of Brazil.
title: Jaú National Park

text: Northeast Greenland National Park is a national park in Greenland, Denmark. It is the largest national park in the world, with an area of 972,000 km2 (375,000 sq mi).
title: Northeast Greenland National Park

text: Wood Buffalo National Park is a national park and the largest one in Canada. The park is in northeastern Alberta and southern Northwest Territories.
title: Wood Buffalo National Park

text: Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve is an American national park that protects portions of the Brooks Range in northern Alaska. The park is the most northern national park in the United States, situated entirely north of the Arctic Circle.
title: Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve

text: Abu Dhabi (Arabic: أبو ظبي, ʼAbū Ẓaby) is the capital city of the United Arab Emirates. It is in the emirate of Abu Dhabi.
title: Abu Dhabi

text: Ahmedabad is the largest city in the Gujarat state, in Western India. The city is the administrative centre of Ahmedabad district, and was the capital of Gujarat from 1960 to 1970.
title: Ahmedabad

text: Almaty (Kazakh: Алматы; formerly known as Alma-Ata (Алма-Ата), also Verniy, (Верный)) is the largest city in Kazakhstan. It has a population of over 1,700,000 people (as of 2015).
title: Almaty

text: Amman (Arabic: عمان ʿAmmān), is the capital of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan and the capital of the Amman Governorate.
title: Amman

text: Ankara is the capital city of the country of Turkey. It is in the center of Anatolia.
title: Ankara

text: Aşgabat (Turkmen: Aşgabat; Persian: عشق آباد, UniPers: Ešq-âbâd; Russian: Ашхаба́д - Ashkhabád) is the capital city of Turkmenistan. It also spelled as Ashgabat, Ashkabat, Ashkhabad, Ashgabad.
title: Aşgabat

text: Bangalore (English pronunciation: ˈbæŋɡəlɔər, bæŋɡəˈlɔər), officially known as Bengaluru (Kannada: ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು), is the capital city of the Indian state of Karnataka. It is famous for its information technology industry and so it is called the Silicon Valley of India.
title: Bangalore

text: Beirut is the capital of Lebanon. It is one of the richest and oldest continuously inhabited cities of the world.
title: Beirut

text: Bishkek (Kyrgyz: Бишкек ) is the capital city of Kyrgyzstan. It has a population of 900,000 (2005).
title: Bishkek

text: Busan (formerly written as Pusan) is the largest port city and second-largest city in South Korea. It lies on the southeast tip of the Korean Peninsula.
title: Busan

text: Chengdu (also called The Hibiscus City), is the fifth largest city in the People's Republic of China. It is the capital of Sichuan province and is on top of the Chengdu Plain.
title: Chengdu

text: Chennai (formerly known as Madras) is the capital city of the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It has a population of about 7 million people.
title: Chennai

text: Chongqing (Simplified Chinese: 重庆, Traditional Chinese: 重慶; pinyin: Chóngqìng; Postal System Pinyin: Chungking) is a city and a district in Central China.
title: Chongqing

text: Colombo (Sinhala: කොළඹ; Tamil: கொழும்பு) is the largest city of Sri Lanka. It is the city which is economically most important to the country.
title: Colombo

text: Dili is the capital of the country East Timor. People from Portugal moved there around 1520.
title: Dili

text: Doha (Arabic: الدوحة;, Ad-Dawḥah or Ad-Dōḥah) is the capital city of Qatar. It has a population of 673,000 (2025) and is at 25.3° N 51.5333° E, on the Persian Gulf.
title: Doha

text: Dushanbe (Tajik: Душанбе, Persian: دوشنبه) is the capital city of Tajikistan. About 562,000 people live in Dushanbe as of 2000.
title: Dushanbe

text: Isfahan or Esfahān (historically also rendered as Ispahan or Hispahan, Old Persian: Aspadana, Middle Persian: Spahān, Persian: اصفهان Esfahān) is the capital of Esfahan Province in Iran. It is about 340 km south of Tehran.
title: Isfahan

text: Gaza (Arabic: غزة, romanized: Ghazza), also called Gaza City, is the largest city inside Gaza and in Palestine. The city has a population of about 400,000.
title: Gaza City

text: Hanoi (Vietnamese: Hà Nội) is the capital of Vietnam. It is also the second most populated city in the country.
title: Hanoi

text: Ho Chi Minh City (Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh) is a city in southern Vietnam. It is governed as a municipality and includes a large rural area.
title: Ho Chi Minh City

text: Islamabad (Urdu: اسلام آباد, abode of Islam) is the Federal capital city of Pakistan. The city is located on the Pothohar Plateau in the northwest of the country.
title: Islamabad

text: The Republic of Uganda is a landlocked country in east Africa. It shares land borders with five countries including the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west, Kenya to the east, South Sudan to the north, Rwanda to the south-west, and Tanzania to the south.
title: Uganda

text: The United Arab Emirates (UAE; in Arabic: الإمارات العربية المتحدة) is a country in Western Asia. It borders Oman, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia.
title: United Arab Emirates

text: Uruguay (officially named Oriental Republic of Uruguay) is a country in South America. The language spoken there is Spanish.
title: Uruguay

text: Uzbekistan, officially the Republic of Uzbekistan, is a country in Central Asia. Its capital and largest city is Tashkent.
title: Uzbekistan

text: Vanuatu is a country in the Pacific Ocean. The official languages of Vanuatu are Bislama, English and French.
title: Vanuatu

text: Venezuela, officially the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, is a country in northern South America. The official language is Spanish, and the capital city is Caracas.
title: Venezuela

text: Western Sahara (Arabic: الصحراء الغربية; Amazigh: Tanẓṛuft Tutrimt; Spanish: Sahara Occidental) is a territory in north Africa. To the north is Morocco, to the east is Algeria, to the south is Mauritania, and to the west is the Atlantic Ocean.
title: Western Sahara

text: Yemen, officially the Republic of Yemen is a nation in the Middle East. It is the old North Yemen and South Yemen, in the southwestern corner of the Arabian Peninsula.
title: Yemen

text: The Republic of Zambia is a country in southern Africa.
title: Zambia

text: The Republic of Zimbabwe is a country in the southern part of the continent of Africa. Its capital city is Harare.
title: Zimbabwe

text: Central America is a subregion of North America and Latin America. The region consists of seven countries including Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama.
title: Central America

text: Scandinavia is a group of countries in Northern Europe, including Denmark, Norway, and Sweden. Some people also think Finland is part of Scandinavia and that Iceland and the Faroe Islands should also count.
title: Scandinavia

text: Southeast Asia or Southeastern Asia, is the southeastern part of Asia. There are 11 countries in this region.
title: Southeast Asia

text: California, officially the State of California, is a state in the western part of the United States, along the Pacific Ocean.
title: California

text: Catalonia (Catalan: Catalunya; Spanish: Cataluña: Occitan: Catalonha) is a Spanish autonomous community. It is south of the eastern Pyrenees, and has a northern border with France.
title: Catalonia

text: England is a country and the largest of the four countries which make up the United Kingdom.
title: England

text: Guangdong (Chinese: 广东省) is a province on the southern coast of China. The meaning of the name in Chinese is "east of the expanse" or "expanse's east".
title: Guangdong

text: Northern Ireland (Irish: Tuaisceart Éireann; Ulster Scots: Norlinn Airlann) is one of the four constituent countries of the United Kingdom. It is on the island of Ireland.
title: Northern Ireland

text: Ontario is a province of Canada that is in the eastern half of Canada, between Manitoba and Quebec. Ontario has the largest population of any province, with over 16 million in 2026, and is home to the largest city in Canada, Toronto, which is also the capital of the province.
title: Ontario

text: Siberia is the part of Russia that is in Asia. It covers wide landscapes, and stretches from the Ural Mountains in the east to the Pacific in the west.
title: Siberia

text: Tuscany (Italian: Toscana) is a region in the center of Italy. It has an area of 22,990 square kilometres (8,880 sq mi) and a population of about 3.6 million people (in 2004).
title: Tuscany

text: An experiment is a test of an idea or a method. It is often used by scientists and engineers.
title: Experiment

text: A laboratory (lab for short) is a work place where scientific research, experiments, or measurement are done.
title: Laboratory

text: Observation is a process of using the senses to learn about the world. It can be taken in multiple perspectives, such as analyzing, viewing, either actively or passively.
title: Observation

text: Research is a way of looking for new information, new understanding, and new facts. A person who does research is called a researcher.
title: Research

text: The scientific method refers to ways to get facts, correct errors and mistakes, and test theories.
title: Scientific method

text: In everyday speech, the word "theory" is used as a "best guess". In modern science, a scientific theory is a hypothesis that has been tested and explains a lot of things.
title: Scientific theory

text: A scientist is a person who studies or has mastered the field in science. A scientist tries to understand how our world, or other things, work.
title: Scientist

text: A quantum computer is a model of how to build a computer. The idea is that quantum computers can use certain ideas from quantum mechanics, such as superposition and entanglement, to perform operations on data.
title: Quantum computer

text: The byte (symbol: B or o, also known as the octet) is a unit of measurement of the size of information on a computer or other electronic device. A single byte is eight bits.
title: Byte

text: The baud (symbol: Bd) is the unit to measure the symbol rate. If one symbol can be transmitted per second, this is equal to one Baud.
title: Baud

text: The radian (symbol: rad) is a unit of measuring angles. It is shown by the symbol "rad" or, less often, c (for circular measure).
title: Radian

text: The steradian (symbol: sr) or square radian is the SI unit for solid angle. It is defined as the solid angle that, when projected onto a surrounding spherical surface, produces an area (of any shape) equal to the square of the radius of the sphere.
title: Steradian

text: Astrobiology is the study of life in outer space. The field of astrobiology looks for conditions necessary for life, such as liquid water or a similar substitute, a good temperature, or the presence of oxygen.
title: Astrobiology

text: Interstellar extinction is when the electromagnetic radiation of an astronomical object is blocked and/or scattered by other astronomical objects and cosmic dust.
title: Extinction (astronomy)

text: Extraterrestrial life is life that is not from the planet Earth. It is also called alien life or just extraterrestrials or aliens.
title: Extraterrestrial life

text: Space, in everyday language, is something that we all know. It is measured in the three dimensions of distance: length, width, and height.
title: Space (physics)

text: Geocentrism is the belief that the Earth is fixed at the centre of the Universe. Geocentrists accept that the Earth is round.
title: Geocentrism

text: Heliocentrism is the idea that the Earth and other planets revolve around the Sun, which is the center of the solar system. Many people proposed heliocentrism, such as Aristarchus of Samos from ancient Greece, but Nicolaus Copernicus was the first to think of good reasons why it is true.
title: Heliocentrism

text: Astrophysics is the study of how stars, planets, and other things in the Universe work, and how we can learn about them. Astrophysicists use physics and chemistry to explain what astronomers find and see.
title: Astrophysics

text: In general relativity, an event horizon is the part of a black hole where light cannot escape. Imagine the black hole to be like a ball that you could see in a large spot of emptiness.
title: Event horizon

text: A Van Allen radiation belt is a zone of charged particles which come from the Sun as the solar wind. They are captured and held by the Earth's magnetic field.
title: Van Allen radiation belt

text: Tunguska event is the name for a very large mid-air explosion that occurred on 30 June 1908 in Siberia. Most eyewitnesses talk about one or more explosions that happened around 7:15 a.m. local time.
title: Tunguska event

text: In astronomy, an apsis, plural apsides (IPA: /apsɪdɪːz/) is the point of greatest or least distance of the elliptical orbit of an astronomical object from its center of attraction, which is generally the center of mass of the system.
title: Apsis

text: The orbital period is the time taken for a given object to make one complete orbit around another object. The year and month are orbital periods.
title: Orbital period

text: In geometry, the semi-major axis is the distance from the center of an ellipse to the farthest point on the perimeter of the ellipse. The semi-major axis is half of the major axis, which goes all the way across the ellipse at the widest part.
title: Semi-major and semi-minor axes

text: Gravitational lensing is caused by a massive body between a distant object and ourselves. It can create the appearance of two or more objects where there is really only one.
title: Gravitational lensing

text: The astronomical unit (AU) is a unit of length derived from the Earth's orbit. It is the average distance the Earth gets from the Sun on the long axis of the ellipse.
title: Astronomical unit

text: A light year (symbol: ly) is the distance that light travels in empty space in one year. Since the speed of light is about 300,000 km per second (about 186,000 miles per second), then a light year is 9.46 trillion kilometers (about 5.87 trillion miles), for AU, one light year is 63,241 AU.
title: Light year

text: The parsec (symbol: pc) is a unit of distance used in astronomy. It is the distance that light travels in 3.26 years, or just under 31 trillion kilometres (about 19 trillion miles).
title: Parsec

text: The magnitude of a star or other celestial object is a number that measures its brightness. Apparent magnitude (m) of a celestial object is a number that measures its brightness as seen by an observer on Earth, and absolute magnitude is its actual brightness adjusted for distance.
title: Magnitude (astronomy)

text: An observatory is a place for making observations. The term is most used for astronomical observatories, which are places for looking at the sky.
title: Observatory

text: An extrasolar planet (or exoplanet) is a natural planet in a planetary system outside our own solar system. A related concept is an exomoon, a natural satellite orbiting an exoplanet.
title: Extrasolar planet

text: Dwarf planet is the name used to classify some objects in the solar system.
title: Dwarf planet

text: A gas giant is a giant planet that has a solid core, but a very thick atmosphere. This means that most of the planet is made up of gas.
title: Gas giant

text: A terrestrial planet, or rocky planet, is a planet that is mostly composed of silicate, rocks and metals. Earth is the "original" terrestrial planet.
title: Terrestrial planet

text: Photometry is a method of problem solving in astronomy. It aims to measure flux.
title: Photometry (astronomy)

text: The astrolabe is a tool using the positions of the stars or sun. It was formerly used in navigation to help explorers and sailors figure out where they were.
title: Astrolabe

text: A sundial shows the current solar time during the day. It does this because the sun appears to move through the sky.
title: Sundial

text: The Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) is an array of radio telescopes in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile. A high and dry site is very important for millimeter wavelength work.
title: Atacama Large Millimeter Array

text: The Great Observatories program is four large, powerful space-based telescopes. They are a series of satellites placed by NASA.
title: Great Observatories program

text: The Herschel Space Observatory was a space observatory built by the European Space Agency (ESA). It was the largest infrared telescope ever put into orbit until the launch of the James Webb Space Telescope.
title: Herschel Space Observatory

text: Hubble Space Telescope (HST) is the first big optical space observatory telescope. Being above the atmosphere means it can see the sky more clearly than a telescope on the ground.
title: Hubble Space Telescope

text: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is a telescope that was launched on 25 December 2021. It is a replacement for the Hubble Space Telescope which was launched in 1990.
title: James Webb Space Telescope

text: The Spitzer Space Telescope is a telescope launched into space by NASA in 2003. It is the fourth telescope in the Great Observatories program (the Hubble Space Telescope was the first).
title: Spitzer Space Telescope

text: The Very Large Telescope (VLT) is a telescope operated by the European Southern Observatory. It is on Cerro Paranal in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile.
title: Very Large Telescope

text: Palomar Observatory is a privately owned observatory in San Diego County, California, 90 miles (145 km) southeast of Mount Wilson Observatory, on Palomar Mountain in the Palomar Mountain Range. It is owned and run by the California Institute of Technology (Caltech).
title: Palomar Observatory

text: Astrometry is a part of astronomy that has to do with measuring the motion of objects in space such as stars. Two main ways to measure these objects are proper motion and parallax.
title: Astrometry

text: The cosmic distance ladder (also known as the extragalactic distance scale) is the way astronomers measure the distance of objects in space. No one method works for all objects and distances, so astronomers use a number of methods.
title: Cosmic distance ladder

text: Parallax is the perceived change in position of an object seen from two different places.
title: Parallax

text: A celestial coordinate system is a coordinate system that helps astronomers specify the location of objects in the sky. These objects may be stars, planets or even satellites.
title: Celestial coordinate system

text: Declination (abbrev. dec or δ) is a word used in astronomy to describe one of the two coordinates of the equatorial coordinate system, the other being either right ascension or hour angle.
title: Declination

text: Right ascension (abbreviated RA; symbol α) is the astronomical word for one of the two coordinates of a point on the celestial sphere when using the equatorial coordinate system. It is the celestial counterpart to longitude.
title: Right ascension

text: The celestial equator is a term in observational astronomy. It is a great circle on the imaginary celestial sphere, in the same plane as the Earth's equator.
title: Celestial equator

text: In astronomy and navigation, the celestial sphere is an imaginary sphere (ball) of a very large unspecified size. The earth and the sphere have the same centre: they are concentric.
title: Celestial sphere

text: An equinox is when the sun passes directly over the equator. There are two equinoxes each year.
title: Equinox

text: The ecliptic is the plane of Earth's orbit around the Sun.
title: Ecliptic

text: The horizon (from Greek orizein, to limit) is the line that separates earth from sky. But at many places the true horizon cannot be seen as there are trees, buildings, mountains and so forth.
title: Horizon

text: In astronomy, the nadir is a point "below" a particular location. "Below" means in the same direction of gravity at that location.
title: Nadir

text: A solstice is an astronomical event that happens twice each year when the Sun reaches its highest position in the sky as seen from the North or South Pole.
title: Solstice

text: A star chart is a graphic device or diagram which shows the night sky as seen from Earth. They are one of the oldest types of written or carved communication.
title: Star chart

text: In astronomy, the zenith is a point "above" a particular location, in the sky. "Above" means in the opposite direction of gravity at that location.
title: Zenith

text: The Zodiac is the twelve constellations in the form of animals, humans or objects.
title: Zodiac

text: A constellation is a group of stars which make up imaginary outline or pattern in the night sky (the celestial sphere). Usually they are said to represent an animal, mythological person or creature in a shape.
title: Constellation

text: Andromeda is a constellation in the northern sky. It is named after the princess Andromeda in Greek mythology.
title: Andromeda (constellation)

text: Aquarius is a constellation of the zodiac. It sits between Capricornus and Pisces.
title: Aquarius (constellation)

text: Aquila is a constellation. The name means 'eagle' in Latin.
title: Aquila (constellation)

text: Ara is a constellation in the southern sky. Ara means altar in Latin.
title: Ara (constellation)

text: Aries is one of the constellations of the zodiac. It is in the Northern Hemisphere.
title: Aries (constellation)

text: Auriga is a constellation in the northern sky. It is the Latin word for "charioteer" - someone who drives a vehicle that is pulled by an animal.
title: Auriga (constellation)

text: Boötes, pronounced with both 'O's as 'boötez', is one of the 88 modern constellations in the northern sky. The name is from the Greek word Βοώτης, which means herdsman – someone who takes care of animals.
title: Boötes

text: Camelopardalis is a constellation in the northern sky. It is hard to see because it is not very bright.
title: Camelopardalis

text: Cancer (pronounced /ˈkænsɚ/) is one of the twelve constellations of the zodiac. The name is Latin for crab.
title: Cancer (constellation)

text: Canes Venatici is a constellation in the northern sky. It means "the hunting dogs" in Latin.
title: Canes Venatici

text: Sirius is 20 times brighter than the sun.
title: Canis Major

text: Canis Minor is a constellation in the northern sky. It is Latin for "smaller dog" or "the lesser dog".
title: Canis Minor

text: Capricornus is one of the constellations of the zodiac. It is often called Capricorn, especially when referring to the corresponding astrological sign.
title: Capricornus

text: Carina is a constellation in the southern sky, only visible from the southern hemisphere. It means the keel of a ship in Latin.
title: Carina (constellation)

text: Cassiopeia is a constellation in the northern sky. It was named after a queen in Greek mythology called Cassiopeia.
title: Cassiopeia (constellation)

text: Centaurus is a constellation in the southern hemisphere of the night sky. It is named after a centaur, which is a creature that is half man and half horse.
title: Centaurus

text: Cepheus is a constellation in the northern sky.
title: Cepheus (constellation)

text: Cetus is a constellation in the northern sky.
title: Cetus

text: Columba is a constellation in the southern sky.
title: Columba (constellation)

text: Coma Berenices is a constellation in the northern sky.
title: Coma Berenices

text: Corona Australis is a constellation in the southern sky.
title: Corona Australis

text: Corona Borealis is a constellation in the northern sky.
title: Corona Borealis

text: Corvus is a small constellation in the southern sky. Its name is Latin for raven or crow.
title: Corvus (constellation)

text: Crater (/ˈkreɪtər/) is a constellation. In Latin it means cup.
title: Crater (constellation)

text: Crux, commonly known as the Southern Cross, is a constellation that can be seen by people in the Southern Hemisphere. Its four brightest stars are in the shape of a cross.
title: Crux

text: Cygnus is a constellation in the northern sky. Cygnus means "swan" in Greek.
title: Cygnus (constellation)

text: Delphinus is a constellation in the southern sky.
title: Delphinus (constellation)

text: Draco is a constellation in the northern sky.
title: Draco (constellation)

text: Equuleus is a constellation in the northern sky.
title: Equuleus

text: Eridanus is a constellation in the southern sky.
title: Eridanus (constellation)

text: Gemini is one of the constellations of the zodiac. It was one of the 48 constellations described by the 2nd century AD astronomer Ptolemy.
title: Gemini (constellation)

text: Hercules is a constellation in the northern part of the sky. It represents the mythological Hercules of Greek mythology.
title: Hercules (constellation)

text: Hydra is a constellation that has parts in the northern sky and parts in the southern sky. It is the biggest constellation.
title: Hydra (constellation)

text: Lacerta is a constellation in the northern sky.
title: Lacerta

text: Leo is one of the constellations of the zodiac. Its name is Latin for lion.
title: Leo (constellation)

text: Leo Minor is a constellation in the northern sky.
title: Leo Minor

text: Lepus is a constellation south of the celestial equator. Its name is Latin for hare.
title: Lepus (constellation)

text: Libra is a constellation of the zodiac and is located in the Southern celestial hemisphere. Its name is Latin for weighing scales.
title: Libra (constellation)

text: Lupus is a constellation in the southern sky.
title: Lupus (constellation)

text: Lynx is a constellation in the northern sky.
title: Lynx (constellation)

text: Lyra is a constellation in the northern sky.
title: Lyra

text: Monoceros (Greek: Μονόκερως) is a constellation on the celestial equator. Its name is Greek for 'unicorn'.
title: Monoceros

text: Ophiuchus (Οφιούχος: say it 'Ofi-youkus'), is one of the 88 listed constellations. In Latin, it means "serpent-holder".
title: Ophiuchus

text: Orion is one of the largest constellations in the sky. It is supposed to look like the warrior Orion from Greek mythology.
title: Orion (constellation)

text: Pegasus is a constellation in the northern sky.
title: Pegasus (constellation)

text: Perseus is a constellation in the northern sky named after Perseus, the mitological greek hero. Perseus is located in the northern celestial hemisphere.
title: Perseus (constellation)

text: Pisces is a constellation located on the celestial equator.
title: Pisces (constellation)

text: Piscis Austrinus is a constellation in the southern sky.
title: Piscis Austrinus

text: Puppis is a constellation that can be seen in the southern sky. It is one of the 88 modern constellations recognized by the International Astronomical Union.
title: Puppis

text: Pyxis is a constellation in the southern sky.
title: Pyxis

text: Sagitta is a small constellation in the northern sky. Its name is Latin for 'arrow'.
title: Sagitta

text: The constellation Sagittarius (meaning "the Archer") is a group of stars in one area of the night sky. The stars are in the shape of a centaur archer.
title: Sagittarius (constellation)

text: Scutum is a constellation in the southern sky.
title: Scutum

text: Serpens is a constellation in the northern sky.
title: Serpens

text: Sextans is a constellation in the southern sky.
title: Sextans

text: Taurus (means bull in latin) is one of the largest and well-known zodiac constellations. It is located in the northern celestial hemisphere.
title: Taurus (constellation)

text: Triangulum is a constellation in the northern sky. The former constellation Triangulum Minus was once its own constellation, as a part of Triangulum.
title: Triangulum

text: Triangulum Australe is a constellation in the southern sky.
title: Triangulum Australe

text: Ursa Major is a constellation in the northern part of the sky. Its name means Great Bear in Latin.
title: Ursa Major

text: Ursa Minor is a constellation in the northern sky. It is often called the Little Bear or the Little Dipper.
title: Ursa Minor

text: Vela is a constellation in the southern sky, which contains the Vela Supercluster. Its name is Latin for the sails of a ship, and it was originally part of a larger constellation, the ship Argo Navis, which was later divided into three parts, the others being Carina and Puppis.
title: Vela (constellation)

text: Virgo is a zodiac constellation which lies on the celestial equator. It is between Leo (at west) and Libra (at east).This constellation is large; the constellation is the second biggest constellation you can see on the sky.
title: Virgo (constellation)

text: Vulpecula is a northern constellation (group of stars). People say that it looks like a fox.
title: Vulpecula

text: The Vermilion Bird is one of the Four Symbols of the Chinese constellations. It represents the fire-element, the south direction, and the season summer correspondingly.
title: Vermilion Bird

text: The Black Tortoise (Chinese: 玄武; pinyin: Xuánwǔ) is one of the Four Symbols of the Chinese constellations. It is usually shown as a tortoise with a snake.
title: Black Tortoise

text: The Azure Dragon, called Qinglong in Chinese, is a Dragon God representing the forces of the Five Regions' Highest Deities. It is a part of the Chinese constellations known as the Four Symbols.
title: Azure Dragon

text: An astronomical object is any natural body that floats in space. For example, stars, planets, meteoroids, moons, and other space objects.
title: Astronomical object

text: Centaurus A or NGC 5128 is a prominent galaxy in the constellation of Centaurus. It was discovered in 1826 by Scottish astronomer James Dunlop at his home in New South Wales, Australia.
title: Centaurus A

text: Cygnus X-1 (abbreviated Cyg X-1) is a well-known galactic X-ray source. It is thought to be a black hole in the constellation Cygnus.
title: Cygnus X-1

text: Eta Carinae (η Carinae or η Car) is a superbright hypergiant star in the constellation Carina, about 7,500 to 8,000 light-years from the Sun.
title: Eta Carinae

text: Halley's Comet (Comet Halley) is a comet which comes round every 75 or 76 years. When it is near, it can be seen with the naked eye.
title: Halley's Comet

text: The Hyades (also known as Melotte 25 or Collinder 50) is the nearest open star cluster to the Solar System and one of the best-studied of all star clusters.
title: Hyades (star cluster)

text: Messier 87 (also known as M87, Virgo A or NGC 4486) is a supergiant elliptical galaxy. It was discovered in 1781 by the French astronomer Charles Messier, who catalogued it as a nebulous feature.
title: Messier 87

text: Mira is a binary star system with a white dwarf (Mira B, also known as VZ Ceti) star and a red giant (Mira A). Scientists think Mira is 200-400 light years away in the constellation Cetus.
title: Mira

text: Omega Centauri (ω Cen or NGC 5139) is a globular cluster in the constellation of Centaurus. It is 15,800 light-years (4,850 pc) away, and is the largest globular cluster in the Milky Way.
title: Omega Centauri

text: The Orion Nebula, or Messier 42, M42, or NGC 1976, is a diffuse nebula. It is visible to the naked eye in the night sky.
title: Orion nebula

text: The Pleiades (also known as M45 or the Seven Sisters) are a group of stars in the night sky. You can see them in the constellation Taurus, the bull.
title: Pleiades

text: Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*) is a bright astronomical radio source at the center of the Milky Way. It is in the direction of the constellations Sagittarius and Scorpius.
title: Sagittarius A*

text: A geosynchronous orbit is an orbit at a height of 35,786 km (22,000 mi) above sea level on the Earth. At this height, the orbit takes 24 hours, so it is in sync with the land on Earth (the 'geo' part of geosynchronous).
title: Geosynchronous orbit

text: The Local Group is the group of galaxies that includes our galaxy, the Milky Way.
title: Local Group

text: The Magellanic Clouds are two irregular, dwarf galaxies. They do not have a regular shape, and only have a few billion stars.
title: Magellanic Clouds

text: The Andromeda Galaxy is the nearest spiral galaxy to the Milky Way, our galaxy. Andromeda is sometimes called Messier 31, M31 or NGC 224 by astronomers.
title: Andromeda galaxy

text: The Triangulum galaxy is a spiral galaxy approximately 3 million light years (ly) from Earth in the constellation Triangulum.
title: Triangulum galaxy

text: Deimos (or Mars II) is the smaller moon of Mars. Its name comes from the Greek word for terror.
title: Deimos (moon)

text: Phobos (or Mars I) is one of Mars' moons. The other is Deimos.
title: Phobos (moon)

text: The asteroid belt or main belt is a ring of small and large rocks and dust between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter. The biggest object in the asteroid belt is Ceres, a dwarf planet.
title: Asteroid belt

text: Ceres, also known as 1 Ceres (symbol: ), is the smallest dwarf planet in the Solar System and the only one in the main asteroid belt.
title: Ceres (dwarf planet)

text: Io is a moon of the planet Jupiter. It is Jupiter's third biggest moon with a diameter of 3642 km, slightly bigger than Earth's moon.
title: Io (moon)

text: Europa is a large moon of the planet Jupiter. It is a little smaller than Earth's Moon and it is the sixth-largest moon in the Solar System.
title: Europa (moon)

text: Callisto is a moon of the planet Jupiter. It was discovered in 1610 by Galileo Galilei and named after Kallisto.
title: Callisto (moon)

text: Enceladus is a moon of Saturn. It is the sixth largest of Saturn's moons, and it has a diameter of 500 km.
title: Enceladus (moon)

text: Titan (Ancient Greek: Τῑτάν) is Saturn's moon. It was found by Christiaan Huygens on 25 March 1655.
title: Titan (moon)

text: Triton, or Neptune I, is the largest moon of the planet Neptune. It is the seventh-largest moon in the Solar System.
title: Triton (moon)

text: Charon is a moon of the dwarf planet Pluto. It is half as wide as Pluto and is much like the dwarf planet itself.
title: Charon (moon)

text: Eris (symbol ) is a dwarf planet and a trans-Neptunian object (TNO). It is the second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
title: Eris (dwarf planet)

text: Makemake (symbol ); officially known as 136472 Makemake) is a dwarf planet. It was discovered on March 31, 2005 by astronomers Michael E. Brown, Chad Trujillo and David Rabinowitz.
title: Makemake (dwarf planet)

text: 136108 Haumea (symbol ) is a dwarf planet in the Solar System. Its discovery was announced in 2005 by astronomers Michael E. Brown, Chad Trujillo and David Rabinowitz of the United States, and J. L. Ortiz of Spain.
title: Haumea (dwarf planet)

text: 90377 Sedna (or simply Sedna; symbol ) is a trans-Neptunian object which is the farthest dwarf planet from the Sun. It was discovered on November 14, 2003 by Mike Brown, Chad Trujillo and David Rabinowitz.
title: 90377 Sedna

text: The Kuiper belt is an area of the Solar System beyond the orbit of Neptune (at 30 astronomical units) to 50 AU from the Sun.
title: Kuiper belt

text: The Oort cloud, Oort's cloud, or Öpik–Oort cloud, is a cloud of comets and other objects. Astronomers believe it is way beyond the orbits of Pluto and the Kuiper belt.
title: Oort cloud

text: PSR B1257+12 B is an extrasolar planet in the constellation of Virgo. It is around 980 light years away from Earth.
title: PSR B1257+12 B

text: 51 Pegasi b, also called Bellerephon, Dimidium or 51 Peg b, is the first extrasolar planet discovered orbiting a main-sequence star, 51 Pegasi. Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz announced the discovery on 6 October 1995.
title: 51 Pegasi b

text: Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky. It is a binary star system in Canis Major, near Orion.
title: Sirius

text: Canopus, or Alpha Carinae in the Bayer designation system, is the brightest star in its constellation (Carina) and the brightest star in the southern night sky.
title: Canopus

text: Arcturus (or α Boo, α Boötis, Alpha Boötis) of the constellation Boötes is the brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere. With an apparent magnitude of −0.04, it is the fourth brightest star in the night sky, after −1.46 magnitude Sirius, −0.86 magnitude Canopus, and −0.27 magnitude Alpha Centauri.
title: Arcturus

text: Alpha Centauri (also known as Rigil Kentaurus) is the brightest star in the southern Centaurus constellation. It is the fourth brightest star in the night sky, with a magnitude of -0.01.
title: Alpha Centauri

text: Vega (α Lyr, α Lyrae, Alpha Lyrae) is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra. It is the fifth brightest star in the night sky and the second brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere, after Arcturus.
title: Vega

text: Rigel is a hot supergiant star in the Milky Way galaxy. It is a blue-white supergiant.
title: Rigel

text: Procyon (α CMi, α Canis Minoris, Alpha Canis Minoris) is the brightest star in the constellation Canis Minor. To the naked eye, it appears to be a single star, the eighth brightest in the night sky with a visual apparent magnitude of 0.34.
title: Procyon

text: Achernar is the name of the primary (or 'A') component of the binary system designated Alpha Eridani (α Eridani).
title: Achernar

text: Betelgeuse (from Arabic: إبط الجوزاء Ibṭ al-Jauzā’, meaning "the armpit of Orion") is a large red supergiant star in the Orion constellation. It is usually the ninth-brightest star in the night sky, and the second-brightest in Orion.
title: Betelgeuse

text: Capella (α Aurigae, α Aur, Alpha Aurigae) is the brightest star in the constellation Auriga, the eleventh brightest star in the night sky and the third brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere, after Arcturus and Vega.
title: Capella

text: Altair, also called α Aquilae, α Aql, is the brightest star in the constellation of Aquila.
title: Altair

text: Aldebaran (α Tau, α Tauri, Alpha Tauri) is an orange giant star. It is about 65 light years away in the zodiac constellation of Taurus.
title: Aldebaran

text: Spica is a blue main-sequence star that is the brightest star in the constellation Virgo. It is more than 7 times larger than the Sun.
title: Spica

text: Antares (α Scorpii, Alpha Scorpii) is a red supergiant star in the Milky Way galaxy and the sixteenth brightest star in the nighttime sky. It is listed as 15th or 16th brightest, depending on how the two brighter components of the Capella quadruple star system are counted.
title: Antares

text: Pollux is a red giant star. It is the brightest star in the Gemini constellation.
title: Pollux (star)

text: Fomalhaut is the brightest star in the southern constellation of Piscis Austrinus, the "Southern Fish". It is one of the brightest stars in the night sky.
title: Fomalhaut

text: Deneb (also named Arided, α Cygni, alpha Cygni, α Cyg) is the brightest star in the constellation of Cygnus. It, along with Vega, and Altair make up the Summer Triangle asterism.
title: Deneb

text: RR Lyrae is a pulsating variable star in the constellation Lyra. It is the model for the variable stars known as RR Lyrae variables.
title: RR Lyrae

text: Beta Centauri (β Centauri, β Cen, Agena, or Hadar), is a triple star system in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
title: Beta Centauri

text: Algol, also known as the Demon Star, is a bright star in the Perseus constellation. It is one of the best known double stars that can only be seen in spectroscopes, the first star of its type discovered, and one of the first variable stars to be discovered before it explodes.
title: Algol

text: Delta Cephei (δ Cep, δ Cephei) is a binary star system about 887 light-years away in the northern constellation of Cepheus, the King. At this distance, the apparent magnitude of the star is reduced by 0.23 as a result of gas and dust along the line of sight.
title: Delta Cephei

text: Polaris (Alpha Ursae Minoris) is the Pole Star or North Star.
title: Polaris (star)

text: 3C 273 is a quasar located about 2 and a half billion light years away in the constellation of Virgo. It is the brightest quasar in the night sky, as well as the first to be discovered.
title: 3C 273

text: The Crab Nebula (catalogue designations M1, NGC 1952, Taurus A) is a supernova remnant and 'pulsar wind nebula' in the constellation of Taurus. The nebula was observed by John Bevis in 1731; it corresponds to a bright supernova recorded by Chinese and Islamic astronomers in 1054.
title: Crab Nebula

text: The Schwarzschild radius (sometimes erroneously referred to as the gravitational radius), is the radius of a sphere that has certain properties: If all the mass of an object is compressed within this sphere, the escape speed from the surface of the sphere would equal the speed of light.
title: Schwarzschild radius

text: A supermassive black hole (SMBH or less often SBH) is a black hole with a mass that is between 105 and 1010 the mass of the Sun. Scientists are confident that almost all galaxies, including the Milky Way, have a supermassive black hole at each of their centers.
title: Supermassive black hole

text: Cosmic rays are very high-energy radiation, mostly from outside the Solar System.
title: Cosmic ray

text: Dark nebulae are astronomical objects. They do not emit or reflect light.
title: Dark nebula

text: Galaxy clusters are large collections of galaxies. They consist of hundreds of galaxies and galaxy groups, bound together by gravity.
title: Galaxy cluster

text: A galaxy group is a group of galaxies made up of less than 50 or so members and bound by gravity. Collections of galaxies larger than groups are called galaxy clusters or superclusters.
title: Galaxy group

text: Superclusters are large collections of smaller galaxy groups and galaxy clusters. They are one of the largest known structures in the cosmos.
title: Supercluster

text: An H II region is a region where huge blue stars are formed from hydrogen. They are named after the ionised atomic hydrogen which they produce: H II.
title: H II region

text: In astronomy, the interstellar medium (sometimes called the ISM) is the tenuous gas and dust that fills the void between stellar systems in galaxies, that consisting mainly of huge clouds of ionized, neutral, or molecular hydrogen.
title: Interstellar medium

text: A molecular cloud is a kind of cloud in space. It has enough density and size so that molecules can form, usually molecules of hydrogen (H2).
title: Molecular cloud

text: A nebula is an interstellar cloud of dust, hydrogen, helium and other ionized gases in a galaxy.
title: Nebula

text: Outer space, commonly shortened to space, is the near-vacuum between celestial bodies. It is where all of the planets, stars, galaxies and objects are found.
title: Outer space

text: The solar wind is a stream of charged particles from the Sun. It is made of charged protons, electrons and plasma shot out of the Sun, and creates the heliosphere.
title: Solar wind

text: A star cluster is a group of stars. They are held together by mutual gravitation.
title: Star cluster

text: A globular cluster is a group of stars of a similar age which orbits the central bulge of a galaxy. Gravity holds clusters together and gives them their spherical shape.
title: Globular cluster

text: An open star cluster, also known as galactic cluster, is a group of a few hundred or thousand stars. They have roughly the same age, and were formed from the same giant molecular cloud.
title: Open star cluster

text: A stellar association is a loose star cluster, looser than both open clusters and globular clusters. Stellar associations usually have from 10 to 100 or more stars.
title: Stellar association

text: Galaxy morphological classification is a system used by astronomers to divide galaxies into groups based on how they look.
title: Galaxy morphological classification

text: A dwarf galaxy is a small galaxy composed of up to several billion stars. This is a small number compared to our own Milky Way's 200–400 billion stars.
title: Dwarf galaxy

text: An elliptical galaxy is a galaxy having an ellipsoidal shape, and a smooth, nearly featureless brightness profile. They are one of the three main types of galaxy originally described by Edwin Hubble in 1936.
title: Elliptical galaxy

text: An irregular galaxy is a galaxy that does not have a distinct regular shape, like a spiral or an elliptical galaxy.
title: Irregular galaxy

text: A lenticular galaxy is a type of galaxy. These galaxies have an elliptical shape and ill-defined spiral arms.
title: Lenticular galaxy

text: A spiral galaxy is a kind of galaxy that looks like a flat, slowly rotating disk with a bulge in the centre, and spiral patterns extending outward from the bulge. It contains stars, gas, dust, dark matter and a supermassive black hole at its centre.
title: Spiral galaxy

text: An active galactic nucleus (AGN) is a compact region at the centre of a galaxy. This central region radiates huge luminosity over the electromagnetic spectrum.
title: Active galactic nucleus

text: A blazar is a very compact quasar (quasi-stellar radio source). They have a presumed supermassive black hole at the center of an active, giant elliptical galaxy.
title: Blazar

text: Quasars or quasi-stellar radio sources are the most energetic and distant active galactic nuclei (AGN).
title: Quasar

text: Radio galaxies and their relatives, radio-loud quasars and blazars, are types of active galaxy that are very luminous at radio wavelengths. They have luminosities up to 1039 W between 10 MHz and 100 GHz.
title: Radio galaxy

text: Seyfert galaxies are a type of galaxy. They are named after Carl Seyfert who first described them in 1943.
title: Seyfert galaxy

text: A starburst galaxy is a galaxy with a very high rate of star formation. The rate of star formation is so large that the galaxy will quickly use all of its gas reservoir (from which the stars are made).
title: Starburst galaxy

text: Cosmology is the branch of astronomy that deals with the universe.
title: Cosmology

text: In cosmology, the age of the universe is the amount of time since the Big Bang. The best measurement of the age of the Universe is 13.8 billion years (specifically, 13.798±0.037 billion years).
title: Age of the universe

text: Cosmic microwave background radiation (CMB radiation) is radiation in the microwave part of the electromagnetic spectrum, which comes from all directions in outer space. It is known to come from our earliest infant universe.
title: Cosmic microwave background radiation

text: Dark energy is the name given to the force that is believed to accelerate the expansion of the universe. Distant galaxies appear to be moving away from us at high speed: the idea is that the universe is getting bigger and has been since the Big Bang.
title: Dark energy

text: Dark matter is a type of matter thought to be responsible for much of the mass in the universe.
title: Dark matter

text: The formation and evolution of the Solar System describes how the Solar System began, and how it changed.
title: Formation and evolution of the Solar System

text: The solar nebula theory explains that the sun and planets formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a massive, rotating cloud of gas and dust called a solar nebula. As gravity caused the cloud to collapse, it spun faster and flattened into a disk, concentrating most of its mass at the center to create the sun.
title: Solar nebula theory

text: Red shift is a method astronomers use to tell the speed of any object that is very far away in the Universe. The red shift is one example of the Doppler effect.
title: Red shift

text: In Big Bang cosmology, the observable universe is what, in theory, can be seen from Earth. That is light, or other signals, which has had time to reach the Earth since the beginning of the cosmological expansion.
title: Observable universe

text: A wormhole is a theoretical passage through space creating a shortcut through time and space. It is not known whether or not they exist.
title: Wormhole

text: A brown dwarf is an object which is made of the same stuff as stars, but does not have enough mass for hydrogen fusion (combining hydrogen atoms into helium atoms). Hydrogen fusion is what makes stars glow.
title: Brown dwarf

text: A habitable zone (HZ) in astronomy is a region of space where conditions are best for life to form as on Earth. Planets in these areas are the most likely to have extraterrestrial life.
title: Habitable zone

text: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are flashes of gamma rays from extremely energetic explosions. They have been seen in distant galaxies.
title: Gamma-ray burst

text: The Hertzsprung-Russell diagram is a graph of many stars. It shows the relation between stars' luminosity (how bright they are) and their temperature (how hot they are).
title: Hertzsprung–Russell diagram

text: Metallicity is a term in astronomy. It means the amount of elements that are heavier than hydrogen and helium.
title: Metallicity

text: A Planetary system is the general term for a star with planets and other objects in orbit around it. The Solar System is one of these.
title: Planetary system

text: Stellar evolution is the study of how a star changes over time. Stars can change very much between when they are first created and when they run out of energy.
title: Stellar evolution

text: A planetary nebula is a nebula that is made up of gas and plasma. They are made by certain types of stars later in their life.
title: Planetary nebula

text: Star formation means the earliest stages in a star's life. Dense regions of particles exist in molecular clouds known as "stellar nurseries".
title: Star formation

text: The main sequence is a region on a Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram where most stars appear. Any star that is plotted in that area is a main-sequence star.
title: Main sequence

text: Protostar is an early stage in the evolution of a star that usually grows to the point of beginning nuclear fusion and becoming a star by gathering mass. It is made of a contracting cloud of cold and dark interstellar medium (mostly hydrogen gas).
title: Protostar

text: A red giant is a giant star that has the mass of about one-half to ten times the mass of our Sun. Red giants get their name because they appear to be colored red and they are very large.
title: Red giant

text: A giant star is a star with much larger radius and luminosity than a main-sequence star of the same surface temperature.
title: Giant star

text: Supergiants are some of the largest stars in the universe. They are larger than giant stars, and less luminous than hypergiants.
title: Supergiant

text: Wolf–Rayet stars (WR stars) are massive stars (over 20 solar masses initially). They are losing mass rapidly by means of a very strong stellar wind, with speeds up to 2000 km/s.
title: Wolf–Rayet star

text: In astronomy, the term compact star or compact object is used to refer collectively to white dwarfs, neutron stars, other exotic dense stars, and black holes.
title: Compact star

text: A white dwarf is a compact star. Their matter is squashed together.
title: White dwarf

text: A neutron star is a very small and dense star made almost completely of neutrons. They are small stars with a radius of about 11–11.5 kilometres.
title: Neutron star

text: A stellar black hole (or stellar-mass black hole) is a type of black hole formed by the gravitational collapse of a star.
title: Stellar black hole

text: Stellar nucleosynthesis is the creation (nucleosynthesis) of chemical elements by nuclear fusion reactions in stars. This fusion reaction also creates the stars' light and heat.
title: Stellar nucleosynthesis

text: A star system or stellar system is a small number of stars which orbit each other, bound by gravitational attraction.
title: Star system

text: A binary star is two stars which orbit around each other. For each star, the other is its companion star.
title: Binary star

text: A circumstellar disc (or circumstellar disk) is a torus pancake or ring-shaped accumulation of matter that composed of gas, dust, planetesimals, asteroids or collision fragments in Orbit around a star.
title: Circumstellar disc

text: A variable star is a star that is sometimes brighter or dimmer. Most stars have only very small differences in brightness, like the Sun; but some stars can vary hugely such as Mira Variables.
title: Variable star

text: Cepheids are a type of very luminous variable stars. There is a strong direct relationship between a Cepheid's luminosity and its pulsation period.
title: Cepheid variable

text: A nova (plural novae or novas) is a huge nuclear explosion on a white dwarf star. It causes a sudden brightening of the star.
title: Nova

text: Pulsars are neutron stars which spin rapidly and produce huge electromagnetic radiation along a narrow beam. Neutron stars are very dense, and have short, regular spins.
title: Pulsar

text: A supernova is the explosion of a giant star. It usually happens when the nuclear fusion in the star cannot hold the core against its own gravity.
title: Supernova

text: Celestial mechanics is a part of astronomy that looks at the movement of the objects in the sky, and tries to find models to describe and explain these movements. The objects described include stars and planets, and also comets, and other similar objects.
title: Celestial mechanics

text: An eclipse is an astronomical event. It is when one object in the sky moves into the shadow of another such object.
title: Eclipse

text: A lunar eclipse is an astronomical phenomenon. It happens when the moon passes through the shadow of the Earth.
title: Lunar eclipse

text: As seen from earth, a solar eclipse /ee-klips/ happens when the moon is directly between the earth and the sun. This makes the moon fully or partially (partly) cover the sun.
title: Solar eclipse

text: An ephemeris is a table giving the predicted positions of an object in space, like another planet, comet, or asteroid.
title: Ephemeris

text: In astronomy, an epoch (or sometimes epochal moment) is a moment in time for which the position or the orbital elements of a celestial body are specified.
title: Epoch (astronomy)

text: Escape speed is the initial speed that something would need to completely escape the gravity of a large body, like a star or a planet (such as the Earth), by mere inertia.
title: Escape speed

text: A gravitational slingshot, gravity assist maneuver or swing-by is the use of the relative movement and gravity of a planet to alter the path and speed of a spacecraft. This helps the spacecraft to save fuel, time, and expense.
title: Gravity assist

text: Lagrange points are stable positions near large bodies in orbit. When two large bodies are in orbit around each other, there are places that a third body can occupy.
title: Lagrange point

text: A natural satellite, also called a moon, in astronomy is a smaller body which moves around a larger body. The smaller body is held in orbit by gravitation.
title: Natural satellite

text: A geostationary orbit (or Geostationary Earth Orbit - GEO) is a type of geosynchronous orbit directly above the Earth's equator (0° latitude). Like all geosynchronous orbits, it has a period (time for one orbit) that is 24 hours.
title: Geostationary orbit

text: A low Earth orbit (LEO) is usually described as an orbit inside the area which comes from the Earth’s surface up to an altitude of 2,000 kilometres (1,200 miles). Other definitions use other numbers such as orbital eccentricity and orbital period.
title: Low Earth orbit

text: In astrodynamics, orbital eccentricity shows how much the shape of an object's orbit is different from a circle.
title: Orbital eccentricity

text: Astrodynamics is a part of physics that deals with movement in space. It is a branch of mechanics dealing with orbits.
title: Astrodynamics

text: An occultation is an event that occurs when one object is hidden by another object that passes between it and the observer. A planet, for example, can pass in front of a star.
title: Occultation

text: The two-body problem is a problem from classical mechanics: there are two bodies which influence each other. Very often they attract or repel each other.
title: Two-body problem

text: A Global Positioning System, also known as GPS, is a system of satellites designed to help navigate on the Earth, in the air, and on water.
title: Global Positioning System

text: A satellite navigation or satnav system is a way of pinpointing position very exactly.
title: Satellite navigation

text: Sidereal time is a time-keeping system. It is used by astronomers to find celestial objects.
title: Sidereal time

text: An atomic clock is a clock that works with energy level of atoms, as opposed to most other clocks which are mechanical. The frequency comes from the crossing radiation of electrons.
title: Atomic clock

text: A sextant is an object used for navigation which measures angles. The user is able to measure the angle between the horizon and an object in the sky, such as the sun, a star, or a planet.
title: Sextant

text: Matter means objects which have mass even when not moving, which is a form of energy that matter has even when it is not moving.
title: Matter

text: In physics, radiation is the emission or transmission of energy in the form of waves or particles through space or through a material medium.
title: Radiation

text: Spacetime or space–time is a mathematical model that joins space and time into a single idea called a continuum. This four-dimensional continuum is known as Minkowski space.
title: Spacetime

text: The Planck time is the length of time at which no smaller meaningful length can be validly measured due to the indeterminacy expressed in Werner Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle.
title: Planck time

text: The Planck units are physical units of measurement. The system of these units was first developed by Max Planck.
title: Planck units

text: The theory of relativity is a theory Albert Einstein created in the early 1900s. There are two theories of relativity.
title: Theory of relativity

text: The Michelson–Morley experiment was a scientific experiment to test for the presence and properties of a substance called aether. This was thought hypothetically to fill empty space.
title: Michelson–Morley experiment

text: In physics, a physical quantity is any physical property that can be quantified, that is, be measured using numbers. Examples of physical quantities are mass, amount of substance, length, time, temperature, electric current, light intensity, force, velocity, density, and many others.
title: Physical quantity

text: Schrödinger's cat is a thought experiment about quantum physics. Erwin Schrödinger suggested it in 1935, in reaction to the Copenhagen interpretation of quantum physics.
title: Schrödinger's cat

text: Time travel is the idea of going back in time to the past or forward to the future. We always travel forward, to the future.
title: Time travel

text: Quantum entanglement is the name given to a special connection between pairs or groups of quantum systems, or any objects described by quantum mechanics. Quantum entanglement is one of the biggest parts of quantum mechanics that makes it hard to understand in terms of the everyday world.
title: Quantum entanglement

text: The Uncertainty principle is also called the Heisenberg's uncertainty principle. In 1927, Werner Heisenberg discovered that nothing has a definite position, a definite trajectory, or a definite momentum.Trying to pin a thing down to one definite position will make its momentum less well understood, and vice-versa.
title: Uncertainty principle

text: The Schrödinger equation is a differential equation (a type of equation that involves an unknown function rather than an unknown number) that forms the basis of quantum mechanics, one of the most accurate theories of how subatomic particles behave.
title: Schrödinger equation

text: In quantum mechanics, the Wave function, usually represented by Ψ, or ψ, describes the probability of finding an electron somewhere in its matter wave.
title: Wave function

text: Wave–particle duality is a concept in physics. It's the idea that there are things that are both waves and particles.
title: Wave–particle duality

text: Mechanics is a branch of physics which looks at objects that are moved by forces (including other bodies, or forces of nature). A person working in this discipline is known as a mechanician.
title: Mechanics

text: In physics, a frame of reference, or reference frame, is a perspective that one uses to determine if an object is moving. A frame of reference consists of an object or environment that is considered to be stationary.
title: Frame of reference

text: 'Inertia is the resistance of the object to any change in its motion, including a change in direction. An object will stay still or keep moving at the same speed and in a straight line, unless it is acted upon by an external unbalanced force.
title: Inertia

text: Moment of inertia (I), also called "angular mass" (kg·m2), is a body's resistance to angular acceleration or deceleration, equal to the product of the mass and the square of its radius measured perpendicularly to the axis of rotation.
title: Moment of inertia

text: Perpetual motion refers to a movement that goes on forever once started without additional energy added. A machine that could be set in motion once would continue to move forever.
title: Perpetual motion

text: Kinematics is the branch of classical mechanics which describes the motion of points, bodies, or objects, and systems of bodies, or groups of objects, without looking at the cause of this motion.
title: Kinematics

text: Kinetic energy is the energy that an object has because of its motion. This energy can be converted into other kinds, such as gravitational or electric potential energy. which is the energy that an object has because of its position in a gravitational or electric field.
title: Kinetic energy

text: Potential energy is the stored or pent-up energy of an object. It is often contrasted with kinetic energy.
title: Potential energy

text: Density is a measurement that compares the amount of matter an object has to its volume. An object with much matter in a certain volume has high density.
title: Density

text: A gyroscope is a device used to measure or maintain an angular position. It works using the principles of angular momentum.
title: Gyroscope

text: Movement, or motion, is the state of changing something's position or changing where something is. A bird that is flying is moving.
title: Movement

text: Isaac Newton (1642–1727) is widely known as the father of dynamics, the study of motion. He developed three laws that are the foundation of classical mechanics.
title: Newton's laws of motion

text: Free fall is what happens when an object is let to fall on its own without propulsion or resistance. Someone who is standing is not in free fall, but someone jumping from an aeroplane is, until air resistance builds up, ending in terminal velocity.
title: Free fall

text: Rotation is the movement of an object in a circular motion.
title: Rotation

text: Centrifugal force is a force that acts on a body in a direction away from the centre, which contributes to making the body try to fly away. When you hold a rope with a heavy object attached to it, and rotate it around, the rope becomes tight and keeps the body from flying away.
title: Centrifugal force

text: Centripetal acceleration is a force that acts on a body that revolves around a centre of a circular path. This force keeps the body in circular motion.
title: Centripetal force

text: The Coriolis effect is a force that is found in a rotating object. Gaspard Gustave de Coriolis first described the Coriolis effect in 1835 using mathematics.
title: Coriolis effect

text: Newton's universal law of gravitation is a physical law that describes the attraction between two objects with mass. Sir Isaac Newton talked about it in his book Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica.
title: Newton's law of universal gravitation

text: In physics, torque is the tendency of a force to turn or twist. If a force is used to begin to spin an object, or to stop an object from spinning, a torque is made.
title: Torque

text: The weight of an object (or the weight of an amount of matter) is the measure of the intensity of the force imposed on this object by the local gravitational field. Weight should not be confused with the related but quite different concept of mass.
title: Weight

text: The Lorentz contraction, also called Length contraction, Fitzgerald contraction or Lorenz-Fitzgerald contraction, is the phenomenon that a moving object becomes shorter than it was when measured in its rest frame. This is because of relativistic effects seen between observers moving toward or away from one another.
title: Lorentz contraction

text: Solid mechanics is the branch of mechanics, physics, and mathematics that concerns itself with how solid matter under external actions works (such as external forces, temperature changes, applied displacements, etc.). It is part of a larger study known as continuum mechanics.
title: Solid mechanics

text: The strength of materials is the ability of materials to resist force. That ability is an important topic in mechanical engineering.
title: Strength of materials

text: Stress is the force per unit area on a body that tends to cause it to change shape.
title: Stress (mechanics)

text: Friction is a force that acts to stop the movement of two touching things. The energy lost to friction is turned into sound and heat.
title: Friction

text: An elastic modulus, or modulus of elasticity, is the mathematical description of an object or substance's tendency to be deformed elastically (i.e. non-permanently) when a force is applied to it.
title: Elastic modulus

text: It is a law of mechanics and physics discovered by Robert Hooke.
title: Hooke's law

text: Plasticity, or plastic deformation, is the ability of a solid material to have a permanent change in shape. In physics and materials science, this is called deformation.
title: Plasticity (physics)

text: The butterfly effect is an idea from chaos theory. A small change can sometimes make much bigger changes happen.
title: Butterfly effect

text: In physics, the angular velocity specifies the angular speed at which an object is rotating along with the direction in which it is rotating.
title: Angular velocity

text: Dynamics is the study of forces and their effects on motion over time. It is a branch of classical mechanics.
title: Dynamics

text: The Foucault pendulum, or Foucault's pendulum (named after the French physicist Léon Foucault) was a pendulum created as an experiment to show the rotation of the Earth.
title: Foucault pendulum

text: An altimeter is an tool that can measure the height of an object, above a reference plane. A common reference plane is meters above sea level.
title: Altimeter

text: A sensor is a device that measures a physical quantity and converts it into a 'signal' which can be read by an observer or by an instrument. For example, a mercury thermometer converts the measured temperature into the expansion and contraction of a liquid which can be read on a calibrated glass tube.
title: Sensor

text: A spectrometer is an optical instrument used to measure properties of light over a specific portion of the electromagnetic spectrum.
title: Spectrometer

text: A theodolite is a tool for measuring angles between two places (or points) from one place. They are usually associated with surveying.
title: Theodolite

text: Units of measurement give standards so that the numbers from our measurements refer to the same thing. Measurement is a process that uses numbers to describe a physical quantity.
title: Unit of measurement

text: The metric system is a number of different systems of measurement with length based on the metre, mass on the gram, and volume on the litre. This system is used around the world.
title: Metric system

text: Metrology is the study of Measurements. It starts a common understanding of units for human uses.
title: Metrology

text: A ruler (or 'rule') is an instrument of measurement. Rulers measure length.
title: Ruler

text: A pendulum is a mass (any object usually metal) on an arm. The arm is attached to a pivot, which is a point to swing from.
title: Pendulum

text: The square meter is the SI-derived unit of area. It has a symbol m² (33A1 in Unicode).
title: Square meter

text: For the state in Brazil, see Acre (state).
title: Acre

text: The hectare (symbol: ha) is a unit of measurement of area. It is equal to 10,000 square metres, or a square with sides of 100 by 100 metres.
title: Hectare

text: An angstrom or ångström (symbol Å) is a unit of length that equals 0.1 nanometer (nm). It can be written in scientific notation as 1×10−10 m (normalized notation) or 1 E-10 m (exponential notation) — both mean 1/10,000,000,000 meters.
title: Angstrom

text: The foot is a unit for measuring length. It is one of the Imperial units and US customary units.
title: Foot (unit)

text: The inch is a unit of length in the Imperial system and the United States customary system. The abbreviation for inches is in or ".
title: Inch

text: The mile (symbol: mi) is a unit of length. There are many different kinds of mile but mile on its own usually means the statute mile.
title: Mile

text: The yard (symbol: yd) is a unit of length in the Imperial System and United States Customary Units.
title: Yard

text: A minute is a customary unit of time. It is equal to 60 seconds.
title: Minute

text: The hour (symbol: h) is a unit of measurement used to measure time. The hour is equal to sixty minutes.
title: Hour

text: A week is 7 days in connecting order. There are usually 52 weeks in a year.
title: Week

text: A month is an amount of time used with calendars. It is about 1/12th of a year.
title: Month

text: A decade (pronunciation: DEK-aid) is a period of 10 years. The word comes from the Ancient Greek word deka ("ten").
title: Decade

text: A millennium (plural: millennia) is a time period of one thousand (1000) years. The word millennium is derived from two Latin words mille ("thousand") and annum ("year").
title: Millennium

text: A gallon is a volumetric unit of measurement. People have used many different gallons throughout history.
title: Gallon

text: The standard atmosphere (symbol: atm) is a unit of atmospheric pressure. It refers to the air pressure at sea level and is defined as equal to 101,325 Pa.
title: Atmosphere (unit)

text: The newton (symbol: N) is the SI unit of force. It is named after Sir Isaac Newton because of his work on classical mechanics.
title: Newton (unit)

text: The pascal (symbol: Pa) is the SI-derived unit of pressure or stress. It is a measure of perpendicular force per unit area and is equal to one newton per square meter.
title: Pascal (unit)

text: The tonne or metric ton (symbol: t) is a unit of measurement for mass. It is equal to one thousand kilograms, or one megagram (one million grams).
title: Metric ton

text: A pound (usually abbreviated as lb, plural lbs) is a unit used to measure the mass of something. It is used in the imperial system and the United States customary system.
title: Pound (mass)

text: The ounce (abbreviated: oz, the old Italian word onza, now spelled oncia) is a unit of mass or of weight in a number of different systems, including various systems of mass that form part of the imperial and United States customary systems. Its size can vary from system to system.
title: Ounce

text: A knot is a unit of speed. It is abbreviated kt or kn.
title: Knot (speed)

text: Hydraulics is a topic of science and engineering subject dealing with the mechanical properties of liquids. Many machines work on hydraulic power.
title: Hydraulics

text: Rheology is the study of the flow of liquids and soft solids like mud or blood. Rheo means flow in Greek.
title: Rheology

text: Bernoulli's principle is an idea of fluid dynamics. It says that as speed of the fluid increases, pressure decreases.
title: Bernoulli's principle

text: In physics, buoyancy (lit: float force) (pronounced /ˈbɔɪ.ənsi/) is a force on an object making that object rise or move upward. It comes from the Spanish word for "float", boyar.
title: Buoyancy

text: Convection is the movement of heat because of the movement of warm matter. Convection is defined as the method of heat transfer through a fluid from places of higher temperature to lower temperature by the movement of the molecules due to their different densities.
title: Convection

text: Diffusion is a process where molecules of a material move from an area of high concentration (where there are many molecules) to an area of low concentration (where there are fewer molecules)until it has reached equilibrium (molecules evenly spread).
title: Diffusion

text: Fluid dynamics is the motion of fluids (liquids and gases). It is one of the oldest studies of physics.
title: Fluid dynamics

text: Fluid statics (also called hydrostatics) is the science of fluids at rest, and is a sub-field within fluid mechanics. The term usually refers to the mathematical treatment of the subject.
title: Fluid statics

text: The Navier–Stokes equations are kinds of partial differential equations, mathematical equations that describe the motion of fluids. The equations are named after Claude-Louis Navier and George Gabriel Stokes.
title: Navier–Stokes equations

text: Surface tension is an effect where the surface of a liquid is strong. The surface can hold up a weight, and the surface of a water droplet holds the droplet together, in a ball shape.
title: Surface tension

text: Turbulence or turbulent flow is violent, unsteady, chaotic movement of fluids like air and water, and is contrasted with laminar flow.
title: Turbulence

text: Viscosity is a physical property of fluids. It shows resistance to flow.
title: Viscosity

text: Archimedes' principle is a basic idea in science that explains why things float or sink in liquids and gases. It was discovered by Archimedes, a famous Greek scientist who lived in the 3rd century BCE.
title: Archimedes' principle

text: Aerodynamics means studying how air (or gas) travels around something moving through it. Streamlining to reduce drag in vehicles is a major field in aerodynamics.
title: Aerodynamics

text: A mach number is a number that describes speed. It is a measure of the speed of an object compared to the speed of sound.
title: Mach number

text: A wave is a kind of disturbance that travels through space and matter. Wave motions transfer energy from one place to another.
title: Wave (physics)

text: Acoustics is a science. It studies the mechanical waves in gases, liquids, and solids.
title: Acoustics

text: The speed of sound is 1,235 kilometres (767 mi) per hour or 343 metres (1,125 ft) per second in dry air in room temperature. It travels at 1500 meters per second through water.
title: Speed of sound

text: Ultrasound (also called ultrasonography, computer echotomography, echography (or echotomography), and ultrasonic imaging) is a type of using sound to make images of what is under the skin (such as in pregnancy) or the blood vessels. The images are made with a frequency higher than humans can hear.
title: Ultrasound
