text: Diffraction is a physics concept which occurs when waves bend around small obstacles, or spread out after they pass through small openings. Diffraction occurs with all waves, including sound waves, water waves, and electromagnetic waves such as light that the eye can see.
title: Diffraction

text: Noise refers to unwanted sound, typically perceived by the ears. It can cause damage to hearing.
title: Noise

text: In physics, resonance is the tendency of a system to vibrate with increasing amplitudes at some frequencies of excitation. These are known as the system's resonant frequencies (or resonance frequencies).
title: Resonance

text: The Doppler effect is a change in frequency and wavelength of a wave. It is caused by the change in distance between the thing creating the wave (causer) and whatever is measuring seeing or hearing the wave (watcher or observer).
title: Doppler effect

text: A metronome is a small device that can be used by people who are practising instruments to help them to play in time. It is also something a composer can use to show the performer what speed to play.
title: Metronome

text: Oscillation is when something "vibrates", or repeats the same pattern. Many things in nature move back-and-forth or up-and down when pushed or struck.
title: Oscillation

text: The amplitude or peak amplitude of a wave is a measure of how big its oscillation is.
title: Amplitude

text: The decibel (symbol: dB) measures ratios of power or intensity. It expresses them as an exponential function.
title: Decibel

text: Sonar is a machine that uses underwater sound waves to find other objects in the sea. A sonar can work by sending out sound and listening for echoes (active sonar), like a radar, or by listening for sound made by the object it is trying to find (passive sonar).
title: Sonar

text: Optics is the science of light and how it interacts with the world. Optics explains how rainbows exist, how light reflects off mirrors, how light refracts through glass or water, and what splits light shining through a prism.
title: Optics

text: An optical illusion (also called a visual illusion) is one which shows images that differ from normal reality.
title: Optical illusion

text: The focal length tells how strongly a lens, a curved mirror or another optical device brings light together or spreads it out. If rays of light go straight into a lens and the focal length is positive, the focal length is the distance to the point behind the lens where the rays will be brought to a focus.
title: Focal length

text: In geometrical optics, a focus (also called an image point) is the point where light rays that come from a point on the object converge (come together).
title: Focus (optics)

text: A wavelength is the length of the shortest repeating part of a "sine wave". All waves can be formed by adding up sine waves.
title: Wavelength

text: Luminosity is the amount of power given off by an astronomical object.
title: Luminosity

text: The albedo of an object is the extent to which it reflects light, more specifically light which comes from the Sun. It is defined as the ratio of reflected to incident electromagnetic radiation.
title: Albedo

text: Reflection is the change in direction of a wave at a boundary between two different media, so that the wave moves back into the medium it came from.
title: Reflection (physics)

text: Refraction is the change in direction of a wave, caused by the change in the wave's speed. Examples of waves include sound waves and light waves.
title: Refraction

text: Rayleigh scattering is the way that light scatters when it hits a very small object. This theory is valid if the wavelength of the light is much bigger than the object.
title: Rayleigh scattering

text: A free-electron laser, or FEL, is a laser that produces a very bright beam of light. It is basically a super flashlight.
title: Free-electron laser

text: Photonics is the science of and technology using photons, the fundamental particle of light. The word's etymology comes from the Greek word "phos", meaning light, and the suffix "-ics", meaning 'matters relevant to'.
title: Photonics

text: Polarization (also polarisation) is a property of transverse waves. Some waves have motion in another direction as well as the direction of the wave.
title: Polarization

text: In wave physics, Dispersion is the idea that the frequency of a wave influences its velocity (speed). Dispersion is most easily seen in the refraction of light, when all the colors inside white light become separated by a prism.
title: Dispersion

text: The candela (symbol: cd) is the SI base unit of luminous intensity. It measures how bright something is.
title: Candela

text: The lumen (symbol: lm) is the SI derived unit for brightness. It is defined as 1 candela times 1 steradian.
title: Lumen (unit)

text: The first law of thermodynamics is that energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can change only from one form to another. The law forms the basis of the principle of conservation of energy.
title: First law of thermodynamics

text: The joule (symbol: J) ( or sometimes ) is a unit in the SI system named after English physicist James Prescott Joule.
title: Joule

text: The calorie is a pre-SI unit of energy, synonymous with heat. A calorie is defined as the amount of energy required to raise the temperature of one gram of water (specific heat capacity = 4,184 J kg-1 K-1) by one K (= °C + 273).
title: Calorie

text: The second law of thermodynamics says that when energy changes from one form to another form, or matter moves freely, entropy (disorder) in a closed system increases.
title: Second law of thermodynamics

text: Heat transfer is the way the heat moves from one physical system (or body) to another. Heat transfer requires a difference in temperature.
title: Heat transfer

text: In thermodynamics, the internal energy of a thermodynamic system, or a body with well-defined boundaries, denoted by U, or sometimes E, is the total of the kinetic energy due to the motion of molecules (translational, rotational, vibrational) and the potential energy associated with the vibrational and electric energy of atoms within molecules or crystals.
title: Internal energy

text: A critical point is a point on a phase diagram at which the liquid and gas phases of a substance have the same density, and so are not distinguishable from each other.
title: Critical point (thermodynamics)

text: Condensation is how gas changes into a liquid when it touches a cooler surface. Condensation is part of the water cycle.
title: Condensation

text: Evaporation is when a liquid becomes a gas without forming bubbles inside the liquid volume. If bubbles are formed we are talking instead about "boiling".
title: Evaporation

text: The triple point of any substance is the combination of temperature and pressure at which it exists in its solid, liquid, and gaseous state all at once, in equilibrium.
title: Triple point

text: Heat, or thermal energy, is the sum of the kinetic energy of atoms or molecules. In thermodynamics, heat means energy which is moved between two things when one of them has a higher temperature than the other.
title: Heat

text: Heat capacity is a measure of how much materials can store up heat as they change temperature.
title: Heat capacity

text: Thermal conductivity is the ability of a material to conduct heat. Metals are good at heat conduction.
title: Thermal conductivity

text: An adiabatic process is a thermodynamic process where a fluid becomes warmer or cooler without getting heat from, or giving it to, something else. Usually the temperature instead changes because of changes in pressure.
title: Adiabatic process

text: Absolute zero is the temperature at which the particles of matter (molecules and atoms) are at their lowest energy points. Some might think that at absolute zero particles lose all energy and stop moving.
title: Absolute zero

text: In physics, power (symbol: P) is how fast work is done. Or how quickly energy is given from one thing to another.
title: Power (physics)

text: Boiling is a process where a liquid changes into a gas or vapor when it gets hot enough. This happens at a special temperature called the boiling point.
title: Boiling

text: Freezing is the process when a liquid changes into a solid because its temperature gets colder than a certain point called the freezing point. When a liquid freezes, its molecules slow down because they lose heat energy.
title: Freezing

text: Melting is the process of changing something from a solid into a liquid (like metal into liquid metal). It is the opposite of freezing.
title: Melting

text: Sublimation is how a solid becomes a gas without becoming a liquid first. It happens when the particles of a solid absorb enough energy to completely overcome the force of attraction between them.
title: Sublimation (phase transition)

text: Brownian motion is the random motion of particles suspended in a medium (a liquid or a gas). The motion is caused by fast-moving atoms or molecules that hit the particles.
title: Brownian motion

text: The boiling point of a substance is the temperature at which the substance boils, or enters a state of rapid evaporation. For pure water this is 100° Celsius or 212° Fahrenheit, at standard pressure.
title: Boiling point

text: The melting point of a substance is the temperature at which this substance goes from the solid state to the liquid one, at a normal pressure. For water, this is 0° Celsius (32° Fahrenheit, 273.15 Kelvin).
title: Melting point

text: A thermometer is an instrument for measuring or showing temperature (how hot or cold something is). One type of thermometer is a narrow, concealed glass tube containing mercury or alcohol which extends along the tube as it expands.
title: Thermometer

text: Celsius (more precisely, a degree Celsius), sometimes called centigrade, is a unit of measurement that is used in most countries to measure temperature. The unit was created by Anders Celsius (1701–1744), a Swedish astronomer.
title: Celsius

text: Fahrenheit (more precisely, a degree Fahrenheit) is a unit of measurement that is used to measure temperature. The conversion rate to degrees Celsius is C= 5/9 x (F − 32).
title: Fahrenheit

text: The Kelvin scale (symbol: K) is the SI unit of temperature. It is named in honour of the physicist William Thomson, the first Lord Kelvin (1824–1907).
title: Kelvin

text: In order to be able to reproduce experiments, standard conditions for temperature and pressure have been defined in different fields of science. Very often these are also called standard temperature and pressure.
title: Standard temperature and pressure

text: An ideal gas is a gas with particular characteristics.
title: Ideal gas

text: Statistical mechanics is the application of probability theory, which includes mathematical tools for dealing with large populations, to the field of mechanics, which is concerned with the motion of particles or objects when subjected to a force.
title: Statistical mechanics

text: Enthalpy is a concept used in science and engineering when heat and work need to be calculated. The name comes from the Greek word "enthalpos" (ενθαλπος), meaning "to put heat into".
title: Enthalpy

text: The entropy of an object is a measure of the amount of energy which is unavailable to do work. Entropy is also a measure of the number of possible arrangements the atoms in a system can have.
title: Entropy

text: The ideal gas law is the equation of a possible ideal gas, first made by Benoît Paul Émile Clapeyron in 1834.
title: Ideal gas law

text: Pressure means how much force something is pushing on something else with.
title: Pressure

text: Gibbs free energy is the available energy in a chemical reaction. It was calculated by Josiah Willard Gibbs.
title: Gibbs free energy

text: A thermodynamic state is the macroscopic condition of a thermodynamic system as described by its particular thermodynamic parameters.
title: Thermodynamic state

text: Enthalpy of vaporization, also called the latent heat of vaporization, is the amount of energy needed to change a liquid into a gas without changing its temperature. Think of it as the heat required to turn water into steam while keeping the temperature the same.
title: Enthalpy of vaporization

text: Vapor pressure is the pressure applied by a vapor in thermodynamic equilibrium with its condensed phases at a given temperature in a closed system. The vapor pressure shows how fast a liquid evaporates.
title: Vapor pressure

text: Boyle's law, also called the Boyle–Mariotte law, is an important rule in physics that explains how the pressure and volume of a gas are related. It says that if the temperature and amount of gas stay the same, the pressure of the gas goes up when the volume goes down, and the pressure goes down when the volume goes up.
title: Boyle's law

text: Blackbody radiation is radiation produced by heated objects, particularly from a blackbody. A blackbody is an object that absorbs all radiation (visible light, infrared light, ultraviolet light, etc.) that falls on it.
title: Blackbody radiation

text: In physics, a field means that a physical quantity is assigned to every point in space (or, more generally, spacetime). A field is seen as extending throughout a large region of space so that it influences everything.
title: Field (physics)

text: Voltage is what makes electric charges move. It is the 'push' that causes charges to move in a wire or other electrical conductor.
title: Voltage

text: For the electric plug-in hybrid concept car, see Chevrolet Volt.
title: Volt

text: There are some materials which offer some resistance to the current flow; they are not good Electrical conductors or good Electrical insulators. They are resistive materials, for example graphite, iron, and certain synthetic materials.
title: Ohm

text: The hertz (symbol: Hz) is a unit derived from time which measures frequency in the International System of Units (SI). Frequency is how often something happens.
title: Hertz

text: The farad (symbol: F) is a unit of measurement used in electronics. It is used for capacitance, which is the ability to store electric charge.
title: Farad

text: The coulomb (symbol: C) is the SI unit of electric charge. It is named after Charles-Augustin de Coulomb.
title: Coulomb

text: In physics, and electronics, the henry (symbol H) is the SI unit of inductance. It is named after Joseph Henry (1797–1878), the American scientist who discovered electromagnetic induction. (In England, Michael Faraday (1791–1867) discovered the same thing independently.
title: Henry (unit)

text: The tesla (symbol T) is the SI unit used to measure the strength of magnetic fields. Tesla can be measured in different ways; for example, one tesla is equal to one weber per square meter.
title: Tesla (unit)

text: The watt (symbol: W) is the SI unit of power. It is named in honour of the physicist James Watt (1736–1819).
title: Watt

text: The ampere (symbol: A, often shortened to amp) is the standard unit of electric current. An electric current of one ampere is one coulomb per second.
title: Ampere

text: An alternating current (AC) is an electric current of which magnitude and direction vary, unlike direct current, whose direction remains constant. This means that the direction of current flowing in a circuit is constantly being reversed back and forth.
title: Alternating current

text: Direct current (DC or "continuous current") is the flow of electricity in a single direction, from the negative to the positive terminals (potential, poles).
title: Direct current

text: Magnetic flux is a measure of the magnetic field lines passing through a surface, such as a loop of wire. The magnetic flux through a closed surface such as a sphere is always zero, because the magnetic field lines going into the closed surface are balanced by field lines coming out.
title: Magnetic flux

text: Electrical resistivity is a concept in electrical engineering. It is a measure of how much a material stops the flow of electric current through it.
title: Electrical resistivity

text: The electrical resistance of an electrical conductor is a measure of the difficulty of passing an electric current through a substance. It explains the relationship between voltage and the current.
title: Electrical resistance

text: Ohm's law says that in an electrical circuit, the current passing through a resistor is related to the voltage difference and the electrical resistance between the two sides, as long as the physical conditions and the temperature of the conductor remain constant.
title: Ohm's law

text: Electrical impedance is the amount of opposition that a circuit presents to current or voltage change.
title: Electrical impedance

text: The electron-volt or electron volt, symbol eV, is used to measure energy. It is defined as the amount of energy an electron gains after being accelerated by 1 volt of electricity.
title: Electronvolt

text: Ferromagnetism is a property of many materials like iron. They are magnets, so they are attracted to, or pulled towards other magnets.
title: Ferromagnetism

text: Magnetism is a force that attracts (pulls closer) or repels (pushes away) objects that have a magnetic material like iron inside them (magnetic objects). In simpler words, it is a property of substances which pull closer or repel other objects.
title: Magnetism

text: Magnetostatics is the study of magnetic fields in systems where the electric currents are steady (not changing with time).
title: Magnetostatics

text: The magnetic moment of a magnet is a quantity that determines the force that the magnet can exert on electric currents and the torque that a magnetic field will exert on it. A loop of electric current, a bar magnet, an electron, a molecule, and a planet all have magnetic moments.
title: Magnetic moment

text: Superfluidity is a state of matter where fluid or a liquid can act very strangely.
title: Superfluidity

text: A conductor is a material which allows electricity, heat or sound to flow through it.
title: Electrical conductor

text: In electromagnetism, a dielectric (or dielectric material or dielectric medium) is an electrical insulator that can be polarized when the insulator is in an electric field.
title: Dielectric

text: An electrical insulator is a material that does not easily allow flow of electricity through an electric current. Materials typically used to insulate include rubber, plastic and glass.
title: Insulator (electricity)

text: Electrostatics (also known as static electricity) is the branch of physics that deals with apparently stationary electric charges.
title: Electrostatics

text: Electric charge is a basic property of electrons, protons and other subatomic particles. Electrons are negatively charged while protons are positively charged.
title: Electric charge

text: Coulomb's law is a formula developed in the 1780s by physicist Charles-Augustin de Coulomb. It explains how strong the force will be between two electrostatic charges.
title: Coulomb's law

text: Gauss's law (or Gauss's flux theorem) is a law of physics. The law is about the relationship between electric charge and the resulting electric field.
title: Gauss's law

text: Electric potential is electric potential energy (EPE) per unit of charge. (The unit of energy is the joule and the unit of charge is the coulomb.) Electric potential tells what the electric potential energy of a charged object will be for every coulomb of charge it has, or how many joules of energy there will be per coulomb.
title: Electric potential

text: Lorentz's law is a law discovered by the Dutch physicist Hendrik Antoon Lorentz. Lorentz's law defines force that acts on moving charged particles in an electromagnetic field.
title: Lorentz force

text: Electromagnetic induction is where a voltage or current is produced in a conductor by a changing magnetic flux. It may happen when a magnet is moved in a solenoid, or when a solenoid is constantly moved in a stationary magnetic field, thus changing the magnetic flux.
title: Electromagnetic induction

text: Faraday's law of induction is a law of physics proposed by English physicist Michael Faraday in 1831. It is one of the basic laws of electromagnetism.
title: Faraday's law of induction

text: Maxwell's equations describe how electric charges and electric currents create electric and magnetic fields. They describe how an electric field can generate a magnetic field.
title: Maxwell's equations

text: Ampère's circuital law, discovered by André-Marie Ampère in 1826, relates the magnetic field around a closed loop to the electric current passing through the loop. It is now one of Maxwell's equations, which form the basis of classical electromagnetism.
title: Ampère's circuital law

text: Electromagnets are temporary and artificial magnets. They are magnets that are only magnetic when there is a coil of wire with electricity running through it.
title: Electromagnet

text: The electromagnetic spectrum is the range of all possible electromagnetic radiation. Electromagnetic radiation can be divided into octaves — as sound waves are — adding up to eighty-one octaves.
title: Electromagnetic spectrum

text: Capacitance is the ability of a body to store electric charge. A common device to do such task is a capacitor.
title: Capacitance

text: Radio waves make up part of the electromagnetic spectrum. These waves are pieces of energy with differing wavelengths, somewhat similar to visible light waves, X-rays or gamma rays, except they are much longer.
title: Radio wave

text: A microwave is a high-frequency radio wave. They are broadly defined as having a wavelength between 1 millimeter and 1 meter, or narrowly between 3 mm and 300 mm.
title: Microwave

text: The visible spectrum (or sometimes called the optical spectrum) is the part of the electromagnetic spectrum that is visible to the human eye. Electromagnetic radiation in this range of wavelengths is called visible light or simply light.
title: Visible spectrum

text: An eddy current can be made when you have a solenoid (coil of wire), in which there is a soft iron core. When you connect the solenoid to an AC power source, metal objects held above the cross sectional area of the solenoid are repelled due to Lenz's Law.
title: Eddy current

text: The photoelectric effect is a phenomenon in physics. The effect is based on the idea that electromagnetic radiation is made of a series of particles called photons.
title: Photoelectric effect

text: X-radiation is a kind of electromagnetic radiation. X-rays are waves of X-radiation.
title: X-ray

text: A gamma ray, also known as gamma radiation (symbol γ), is a type of electromagnetic radiation. Gamma rays carry more energy and have a shorter wavelength than any other kind of electromagnetic wave in the electromagnetic spectrum.
title: Gamma ray

text: A Bose–Einstein condensate (BEC) is a very special and unusual state of matter. It happens when a group of tiny particles called bosons are cooled down to temperatures almost as cold as possible, close to absolute zero, which is -273.15 degrees Celsius.
title: Bose–Einstein condensate

text: Condensed matter physics is a branch of physics which talks about matter that has its molecules packed together very closely. This usually means it deals with solids (solid matter).
title: Condensed matter physics

text: The atoms of a chemical element can exist in different types that have very similar behavior, but weigh different amounts. These are called isotopes of the element.
title: Isotope

text: An amorphous solid does not have a definite geometric or crystalline shape. It is a solid in which there is no long-term order in the positions of the atoms.
title: Amorphous solid

text: In physics, Compton scattering, or the Compton effect, is the name used for what happens to the energy (or frequency or wavelength) of an X-ray or gamma ray photon when it interacts with matter; the wavelength increases (or energy/frequency decreases) as it scatters off electrons.
title: Compton scattering

text: Quantum tunnelling is a part of the theoretical branch of physics known as quantum mechanics. It states that electrons can behave like both particles and waves, and can cancel the effects of an energy barrier if the energy barrier is thin enough, due to quantum mechanics being dependent on probability.
title: Quantum tunnelling

text: There are four fundamental forces, sometimes called fundamental interactions. The forces are called fundamental because there is no simpler way for physicists to understand what the forces do or how they do it (their action).
title: Fundamental force

text: In physics, an elementary particle or fundamental particle is a particle that is not made of other particles.
title: Elementary particle

text: The Dirac equation is an equation from quantum mechanics. Paul Dirac formulated the equation in 1928.
title: Dirac equation

text: A graviton is a hypothetical particle that 'transfers' gravitation's force (particles like this are known as gauge bosons) from its field. Gravitons have never been observed, directly or indirectly, however, there have been several theories that use gravitons to explain certain phenomena.
title: Graviton

text: Quantum chromodynamics (QCD) is the theory of the strong interaction between quarks and gluons. These are the fundamental particles that make up hadrons such as the proton, neutron and pion.
title: Quantum chromodynamics

text: Quantum electrodynamics (also called QED for short) is the quantum theory of electricity and magnetism. QED describes how electric and magnetic forces work on the scale of things smaller than atoms.
title: Quantum electrodynamics

text: Particle physics is a branch of physics that studies tiny pieces of elements, known as particles. These particles are extremely small pieces that build up the world around us.
title: Particle physics

text: A particle is a tiny bit of matter that makes up everything in the universe. In particle physics, an elementary particle is a particle which cannot be split up into smaller pieces.
title: Particle

text: A cloud chamber is a sealed box with a supersaturated vapour of water or alcohol. When a charged particle (e.g. an alpha or beta particle) goes through it, the vapour is ionized.
title: Cloud chamber

text: The Standard Model (SM) of physics is a theory of the elementary particles, which are either fermions or bosons. It also explains three of the four basic forces of nature.
title: Standard Model

text: String theory tries to use math to explain the four known fundamental forces—gravitation, electromagnetism, strong nuclear force, weak nuclear force—together in one theory. This tries to solve the problems of having both classical physics and quantum physics.
title: String theory

text: Spontaneous symmetry breaking is a way symmetry breaks in a physical system. The underlying laws do not change, but the system as a whole changes.
title: Spontaneous symmetry breaking

text: Super symmetry is a scientific theory that says that when elementary particles (such as photons, electrons, and quarks) were formed at the beginning of the universe, matching kinds of theoretical "super particles" were also created.
title: Supersymmetry

text: A particle accelerator, also called an atom smasher, is a machine that accelerates (speeds up) particles and makes them travel at very high speeds. Accelerators work by pushing particles like electrons, protons, or atomic nuclei (the centers of atoms) with electric fields and by steering them with magnetic fields.
title: Particle accelerator

text: The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is the world's biggest and most powerful particle accelerator. It was built by the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN).
title: Large Hadron Collider

text: A synchrotron is a type of particle accelerator where particles travel around many times in a circle. It uses a magnetic field to turn the particles in the circle and an electric field to speed up the particles.
title: Synchrotron

text: The Tevatron was a giant Particle accelerator in Illinois that was used by scientists to make protons go very fast, almost the speed of light in some cases. Scientists looked at what happens when the protons hit antiprotons to see if they are right about their ideas as to what protons are made of.
title: Tevatron

text: The Geiger–Marsden experiment (also called the Gold foil experiment or the Rutherford experiment) was a scientific experiment done by Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden in 1909.
title: Geiger–Marsden experiment

text: A subatomic particle is a particle smaller than an atom. Like atoms and molecules, a subatomic particle is far too small to be seen with the eye.
title: Subatomic particle

text: A fermion is a category of elementary particles. They are very small and very light.
title: Fermion

text: Leptons are elementary particles with spin 1/2 (a fermion) that are not affected by strong nuclear force. They are a family of particles that are different from the other known family of fermions, the quarks.
title: Lepton

text: An electron is a very small piece of matter made up of negative charge. Its symbol is e− or β-, and it was discovered by J. J. Thomson in 1897.
title: Electron

text: The muon is an elementary particle. It has a negative electric charge and half spin.
title: Muon

text: Tau (τ) leptons (aka tauons, tau particle) are one of the very small elementary particles. This means that they are believed to be so small that they can not be divided any more.
title: Tau (particle)

text: Neutrinos are a type of elementary particle that exist all across the universe. The word neutrino means a small neutral particle.
title: Neutrino

text: A quark is an elementary particle which makes up hadrons, the most stable of which are protons and neutrons. Atoms are made of protons, neutrons and electrons.
title: Quark

text: Up quarks are subatomic particles that help make up many larger particles, such as protons. Up quarks have a charge of +2/3, and are the lightest of the six types of quarks.
title: Up quark

text: Down quarks (sometimes written as a "d") are subatomic particles that help make up many larger particles, like protons and neutrons. Down quarks have a charge of -1/3.
title: Down quark

text: Charm quarks or c quarks are the third most massive of the six quarks. Like all quarks, they are thought to be so small that they can not be divided. (They are called elementary particles for this reason).
title: Charm quark

text: Strange quarks are the third lightest quarks, which are subatomic particles that are so small, they are believed to be the fundamental particles, and not further divisible. Like down quarks, strange quarks have a charge of -1/3.
title: Strange quark

text: Top quarks or truth quarks are the heaviest known elementary particles (particles that are so small that they can not be divided). All quarks are elementary particles, and since they are fermions (which means that no two of them can exist in the same place at the same time), they have a spin of 1/2.
title: Top quark

text: Bottom quarks or beauty quarks are the second most massive of the elementary particles (particles that are so small that they can not be divided any more). All quarks are elementary particles.
title: Bottom quark

text: A hadron, in particle physics, is any subatomic (smaller than the atom) particle or antiparticle which is made of quarks.
title: Hadron

text: Baryons are composite subatomic particles made of an odd number of valence quarks (at least three quarks). The most familiar baryons are the protons and neutrons which make up most of the visible matter in the universe.
title: Baryon

text: Neutrons, with protons and electrons, make up an atom. Neutrons and protons are found in the nucleus of an atom.
title: Neutron

text: A proton is part of an atom. They are found in the nucleus of an atom along with neutrons.
title: Proton

text: Mesons are incredibly small subatomic particles that are made of one quark and one antiquark. Antiquarks are the antimatter counterpart of a regular quark.
title: Meson

text: A boson is a particle which carries a force. It has a whole number spin (spin is a property of subatomic particles).
title: Boson

text: Gauge bosons are carrier particles for three of the four fundamental forces. In the Standard Model of particle physics, there are four kinds of gauge bosons.
title: Gauge boson

text: Gluons are what hold quarks together to make bigger particles called hadrons. Gluons carry the strong force between other quarks, so it is considered a force carrying particle.
title: Gluon

text: Photons (from Greek φως, meaning light), in many atomic models in physics, are particles which transmit light. In other words, light is carried over space by photons.
title: Photon

text: The Higgs boson (or Higgs particle) is an elementary particle in the Standard Model of physics. In the 1960s Peter Higgs was the first person to suggest that this particle might exist.
title: Higgs boson

text: W and Z bosons are a group of elementary particles. They are bosons, meaning they have a spin of 0 or 1.
title: W and Z bosons

text: Ionizing radiation is a process in physics where something sends out particles or waves that can ionize an atom or molecule through atomic interactions.
title: Ionizing radiation

text: An alpha particle is a subatomic particle that is made up of two protons and two neutrons. It is a helium nucleus: that is a helium atom without electrons.
title: Alpha particle

text: Beta particles are electrons or positrons emitted by some radioactive nuclei such as potassium-40 or carbon-14 (which becomes nitrogen-14). The beta particles emitted are a form of ionizing radiation sometimes called beta rays.
title: Beta particle

text: In nuclear physics, beta decay is a type of radioactive decay where a beta particle (an electron or a positron) is made and sent away, or emitted. When it is an electron, it is called beta minus, and changes a neutron into a proton.
title: Beta decay

text: Antimatter is a special kind of matter made up of tiny particles that are like the normal particles we know but with opposite electric charges. For every particle in regular matter, there is a matching antiparticle.
title: Antimatter

text: There is an antiparticle corresponding to most kinds of particle. It has the same mass and opposite electric charge.
title: Antiparticle

text: A positron (also called an antielectron) is the antimatter version of an electron. It has the same mass and spin as an electron.
title: Positron

text: Antihydrogen is an atom made of antimatter. Just as normal matter, antihydrogen can bond and form molecules with other antimatter – it would annihilate any normal matter that it touches.
title: Antihydrogen

text: Antiprotons are tiny particles of antimatter. They have a negative charge, and are the nucleus of an Antihydrogen atom.
title: Antiproton

text: Antineutron is the antiparticle of a neutron. Anti-neutrons were found in 1956 at the University of California, Berkeley.
title: Antineutron

text: The becquerel (symbol: Bq), equivalent to s-1, is the SI derived unit of radioactivity (A). 1 Bq is defined as the number of times a nucleus decays every second.
title: Becquerel

text: The gray (symbol Gy) is the SI Unit used to show how much ionizing radiation someone has been exposed to. It measures how much energy has been deposited, or left behind, in someone.
title: Gray (unit)

text: The sievert (symbol: Sv) is the SI unit to measure the equivalent dose and committed dose of an ionizing radiation, which represent the risk of bodily radiation dosage and harm as a result of it. It looks at how an organism reacts to a given dose.
title: Sievert

text: Nuclear physics is the part of physics that studies the nucleus of the atom. Everything on the earth is made up of atoms; they are the smallest part of a chemical element that still has the properties of that specific element.
title: Nuclear physics

text: Nuclear fusion is the process of making a single heavy nucleus (part of an atom) from two lighter nuclei. This process is called a nuclear reaction.
title: Nuclear fusion

text: Nuclear fusion is when two atoms merge to form a new one. This reaction with plasma generates energy.
title: Fusion power

text: The nucleus is the center of an atom. It is made up of nucleons called protons and neutrons and is surrounded by the electron cloud.
title: Atomic nucleus

text: Atomic physics is the field of physics studying atoms as an isolated system of electrons and an atomic nucleus. It is primarily concerned with the arrangement of electrons within the atom and the processes by which it changes.
title: Atomic physics

text: Atomic orbitals are the places surrounding the nucleus of an atom where the electrons are most likely to be at any given time. It is a mathematical function that describes the wave-like behavior of either one electron or a pair of electrons in an atom.
title: Atomic orbital

text: In chemistry and physics, the atomic theory explains how our understanding of the atom has changed over time. Atoms were once thought to be the smallest pieces of matter.
title: Atomic theory

text: In quantum mechanics, a branch of physics, the Bohr model is the model of the atom proposed by Niels Bohr. Bohr's model is useful only when discussing the behavior of a hydrogen atom.
title: Bohr model

text: An electron configuration is the arrangement of electrons within an atom. The electron configuration describes where the electrons are inside orbitals.
title: Electron configuration

text: An electron shell, or main energy level, is the part of an atom where electrons are found orbiting the atom's nucleus.
title: Electron shell

text: When an electron is transferred from its ground state to other upper energy levels (called excited state of an electron) by providing heat enthalpy then the atom is said to be in excited state. An atom is not stable in its excited state.
title: Excited state

text: The plum pudding model is an early 20th century model of an atom (it was later found to be wrong). It was proposed by J.J. Thomson in 1904, after the electron had been discovered by him, but before the atomic nucleus was discovered.
title: Plum pudding model

text: The Pauli exclusion principle refers to the fact that certain particles cannot be at the same place at the same time, with the same energy. Only fermions (examples are protons, neutrons and electrons) are bound by the Pauli exclusion principle, while bosons (an example is a photon - light beam) are not.
title: Pauli exclusion principle

text: Ionization energy is the energy needed to remove the most loosely attached electron from an atom. The atom is not connected to any other atoms.
title: Ionization energy

text: An ion is an electrically charged atom or molecule (group of atoms). It is "charged" so it will move near electricity.
title: Ion

text: The dalton or unified atomic mass unit (symbol: Da, amu or u) is a unit of measurement for measuring the mass of atoms, equalling ¹⁄₁₂ of the mass of the carbon-12 isotope, the most abundant form of carbon atoms in nature.
title: Dalton (unit)

text: The atomic radius of an element is the distance between the nucleus and the edge of the electron cloud.
title: Atomic radius

text: In physics, spin is the constant rotation of an object.
title: Spin (physics)

text: Ionization is when an atom or molecule gains or loses electrons, turning it into a charged particle called an ion. Normally, atoms have no charge because they have the same number of positive protons and negative electrons.
title: Ionization

text: In chemistry, a molecular orbital (or MO) explains what happens to electrons when atoms join together in a molecule. An MO is a mathematical function that describes the wave-like behaviour of an electron in a molecule.
title: Molecular orbital

text: The Krebs cycle (named after Hans Krebs) is a part of cellular respiration. Its other names are the citric acid cycle, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA cycle).
title: Krebs cycle

text: In chemistry, concentration is how much of a substance is mixed with another substance.
title: Concentration

text: Electronegativity, symbol χ, is a chemical property that says how well an atom can attract electrons towards itself.
title: Electronegativity

text: In organic chemistry, a functional group is a piece of a molecule that helps determine how it reacts with other chemicals. Having specific functional groups is what defines a family of organic chemicals.
title: Functional group

text: Fluorescence is the light given off by certain substances when it absorbs light or other electromagnetic radiation. First the substance absorbs the energy, then it emits light.
title: Fluorescence

text: Glycolysis is a metabolic process in most organisms. It is the first stage in cellular respiration.
title: Glycolysis

text: Hydroxide in chemistry is a name given to the diatomic anion OH−, made up of oxygen and hydrogen atoms. Most chemical compounds that contain hydroxides are bases.
title: Hydroxide

text: Hydrophobe is a term from chemistry for a substance that does not mix with water. Examples of such substances are different types of vegetable oils, and fats.
title: Hydrophobe

text: Monosaccharides are the simplest form of carbohydrates. They consist of one sugar and are usually colorless, water-soluble, crystalline solids.
title: Monosaccharide

text: Polymerization or polymerisation is the process in which small molecules, called monomers, join chemically to produce a very large chain-like or network molecules, called polymers. The monomer molecules may all be alike, or they may represent two, three, or more different compounds.
title: Polymerization

text: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a way to make many copies of a sequence of DNA (this is sometimes called 'amplifying' the DNA). It is done in a lab, using an enzyme called DNA polymerase.
title: Polymerase chain reaction

text: The phlogiston theory is a superseded scientific theory that was used to explain fire and combustion before modern chemistry and the discovery of oxygen. The concept was put forward in 1667 by Johann Joachim Becher, and many varieties of phlogiston theory were proposed by other 17th- and 18th-century chemists.
title: Phlogiston theory

text: A polysaccharide is a complex carbohydrate. Polysaccharides are polymers made up of many monosaccharides.
title: Polysaccharide

text: Stoichiometry is a sort of math used in chemistry that studies and measures the amount of matter in chemical reactions. It can be used to predict the amount of things that will be made in a chemical reaction.
title: Stoichiometry

text: Tritium is an isotope of hydrogen, the lightest element. Tritium has one proton and two neutrons.
title: Tritium

text: A radionuclide is a naturally or artificially produced radioactive isotope of an element. They are often referred to as radioactive isotopes or radioisotopes.
title: Radionuclide

text: A solvent is a substance that becomes a solution by dissolving a solid, liquid, or gaseous solute. A solvent is usually a liquid, but can also be a solid or gas.
title: Solvent

text: The covalent radius is the radius of an atom that is measured when that atom is in a covalent bond. It is normally measured in picometers.
title: Covalent radius

text: The oxidation state (or oxidation number) of an element is used to predict what sort of chemical compounds form. Every element has oxidation states that it likes, and will not form compounds that would put it in a bad state.
title: Oxidation state

text: The carbon cycle is the way carbon is stored and replaced on Earth. Some of the main events take hundreds of millions of years, others happen annually.
title: Carbon cycle

text: Eutrophication is what a water-based ecosystem does when too many nutrients are added to it. Eutrophication is mainly caused by two nutrients, phosphorus and nitrogen.
title: Eutrophication

text: A phase diagram is a diagram that describes a physical system (an element or a mixture). It shows under what conditions the system is in what state.
title: Phase diagram

text: The Van der Waals radius is the radius of an atom that is seen as a hard sphere. It is named after the person who realized that atoms were not points, but actual objects.
title: Van der Waals radius

text: A macromolecule is a molecule with a large number of atoms. The word is usually used only when describing polymers, molecules which are made up of smaller molecules called monomers.
title: Macromolecule

text: Parts per million is a unit which expresses a small amount of dimensionless quantities. Proportionally, parts per million represents one thousandth of a millilitre of something per litre of water, or one milligram of something per kilogram of soil.
title: Parts per million

text: A glycoprotein is a big molecule. It is composed of a protein and a carbohydrate (which is usually a sugar-like substance).
title: Glycoprotein

text: Poisson's ratio (letter v) is a measure of the contraction that happens when an object is stretched. It is named after Siméon Denis Poisson.
title: Poisson's ratio

text: In chemistry, valence electrons are the electrons in the outside or valence electron shell of an atom. They determine the valency of the atom which is important in how a chemical element reacts with other elements.
title: Valence electron

text: Adhesion is the process in which dissimilar particles stick together. In the case of similar particles, this effect is called cohesion.
title: Adhesion

text: This article is about the chemical concept of valence, or valency. Other meanings are at valence.
title: Valency

text: Cosmic dust (also known as star dust and space dust) is a type of dust. It is very small crystals sent out from stars.
title: Cosmic dust

text: A free radical, or radical, is an atom or molecule with an unpaired electron. The radical is reactive and seeks another electron to pair.
title: Free radical

text: An isomer in chemistry is a chemical compound that has the same molecular formula as another, but it has a different arrangement of atoms in space. In other words, isomers are compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formula.
title: Isomer

text: Amount of substance (also called chemical amount) is a quantity defined by standards to measure the size a group of individual elementary entities, such as atoms, molecules and electrons, along with other particles.
title: Amount of substance

text: The mole (symbol: mol) is the SI unit used to measure how many molecules or atoms there are. One mole is around 600 sextillion molecules.
title: Mole (unit)

text: Computational chemistry is a type of chemistry that uses computer science to help solve chemical problems. These programs help scientists learn about molecules and solids.
title: Computational chemistry

text: Electrochemistry is a kind of chemistry that studies chemical reactions that use or make electricity. Reactions like this happen at electrodes which are made from something that conducts electricity, and put in an electrolyte.
title: Electrochemistry

text: Electrolysis is a scientific way of 'splitting' substances. It means 'electric-splitting' and involves the separation of substances through an electric current.
title: Electrolysis

text: Environmental chemistry is the scientific study of the chemical and biochemical phenomena that occur in natural places. It is the study of the sources, reactions, transport, effects, and fates of chemical species in the air, soil, and water environments; and the effect of human activity on these.
title: Environmental chemistry

text: Forensic science (or forensics) is when science works to answer questions a lawyer might ask.
title: Forensic science

text: Pharmaceutical chemistry or medicinal chemistry is a discipline of chemistry and pharmacology. Medicinal chemistry is interested in finding out about the chemical properties drugs have, and about the synthesis and production of drugs.
title: Pharmaceutical chemistry

text: Nuclear chemistry is the part of chemistry dealing with radioactivity and other parts of atoms.
title: Nuclear chemistry

text: Organometallic chemistry is the study of chemical compounds containing bonds between carbon and a metal. It combines aspects of inorganic chemistry (the study of non-carbon bonds) and organic chemistry (the study of carbon bonds).
title: Organometallic chemistry

text: Photochemistry is the study of chemical reactions with light. There are many natural examples.
title: Photochemistry

text: Polymer chemistry (also called macromolecular chemistry) is the science of chemical synthesis and chemical properties of polymers or macromolecules. According to IUPAC recommendations, macromolecules refer to the individual molecular chains and are the domain of chemistry.
title: Polymer chemistry

text: Alchemy is the very old study and philosophy of how to change basic substances (such as metals) into other substances. It also studied how substances (and how they are changed into other substances) were related to magic and astrology.
title: Alchemy

text: A chemical bond is a type of attraction force which holds together different chemical species. Atoms bonded stay together unless the needed amount of energy is transferred to the bond.
title: Chemical bond

text: An ionic bond is a chemical bond between a non-metal and a metal ion in a giant ionic crystal lattice. This occurs when charged atoms (ions) attract.
title: Ionic bond

text: A covalent bond is a chemical bond between two non-metal atoms. In a covalent bond, atoms share electrons with each other.
title: Covalent bond

text: A metallic bond is the sharing of many detached electrons between many positive ions, where the electrons act as a "glue" giving the substance a definite structure. It is unlike covalent or ionic bonding.
title: Metallic bond

text: A hydrogen bond is a type of chemical bond that weakly attaches a molecule to another molecule. It is based on the attraction between opposite electric charges.
title: Hydrogen bond

text: In physics, chemistry, and biology, intermolecular forces are forces that act between stable molecules or between functional groups of macromolecules.
title: Intermolecular force

text: A chemical reaction happens when one or more chemicals are changed into one or more other chemicals.
title: Chemical reaction

text: An acid-base reaction is a chemical reaction between an acid and a base. The products of such a reaction are a salt and water.
title: Acid–base reaction

text: Catalysis is the process of change in rate (speed) of a chemical reaction due to the help of a catalyst. Unlike other chemicals which take part in the reaction, a catalyst is not consumed by the reaction itself.
title: Catalysis

text: A chemical equation is a way to predict the way that two or more chemicals will work together. Using what chemists know about the way chemicals act, we add the letter symbols together just like a math problem.
title: Chemical equation

text: A chemical formula is a way that chemists describe a molecule. The formula says what atoms, and how many of each type, are in the molecule.
title: Chemical formula

text: Chemical kinetics, also called reaction kinetics, is the branch of physical chemistry connected with study of how fast chemical reactions go. This includes studying how different conditions such as temperature, pressure or solvent used, affect the speed of a reaction.
title: Chemical kinetics

text: A reaction mechanism is writing step by step how a chemical reaction works. Usually, only the overall change can be seen in a reaction.
title: Reaction mechanism

text: Redox (shorthand for reduction/oxidation) describes all chemical reactions in which atoms have an increase or decrease in oxidation number (oxidation state).
title: Redox

text: In chemistry, a substitution reaction happens when an atom or a group of atoms is replaced by a different one. Substitution reactions can be of many different types.
title: Substitution reaction

text: A chemical substance is any material with a known chemical composition. For example, water has the same properties and the same ratio of hydrogen to oxygen whether it came from a river or was made in a laboratory.
title: Chemical substance

text: In chemistry, chemical synthesis means using chemical reactions to get a product, or several products. This happens by physical and chemical manipulations.
title: Chemical synthesis

text: A chemist is a scientist who studies chemistry. In England, it can also mean a pharmacist (person who dispenses prescription medication).
title: Chemist

text: The law of conservation of mass states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. Thus, the amount of matter cannot change.
title: Conservation of mass

text: Atomism is an idea in Metaphysics. It says that everything that can be touched is made of smaller things that are made of smaller things that are made of even smaller things but that eventually you get to something so small that nothing smaller can exist called an Atom.
title: Atomism

text: The Greek classical elements are fire, air, water, and earth. In Greek philosophy, science and medicine, these make up a whole.
title: Classical element

text: Hydrolysis is a chemical reaction or process where a chemical compound reacts with water. This is the type of reaction that is used to break down polymers into many smaller units.
title: Hydrolysis

text: Solubility is the ability of a substance (the solute), to mix into a liquid (the solvent).
title: Solubility

text: Adsorption is the sticking of atoms or molecules to a surface (called "adsorbent"). The particles which get stuck on can be from a gas, liquid or a dissolved solid.
title: Adsorption

text: pH is a scale of acidity from 0 to 14. It tells how acidic or alkaline a substance is.
title: PH

text: An electrolyte is a chemical that conducts electrical current. It is used in batteries to make the ions flow, producing current.
title: Electrolyte

text: Heavy water (deuterium oxide, 2H2O, D2O) is a form of water based on deuterium.
title: Heavy water

text: Crystallization is the way that atoms link up in a regular structure. The structure is held together by chemical bonds or connected groups.
title: Crystallization

text: A crystal is a solid whose atoms (or molecules) are arranged in a repeating pattern.
title: Crystal

text: A phase change is a change in the states of matter. For example, a solid may become a liquid.
title: Phase change

text: Hardness is a measure of how much a material resists changes in shape. Hard things resist pressure.
title: Hardness

text: Allotropy (or allotropism) is when a chemical element can exist in two or more different forms in the same physical state or phase. These different forms are called allotropes.
title: Allotropy

text: Crystallography is the science of studying how atoms are arranged in solid materials that form crystals. Crystals are special because their atoms are packed in a repeating pattern.
title: Crystallography

text: In crystallography, the crystal structure is how the atoms (or ions or molecules) are arranged in a crystalline material. Crystals occur naturally from the way the chemical bonds of the atoms connect.
title: Crystal structure

text: Mohs' scale of mineral hardness is named after Friedrich Mohs, a mineralogist. Mohs scale is ordered by hardness, determined by which minerals can scratch other minerals.
title: Mohs scale of mineral hardness

text: Chromatography is a lab technique that helps scientists separate, identify, and purify the different parts of a mixture. It works by using differences in the speed at which the mixed substances move through special media, or chemical substances.
title: Chromatography

text: Mass spectrometry (MS) is a science tool used to find out what things are made of by measuring mass and charge of tiny particles called ions. This helps scientists identify, measure, and even understand the structure of different chemical substances.
title: Mass spectrometry

text: Spectroscopy is the study of light as a function of length of the wave that has been emitted, reflected or shone through a solid, liquid, or gas.
title: Spectroscopy

text: Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) is a common sulfate mineral made of calcium sulfate. Gypsum has been used as a building material for a long time, possibly since the neolithic.
title: Gypsum

text: In chemistry, a silicate is an anion (negatively charged ion) made of silicon and oxygen. Silicate anions, with a negative net electrical charge, must have that charge balanced by other cations to make an electrically neutral compound.
title: Silicate

text: Graphite, like diamond, is an allotrope of carbon. They are very similar to each other but the different structures of the molecule affect the chemical and physical properties.
title: Graphite

text: Quartz is a tectosilicate mineral that is the second most common mineral in Earth's continental crust. Its crystal structure is a framework of SiO4 silicon–oxygen tetrahedra.
title: Quartz

text: An oxide is a chemical compound containing at least one oxygen atom and at least one atom of one other element. Most of the Earth's crust consists of oxides (mainly silica).
title: Oxide

text: Ozone, or trioxygen, is a chemical with the symbol O3. This means one molecule of ozone is made of three oxygen atoms.
title: Ozone

text: A carbonate is a chemical compound that has the carbonate ion, CO2−3. This ion is made of carbon and oxygen.
title: Carbonate

text: Chloride is an ion of chlorine. It occurs when chlorine gets reduced, gaining an electrons and becoming an ion.
title: Chloride

text: Organosilicon chemistry is the scientific study of organosilicon compounds, a type of chemical compound where silicon atoms are connected to carbon atoms. Silicon has similar chemistry to carbon because they are both in the same group, and many organosilicon compounds are similar to those made with just carbon.
title: Organosilicon chemistry

text: Organosulfur chemistry is the study of how organosulfur compounds are made and what they do. These compounds are made of sulfur and carbon.
title: Organosulfur chemistry

text: A thiol is a molecule that has a R–SH group. Thiols are like alcohols with an oxygen atom changed with a sulfur one.
title: Thiol

text: An ester is a molecule that includes a carbon atom, double-bonded to an oxygen atom, and single-bonded to another oxygen atom that is bonded to a carbon atom. In other words, a carbonyl with an ether group on the carbon atom.
title: Ester

text: In organic chemistry, an ether is a part of a molecule called a functional group. An ether group is a structure where two carbon atoms are linked by chemical bonds to the same oxygen atom, and neither carbon has a double bond to another oxygen atom.
title: Ether

text: A hydrocarbon is a type of chemical compound. It is made of only hydrogen and carbon atoms.
title: Hydrocarbon

text: An alkyne is a molecule that has a triple bond between two carbon atoms. They have general formula CnH2n-2.
title: Alkyne

text: This page shows a list of all 118 chemical elements that have been identified.
title: List of elements

text: The atomic number (symbol: Z) of an atom is the number of protons in the nucleus of the atom. The atomic number of an atom identifies which element it is.
title: Atomic number

text: An atomic mass (symbol: ma) is the mass of a single atom of a chemical element. It includes the masses of the 3 subatomic particles that make up an atom: protons, neutrons and electrons.
title: Atomic mass

text: A period in the periodic table is any horizontal row of elements.
title: Period (periodic table)

text: Alkali metals are the chemical elements in periodic table group 1, other than hydrogen. The term group 1 element can be used to include hydrogen.
title: Alkali metal

text: The alkaline earth metals are the second group of metals on the periodic table. They are related to the Alkali metals, but they do not react as much because they need more energy to remove their two electrons, so they do not have to be stored in petrol.
title: Alkaline earth metal

text: A lanthanide is one of a group of 15 elements that have atomic numbers 57 to 71. This is also known as the lanthanide series or lanthanoid series.
title: Lanthanide

text: The actinide series is the 15 chemical elements between actinium and lawrencium on the periodic table. They have the atomic numbers between 89 and 103.
title: Actinide

text: The transition metals are a group of metals that are found in the middle of the periodic table. The alkaline earth metals, beginning with beryllium are to the left and the boron group (triels) elements are to the right.
title: Transition metal

text: A group 3 element is a group in the periodic table of chemical elements. It is also called the scandium group after its lightest member.
title: Group 3 element

text: Group 4 is a group of elements in the periodic table. It contains the elements titanium, zirconium, hafnium and rutherfordium.
title: Group 4 element

text: Group 5 is a group of elements in the periodic table.
title: Group 5 element

text: Group 6, numbered by IUPAC style, is a group of elements in the periodic table. Its members are chromium (Cr), molybdenum (Mo), tungsten (W), and seaborgium (Sg).
title: Group 6 element

text: A noble metal is a metal that has a low chemical reactivity. Normally, this means it is resistant to corrosion and oxidation in air, but more specific definitions exist in different fields of chemistry, with different levels of "nobility" for different elements depending on the definition.
title: Noble metal

text: A Group 11 element is one in the series of elements in group 11 (IUPAC style) in the periodic table, consisting of transition metals which are the traditional coinage metals of copper (Cu), silver (Ag), and gold (Au).
title: Group 11 element

text: A group 12 element is a group in the periodic table of chemical elements. It includes zinc, cadmium, mercury, and copernicium.
title: Group 12 element

text: A metalloid is a type of chemical element. Metalloids are elements that have the properties of both metal and non-metal elements.
title: Metalloid

text: Nonmetals or non-metals are chemical elements which do not have the properties of a metal.
title: Nonmetal

text: The boron group, also known as Group III and Group 13, is a group of elements on the periodic table. Most of its members are poor metals, except for boron.
title: Boron group

text: The Group 14 elements, also known as the carbon group and the Group IV elements, is a group of elements on the periodic table. Each element has 4 valence electrons.
title: Group 14 element

text: The Group 15 elements, also called the pnictogens, Group V elements, or Group VB elements, are a group on the periodic table. They have many different properties.
title: Pnictogen

text: Group 16 is the third last group in the periodic table. This group is called the oxygen family or the chalcogens.
title: Group 16 element

text: The halogens are chemical elements under the second-to-right column in the periodic table, also known as Group 17. The elements in the group are fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, astatine, and tennessine.
title: Halogen

text: The noble gases are a group of elements that are all gases. These elements are all in group 18 of the periodic table.
title: Noble gas

text: A period 1 element is an element in the first period (row) of the periodic table. The periodic table is arranged in rows to show repeating properties of the elements.
title: Period 1 element

text: A period 2 element is an element in the second period (row) of the periodic table. Period 2 has eight elements: lithium, beryllium, boron, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, fluorine and neon.
title: Period 2 element

text: A period 3 element is an element found on the third period (row) of the periodic table. The row has eight elements sodium, magnesium, aluminium, silicon, phosphorus, sulfur, chlorine, and argon.
title: Period 3 element

text: Helium is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol He, atomic number 2, and atomic weight of about 4.002602.
title: Helium

text: Lithium (from Greek lithos 'stone') is a soft, silver-white metal with symbol Li. It is the third chemical element in the periodic table.
title: Lithium

text: Beryllium is in group 2 of the periodic table, so it is an alkaline earth metal. It is grayish (slightly gray) in color.
title: Beryllium

text: Boron is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol B. It has the atomic number 5.
title: Boron

text: Fluorine (symbol F) is a chemical element that is very poisonous. Its atomic number (which is the number of protons in it) is 9, and its atomic mass is 19.
title: Fluorine

text: Neon is a chemical element on the periodic table. It is part of the noble gas group and it has an atomic number of 10.
title: Neon

text: Sodium is a chemical element with an atomic number of 11. Its symbol is Na (from its Latin name natrium).
title: Sodium

text: Magnesium ( /mæɡˈniːziəm/ mag-NEE-zee-əm) is a chemical element. It has the symbol Mg, atomic number 12 and common oxidation state +2.
title: Magnesium

text: Silicon is a chemical element. Its atomic number is 14 on the periodic table.
title: Silicon

text: Phosphorus has the chemical symbol P, and its atomic number is 15. Its mass number is 30.97.
title: Phosphorus

text: Sulfur (American English) or sulphur (British English) is a chemical element. The symbol for sulfur is S, and its atomic number is 16.
title: Sulfur

text: Chlorine (chemical symbol Cl) is a chemical element. Its atomic number (which is the number of protons in it) is 17, and its atomic mass is 35.45.
title: Chlorine

text: Argon is a chemical element. Its symbol is argon is Ar and its atomic number is 18.
title: Argon

text: Potassium is a chemical element in the periodic table. It has the symbol K. This symbol is taken from the Latin word kalium.
title: Potassium

text: Calcium is a chemical element. Its symbol on the periodic table (a list of all the elements) is Ca. and its atomic number is 20.
title: Calcium

text: Scandium is chemical element. Its symbol is Sc.
title: Scandium

text: Titanium is a very strong metal that is used in special applications. The most common isotope has 26 neutrons.
title: Titanium

text: Vanadium is chemical element 23 on the periodic table. Its symbol is V. It is a metal and is part of the group known as the transition metals.
title: Vanadium

text: Chromium is a chemical element. Its symbol on the periodic table (a list of all the elements) is Cr.
title: Chromium

text: Manganese is chemical element 25 on the periodic table. Its symbol is Mn. (Some people get it confused with magnesium, the symbol is Mg).
title: Manganese

text: Cobalt (chemical symbol Co) is a chemical element. It has an atomic number of 27 and an atomic mass of about 59.
title: Cobalt

text: Nickel (chemical symbol Ni) is an element. It has an atomic number of 28 and an atomic mass of about 58.69amu.
title: Nickel

text: Zinc, sometimes called spelter, is a chemical element. It is in the group of metals called the transition metals.
title: Zinc

text: Gallium (chemical symbol: Ga) is element 31 on the periodic table. It is a soft, gray metal that is rare on Earth.
title: Gallium

text: Germanium is a chemical element. Its chemical symbol is Ge.
title: Germanium

text: Arsenic is chemical element 33 on the periodic table. Its symbol is As.
title: Arsenic

text: Selenium is a chemical element. Its chemical symbol is Se and its atomic number is 34.
title: Selenium

text: Bromine (Br) is a chemical element. Its atomic number (which is the number of protons in it) is 35, and its atomic weight is 80.
title: Bromine

text: Krypton is a stable noble gas. It has an atomic number of 36.
title: Krypton

text: Rubidium is chemical element 37 on the periodic table. Its symbol is Rb.
title: Rubidium

text: Strontium is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol Sr. It has the atomic number 38.
title: Strontium

text: Yttrium is a chemical elemental metal with an atomic number of 39, a chemical symbol of Y, and an atomic weight of 88.905(abridged). It is classified as a transition metal.
title: Yttrium

text: Zirconium is a chemical elemental metal. It is a greyish-white in color.
title: Zirconium

text: Niobium is a chemical element. It is sometimes named columbium.
title: Niobium

text: Molybdenum is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol Mo.
title: Molybdenum

text: Technetium is a radioactive chemical element that has the chemical symbol Tc and has the atomic number 43. It is the lightest synthetic element.
title: Technetium

text: Ruthenium is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol Ru.
title: Ruthenium

text: Rhodium is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol Rh.
title: Rhodium

text: Palladium is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol Pd.
title: Palladium

text: Cadmium is a metal. It is element 48 on the periodic table.
title: Cadmium

text: Indium is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol In.
title: Indium

text: Antimony is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol Sb.
title: Antimony

text: Tellurium is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol Te and the atomic number 52.
title: Tellurium

text: Iodine is a chemical element. Its atomic number (which is the number of protons in it) is 53, and its atomic mass (the number of protons plus neutrons) is 127.
title: Iodine

text: Xenon is a non-metal chemical element. It has the chemical symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
title: Xenon

text: Caesium (or cesium) is the chemical element with the atomic number 55 on the periodic table. Its symbol is Cs.
title: Caesium

text: Barium is chemical element 56 on the periodic table. Its symbol is Ba.
title: Barium

text: Lanthanum is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol La.
title: Lanthanum

text: Cerium is a chemical element with an atomic number of 58. This means that the nucleus of cerium has 58 protons in it.
title: Cerium

text: Praseodymium is a chemical element that has the symbol Pr on the periodic table. It has the atomic number 59 which means it has 59 protons in an atom.
title: Praseodymium

text: Neodymium is a chemical element that has the symbol Nd on the periodic table. It has the atomic number 60 which means it has 60 protons in an atom.
title: Neodymium

text: Promethium is a synthetic radioactive chemical element that has the symbol Pm on the periodic table. It has the atomic number 61 which means it has 61 protons in its atom.
title: Promethium

text: Samarium is a chemical element that has the symbol Sm on the periodic table. It has the atomic number 62 which means it has 62 protons in an atom.
title: Samarium

text: Europium is a chemical element. It has the symbol Eu on the periodic table.
title: Europium

text: Gadolinium is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol Gd.
title: Gadolinium

text: Terbium is a chemical element that has the symbol Tb on the periodic table. It has the atomic number 65 which means it has 65 protons in an atom.
title: Terbium

text: Dysprosium (pronounced /dɪsˈproʊziəm/) is a chemical element with the symbol Dy and atomic number 66. It has a very high melting temperature of 1,407°C. It can also absorb neutrons.
title: Dysprosium

text: Holmium (pronounced /ˈhoʊlmiəm/) is a chemical element with the symbol Ho and atomic number 67. Part of the lanthanide series, holmium is a relatively soft and malleable silvery-white metallic element, which is stable in dry air at room temperature.
title: Holmium

text: Erbium (pronounced /ˈɝbiəm/) is an element on the periodic table. Its symbol is Er.
title: Erbium

text: Thulium (pronounced /ˈθjuːliəm/) is a chemical element that has the symbol Tm and atomic number 69. It is a lanthanide element.
title: Thulium

text: Ytterbium is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol Yb.
title: Ytterbium

text: Lutetium is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol Lu.
title: Lutetium

text: Hafnium is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol Hf.
title: Hafnium

text: Tantalum is a chemical element. Tantalum was named tantalium.
title: Tantalum

text: Tungsten (sometimes named wolfram) is a chemical element on the periodic table. It has the chemical symbol W and it has the atomic number 74.
title: Tungsten

text: Rhenium is a chemical element. It has the chemical symbol Re.
title: Rhenium

text: Osmium is a chemical element. It is element number 76 on the periodic table.
title: Osmium

text: Iridium is the 77th element on the periodic table. Its symbol is Ir and its atomic number is 77.
title: Iridium

text: Platinum is a chemical element. It has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.
title: Platinum

text: Mercury, also known as quicksilver or hydrargyrum (pronounced hai-DRAR-jər-əm), is a chemical element. Its symbol on the periodic table is Hg, and its atomic number is 80.
title: Mercury (element)

text: Thallium is at chemical element, it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81. Its standard atomic weight is 204.4.
title: Thallium

text: Lead (pronunciation: /'lɛd/) is a chemical element. Its chemical symbol is Pb, which comes from plumbum, the Latin word for lead.
title: Lead

text: Bismuth is a chemical element. It is element 83 on the periodic table and its symbol is Bi.
title: Bismuth

text: Polonium is a rare radioactive metalloid. It is chemical element 84 on the periodic table and its symbol is Po.
title: Polonium

text: Astatine is a radioactive, chemical element. Its atomic number is 85, and its atomic weight is 210.
title: Astatine

text: Radon is a chemical element in the periodic table. It is element 86 on the periodic table and its symbol is Rn.
title: Radon

text: Francium is a chemical element with the chemical symbol Fr and an atomic number of 87. It is a metal.
title: Francium

text: Radium is a chemical element. The symbol for radium is Ra, and its atomic number is 88.
title: Radium

text: Actinium is chemical element 89 on the periodic table. Its symbol is Ac.
title: Actinium

text: Thorium is a chemical element in actinide group. It is a weakly radioactive metal.
title: Thorium

text: Protactinium is a very radioactive chemical element with the symbol Pa and atomic number 91. The density of this element is 231.04.
title: Protactinium

text: Uranium is a chemical element (a metal) on the periodic table. It has an atomic number of 92, which means that a uranium atom has 92 protons in its center, the nucleus.
title: Uranium

text: Neptunium is a chemical element that has the symbol Np on the periodic table. It has the atomic number 93 which means it has 93 protons and electrons in its atoms.
title: Neptunium

text: Plutonium is the chemical element with the atomic number 94 and chemical symbol Pu. It is a highly radioactive metal, and is the metal used in most nuclear weapons.
title: Plutonium

text: Americium is a radioactive chemical element with the symbol Am and the atomic number 95. In chemistry, it is placed in a group of metal elements named the actinides.
title: Americium

text: Curium is a synthetic chemical element in the periodic table that has the atomic number 96. It has the chemical symbol Cm and it is a radioactive metal.
title: Curium

text: Berkelium (IPA: /bəˈkiːliəm/) is a synthetic, radioactive, chemical element in the periodic table that has the symbol Bk and atomic number 97. It is a metallic element and part of the actinide series.
title: Berkelium

text: Californium is a chemical element. It is a radioactive metal.
title: Californium

text: Einsteinium is a chemical element with the atomic number 99 it is a synthetic element, so all isotopes are radioactive.
title: Einsteinium

text: Fermium (symbol Fm) is a chemical element. It has an atomic number of 100, which makes it at position 100 at the periodic table.
title: Fermium

text: Mendelevium (pronounced /ˌmɛndəˈlɛviəm/)) is a synthetic element with the symbol Md (used to be Mv) and the atomic number 101. It is a metallic radioactive transuranic element of the actinides.
title: Mendelevium

text: Nobelium is a synthetic element with the symbol No and atomic number 102.
title: Nobelium

text: Lawrencium is a chemical element. Before being officially named, it was known as eka-lutetium and unniltrium.
title: Lawrencium

text: Rutherfordium is a very radioactive man made chemical element with the symbol Rf that has the atomic number of 104, though it has also been named eka-hafnium and unnilquadium. Rutherfordium is the first transactinide element on the periodic table.
title: Rutherfordium

text: Dubnium is a chemical element. It has the symbol Db and it has the atomic number 105.
title: Dubnium

text: Seaborgium is a man made radioactive chemical element with the symbol Sg and the atomic number of 106. The most stable isotope is 271Sg, which has a half-life of 2.4 minutes.
title: Seaborgium

text: Bohrium is a chemical element. At the periodic table of the elements it is at position 107.
title: Bohrium

text: Hassium is a very radioactive man made chemical element that has the symbol Hs and it has the atomic number 108. It is a superheavy transuranium element.
title: Hassium

text: Meitnerium is a radioactive man made chemical element in the periodic table, with the symbol Mt and an atomic number of 109. Because it is not found naturally on Earth, chemists have to create it in a lab.
title: Meitnerium

text: Darmstadtium is a chemical element. It has been named ununnilium (Uun) or eka-platinum but is now named darmstadtium.
title: Darmstadtium

text: Roentgenium (pronounced /rɛntˈgɛniəm/, /rʌntˈdʒɛniəm/) is a chemical element. It is a transition metal.
title: Roentgenium

text: Copernicium (formerly Ununbium) is a radioactive man made chemical element that has the symbol Cn and the atomic number of 112. It is also named eka-mercury and is a transuranium element.
title: Copernicium

text: Nihonium (ニホニウム) is a chemical element. It is also named eka-thallium.
title: Nihonium

text: Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element also known as eka-lead. It has the symbol Fl and has the atomic number 114.
title: Flerovium

text: Moscovium is a superheavy synthetic radioactive chemical element also known as eka-bismuth. It has the symbol Mc and the atomic number 115.
title: Moscovium

text: Livermorium is a radioactive chemical element that has the chemical symbol Lv and the atomic number 116. Its longest half-life lasts only 47 milliseconds.
title: Livermorium

text: Tennessine is a radioactive superheavy man-made chemical element. It has a symbol Ts and atomic number of 117.
title: Tennessine

text: Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element with symbol Og and atomic number 118. Oganesson has the highest atomic number and highest atomic mass of all known elements to date.
title: Oganesson

text: Acetic acid, or ethanoic acid, is a carboxylic acid. It is the main compound of vinegar, other than water.
title: Acetic acid

text: Boric acid is an acid of boron. Its salts are called borates.
title: Boric acid

text: Citric acid is a weak organic acid. It can be found in citrus fruits.
title: Citric acid

text: Hydrochloric acid is a chemical compound. It is a solution of hydrogen chloride (HCl) gas that is dissolved in water.
title: Hydrochloric acid

text: Hydrofluoric acid (HF) is a solution of hydrogen fluoride in water. Its chemical formula is HF.
title: Hydrofluoric acid

text: Lactic acid is an acid that is very common in nature. Lactic Acid is a carboxylic acid with a chemical formula of C3H6O3.
title: Lactic acid
