text: Nitric Acid (HNO3) is a very corrosive and toxic strong acid that can cause severe burns. It is also known as aqua fortis.
title: Nitric acid

text: Phosphoric acid, also known as orthophosphoric acid, is a chemical compound. It is also an acid.
title: Phosphoric acid

text: Sulfuric acid, also known as sulphuric acid, is a chemical compound and strong acid. The chemical formula is H2SO4.
title: Sulfuric acid

text: Tannic acid is a term for a mixture of related chemical compounds that are used to make leather. These chemicals are an example of tannins, a larger group of bitter-tasting chemicals that attach to proteins.
title: Tannic acid

text: In chemistry, an alkali is an aqueous (from water) solution with a pH value of more than seven.
title: Alkali

text: An inorganic compound is a chemical compound that does not have carbon–hydrogen bonds that is, it is not an organic compound. That means it is not a carbon-based compound.
title: Inorganic compound

text: Ammonia is a chemical compound made from nitrogen and hydrogen atoms. It has the chemical formula NH3.
title: Ammonia

text: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a chemical compound and is acidic. It is a gas at room temperature.
title: Carbon dioxide

text: Carbon monoxide, with the chemical formula CO, is a colorless, odorless, and tasteless gas. It consists of one carbon atom covalently bonded to one oxygen atom.
title: Carbon monoxide

text: Organic compounds are carbon-based compounds. Organic compounds contain carbon bonds in which at least one carbon atom is covalently linked to an atom of another type (usually hydrogen, oxygen or nitrogen).
title: Organic compound

text: Acetone, or propanone, is an organic compound with the chemical formula (CH3)2CO. This clear, mobile, easy-to-burn liquid is the simplest example of the ketones.
title: Acetone

text: Alkanes are chemical compounds, made of carbon and hydrogen. The simplest alkane is methane, which is made of one carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms.
title: Alkane

text: In organic chemistry, an alkene, olefin, or olefine is an unsaturated chemical compound containing at least one carbon-to-carbon double bond. The simplest alkenes, with only one double bond, no rings, and no other functional groups, are hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n.
title: Alkene

text: Amides are two related groups of chemical compounds, both derived from ammonia and amines.
title: Amide

text: An amine is a molecule which has a nitrogen atom that can behave as a base. An amine can be thought of coming from ammonia.
title: Amine

text: Benzene, also known as benzol, is an organic chemical compound with the formula C6H6. It is a colorless and flammable liquid with a sweet smell.
title: Benzene

text: Butane is an organic compound with the chemical formula C4H10. It is an alkane with four carbon atoms.
title: Butane

text: Ethane is an organic chemical compound with chemical formula C2H6.
title: Ethane

text: Caffeine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant drug. It is found in parts of plants, for example tea leaves and coffee beans.
title: Caffeine

text: A carboxylic acid is any molecule that has a COOH group. This group contains a carbonyl (C=O double bond) together with an hydroxyl group (OH) on the same carbon atom.
title: Carboxylic acid

text: A chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) is a gas used for various purposes including solvents, refrigerants, and aerosol sprays. They are organic chemicals and contain carbon, hydrogen, chlorine, and fluorine.
title: Chlorofluorocarbon

text: Cocaine (also cocain) is a strong stimulant drug that is made from coca leaves. It is often used recreationally and is illegal in most countries.
title: Cocaine

text: Ethylene or ethene is a chemical compound with two carbon atoms and four hydrogen atoms in each molecule. These molecules are put together with a double bond that makes it a hydrocarbon.
title: Ethylene

text: Formaldehyde (or methanal) is an organic chemical compound with the formula CH2O. It is the simplest aldehyde.
title: Formaldehyde

text: Fructose is a simple sugar (monosaccharide) found in many foods. It is also one of the three most important blood sugars, the other two are glucose and galactose.
title: Fructose

text: Glucose (C6H12O6) is a simple carbohydrate, or sugar. It is one of several kinds of sugars.
title: Glucose

text: Haloalkanes are alkanes that contain one or more halogens. A variety of different reactions can form these organic compounds.
title: Haloalkane

text: A ketone is an organic compound that has a carbon atom with a double bond to an oxygen atom (this is called carbonyl functional group). This carbon atom must also have single bonds to two other carbon atoms.
title: Ketone

text: Methane is an organic compound with the chemical formula CH4. It is an alkane with one carbon atom.
title: Methane

text: Methanol, or methyl alcohol, is the simplest alcohol: CH3OH. It has similarities to ethanol (the alcohol humans drink) but is very toxic.
title: Methanol

text: Nicotine is a chemical in tobacco, which is used in cigarettes, cigars, pipes tobacco, chewing tobacco, some vaping liquids and some e-cigarette products.
title: Nicotine

text: Phenol is the organic compound with formula C6H5OH. It is a white solid.
title: Phenol

text: A tablet (also known as a pill) is a drug in solid form taken by mouth. They have active substances and excipients, usually in powder form, that are pressed into a solid.
title: Tablet (pharmacy)

text: A placebo is a treatment for a disease or condition which is deliberately ineffective. The motive usually is that if a person believes that a medicine, diet, or other treatment is good for them, then it is good for them.
title: Placebo

text: Earth science is an all-covering term for the sciences related to the planet Earth. Earth science may also be called geoscience.
title: Earth science

text: Ocean surface waves are surface waves that occur in the upper layer of the ocean. They usually result from wind.
title: Ocean surface wave

text: Water vapor is water that is in the form of a vapor, or gas. It is a part of the water cycle.
title: Water vapor

text: A magnetosphere is a region around an astronomical object, such as a planet. It is the region where charged particles are affected by the object's magnetic field.
title: Magnetosphere

text: St. Elmo's fire (also called St. Elmo's light) is a weather event in which bright, glowing, ball of light is seen near pointed objects, like the mast of a ship. It is plasma made by a coronal discharge from a sharp or pointed object in a strong electric field in the air.
title: St. Elmo's fire

text: The dew point is the temperature where water vapor condenses into liquid water.
title: Dew point

text: A corona is an aura of plasma which surrounds the sun and other stars. The Sun's corona extends millions of kilometres into space and is most easily seen during a total solar eclipse.
title: Corona

text: Obsidian is a natural volcanic glass: it is a kind of igneous rock. It is produced when lava high in silica (SiO2) cools rapidly, and solidifies quickly.
title: Obsidian

text: Cartography is making maps. It is part of geography.
title: Cartography

text: A map is an image of the Earth or part of the Earth. A map is different from an aerial photograph because it includes interpretation.
title: Map

text: An avalanche is a natural disaster linked to snow. When there is too much snow on a mountain, some of the snow may fall, causing damage to things in its path.
title: Avalanche

text: Drought is a continuous period of dry weather, when an area gets less than its normal amount of rain, over months or even years. Crops and other plants need water to grow, and animals need it to live.
title: Drought

text: The structure of the Earth is divided into layers. These layers are both physically and chemically different.
title: Structure of the Earth

text: A fold is rock that is bent, instead of being broken, by its deformation. The term is used in geology when one or a stack of surfaces that were originally flat and level, such as sedimentary strata, are bent or curved as a result of high pressures and temperatures.
title: Fold (geology)

text: A formation, or rock formation, is the fundamental unit of lithostratigraphy.
title: Geological formation

text: A fossil is the remains or trace of an ancient living thing.
title: Fossil

text: Impact craters are craters formed by meteorites or comets striking the Earth or other solid body. There is a system for recording and assessing craters.
title: Impact crater

text: The lithosphere is the solid shell of the planet Earth. This means the crust, plus the part of the upper mantle which behaves elastically over long time scales.
title: Lithosphere

text: The Earth's crust is the Earth's hard outer layer. It is less than 1% of Earth's volume.
title: Earth's crust

text: A fault is a fracture, or break, in the Earth's crust (lithosphere). Some faults are active.
title: Fault (geology)

text: Basalt is a common grey to black rock. It is pushed out (extruded) by volcanos.
title: Basalt

text: Flint, or flintstone, is a kind of sedimentary rock, made of silica.
title: Flint

text: Igneous rock is one of the three main rock types, the others being sedimentary and metamorphic rock.
title: Igneous rock

text: Limestone is a sedimentary rock, made up mostly of the minerals calcite and aragonite, two forms of calcium carbonate, CaCO3.
title: Limestone

text: Magma is the melted rock under the ground. The liquid rock may have solid bits mixed in with it, and volcanic gas.
title: Magma

text: A metamorphic rock is a type of rock which has been changed by extreme heat and pressure. Its name is from 'morph' (meaning form), and 'meta' (meaning change).
title: Metamorphic rock

text: Sedimentary rocks are rocks formed from sediment. They are deposited over time, and often show layers which can be seen in cliffs.
title: Sedimentary rock

text: Mineralogy is the study of minerals. Minerals are things that make rocks.
title: Mineralogy

text: Stratigraphy is a branch of geology which studies rock formations called strata (layers). It is important in the study of sedimentary and layered vocanic rocks.
title: Stratigraphy

text: Strata are layers of rock, or sometimes soil. In nature, strata come in many layers.
title: Strata

text: A silicate mineral is a mineral that has a combination of the elements silicon and oxygen. In other words, a silicate mineral has one or more silicates.
title: Silicate mineral

text: Feldspar is the name of a group of rock-forming tectosilicate minerals that make up as much as 60% of the Earth's crust.
title: Feldspar

text: Kaolinite or Kaolin is a clay mineral. It is in a group with the chemical composition Al2Si2O5(OH)4.
title: Kaolinite

text: Talc (from the Arabic talk) is a silicate mineral, a type of clay. It is the standard for grade 1 in the Mohs scale of mineral hardness.
title: Talc

text: The mica group of minerals are aluminosilicates with various metals. They split into fine sheets, which puts them in the phyllosilicate group of silicate minerals.
title: Mica

text: Asbestos is a set of six silicate minerals which occur naturally. White asbestos makes up 95% of the asbestos found in buildings.
title: Asbestos

text: Beryl is a cyclosilicate, and is the second main ore of beryllium metal. It is sometimes found as very, very large crystals, as much as 18 m. (59 ft.) long.
title: Beryl

text: An emerald is a mineral gemstone and a variety of beryl. It is the birthstone of someone whose birthday is in the month of May.
title: Emerald

text: Sapphire is a type of the mineral corundum, an aluminium oxide (Al2O3). Sapphires are a type of corundum, the same mineral as rubies.
title: Sapphire

text: A ruby is a kind of precious stone. It is often associated with emerald, sapphire and topaz.
title: Ruby

text: Topaz is a silicate mineral. Along with silicate, it includes the chemical elements aluminium and fluorine with the chemical formula Al2SiO4(F,OH)2.
title: Topaz

text: Amber is the common name for fossil resin. It occurs in different colours, and is widely used for making jewellery and other ornaments.
title: Amber

text: Ivory is a hard yellowish-white material made from the tusks and teeth of animals such as elephants, hippopotamuses and walruses. Ivory is now very rare and expensive since there are restrictions on hunting elephants for ivory.
title: Ivory

text: Pearls are made of a kind of material made by mollusks, like oysters. Pearls are small and often white but sometimes in pale colors or even black.
title: Pearl

text: Petrology is a type of geology. It is concerned with rocks, how they form, and how they are used.
title: Petrology

text: A conglomerate is a rock consisting of individual clasts within a finer-grained matrix that have become cemented together.
title: Conglomerate (geology)

text: Gravel is small, loose, rock particles. It is any loose rock that is larger than 2 mm (0.079 in) in its smallest dimension (about 1/12 of an inch) and no more than 64 mm (2.5 in).
title: Gravel

text: Granite is a kind of igneous rock, found on Earth but nowhere else in the Solar System. It is formed from hot, molten magma.
title: Granite

text: Tuff (from Italian tufo) is a type of rock produced by the eruption of volcanoes.
title: Tuff

text: The schists are a group of metamorphic rocks which have lamellar (plate-like) minerals, such as micas, chlorite, talc, hornblende, graphite, and others. Quartz often occurs in drawn-out grains so that a form called quartz schist is produced.
title: Schist

text: Gneiss is a type of metamorphic rock. The minerals in gneiss may come from rocks which were originally either igneous or sedimentary.
title: Gneiss

text: Sand is a mixture of very small pieces of different rocks or minerals. It is the same minerals from which those pieces are broken, such as granite and feldspar.
title: Sand

text: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock. It is a rock made of compacted sand.
title: Sandstone

text: Bauxite is the main ore of aluminium. It is mostly aluminium oxide.
title: Bauxite

text: Peat, or turf, is an accumulation of partially decayed vegetation. Peat forms in wetland bogs, moors, mires, and swamps.
title: Peat

text: Quartzite is a hard metamorphic rock. It is formed when sandstone is squeezed and heated under a chain of mountains.
title: Quartzite

text: Slate is a metamorphic rock. It is formed from shale by being under pressure and moderate heat.
title: Slate

text: Oil shale is a sedimentary rock which can be squeezed to get oil out if it. The part which has oil in it is called kerogen.
title: Oil shale

text: Geodesy, sometimes called geodetics, is a scientific branch of geography which accurately measures the surface of the Earth.
title: Geodesy

text: The Earth’s magnetic field is the magnetic field which surrounds the Earth. It is sometimes called the geomagnetic field.
title: Earth's magnetic field

text: The inner core is the very center of the Earth, and the hottest part of the planet. It is a mainly a solid ball with a radius of about 1,220 km (760 mi), according to seismological studies.
title: Earth's inner core

text: The Earth's mantle has two layers. There is a rigid upper layer and a softer layer.
title: Earth's mantle

text: Seismology is the study of what is under the surface of the Earth by measuring vibrations on the Earth's surface. A person who does this is called a seismologist.
title: Seismology

text: Geologic time scale uses the principles and techniques of geology to work out the geological history of the Earth. It looks at the processes which change the Earth's surface and rocks under the surface.
title: Geologic time scale

text: Pangaea was the global supercontinent which formed in the Palaeozoic era. The process started about 450 million years ago (mya) and was complete by 210 mya.
title: Pangaea

text: An extinction event is a relatively fast drop in the number of species living on Earth. It occurs when the rate of extinction increases more than the rate of speciation.
title: List of extinction events

text: The Permian/Triassic extinction event was the largest extinction event in the Phanerozoic eon. 57% of all biological families, 83% of all genera, 96% of all marine species became extinct.
title: Permian–Triassic extinction event

text: The Cretaceous–Tertiary extinction event, now called the Cretaceous–Palaeogene extinction event, was about 65.5 million years ago. It may be called the K/T extinction event or K/Pg event for short.
title: K/T extinction event

text: An ice age is a period that for a long time the temperature of Earth's climate is very low. That leads to an expansion of the continental ice sheets, polar ice sheets and mountain glaciers.
title: Ice age

text: Pre-cambrian (or Precambrian) is a term used to describe the eons before the Cambrian. It lasted from about 4.567 billion years BC to about 542 million years BC.
title: Precambrian

text: The Phanerozoic eon is the current eon on the geologic timescale. It is the one in which abundant animal life has existed.
title: Phanerozoic

text: The Palaeozoic (or Paleozoic) era is the earliest of the three eras of the Phanerozoic. Its name means early life.
title: Palaeozoic

text: The Cambrian is the first geological period of the Palaeozoic era and the Phanerozoic eon. It lasted from 541 million years ago to 485.4 million years ago.
title: Cambrian

text: The Permian is a geological period which started about 299 million years ago (mya), and ended about 252 mya. It is the sixth and last period of the Paleozoic era and the sixth period in the Phanerozoic eon, and ended in the largest mass extinction known to science.
title: Permian

text: The Mesozoic Era was the geological era in which dinosaurs lived, as well as the first mammals. It lasted about 186 million years, starting 252.2 mya (million years ago) with the P/Tr extinction and ending 65 mya with the K/T extinction (the one that killed all dinosaurs except birds).
title: Mesozoic

text: The Triassic is the first geological period in the Mesozoic era and the seventh period of the Phanerozoic eon. It lasted 50.6 million years.
title: Triassic

text: The Jurassic is the second and middle geological period in the Mesozoic era and the eighth period in the Phanerozoic eon.
title: Jurassic

text: The Cretaceous period is the ninth and longest period in the Phanerozoic eon, lasting 80 million years from 145 to 65 million years ago (mya). It followed the Jurassic period, and is the third and last period of the Mesozoic era.
title: Cretaceous

text: The Cainozoic (Cenozoic) is the current geological era. It began 66 million years ago and continues today.
title: Cenozoic

text: The Quaternary is the current geological period. It is the most recent of the three periods of the Cainozoic era.
title: Quaternary

text: The Holocene is the present geological epoch. It started around 11,000 years ago after the last ice age.
title: Holocene

text: Geomorphology is the scientific study of landforms and the processes that shape them.
title: Geomorphology

text: Erosion is a process where natural forces like water, wind, ice, and gravity transport rocks and soil. It is a geological process, and part of the rock cycle.
title: Erosion

text: Mesa (Spanish and Portuguese for "table") is a steep-sided, flat-topped hill or mountain. They are sometimes called "table mountains." These mountains are mainly found in Spain, Africa and in some parts of the United States.
title: Mesa

text: Weathering is the breaking down of rocks, soil and their minerals through direct contact with the Earth's atmosphere, waters, or living things. It is a natural process.
title: Weathering

text: A landform is a word that describes a form of land. Each type of landform is defined by its size, shape, location, and what it is made of.
title: Landform

text: A mountain range, also called mountain chain or mountain belt, is a geographic area with many mountains. A mountain system, or system of mountain ranges, includes geological features that are in the same region as a mountain range.
title: Mountain range

text: A plateau is an area of raised land that is flat on top.
title: Plateau

text: A hill is a landform that is higher than the surrounding terrain and that is smaller than a mountain. Hill is a highland of much lower elevation than a mountain.
title: Hill

text: A valley is a type of landform. A valley is a lower part in the land that sits between two higher parts which might be hills or mountains.
title: Valley

text: In geography, a plain is a large area of land with no hills or mountains. Plains mostly are more suitable for farming than plateaus or mountains.
title: Plain

text: An alluvial fan is a fan-shaped deposit of soil and rocks. It forms where a fast-flowing river spreads out over a flat plain.
title: Alluvial fan
